# Implementation Notes

## 2026-10-20 — Moodboard reader: one swappable reading source (plan v2.6 §5.6.2, on PR4)

Plan v2.6 asks PR4 to keep the provider call behind one interface so PR10c's agent reader changes nothing in the shared core. Built on c028991e after the merge with origin/main 0a58a573. No paid API was called.

- **What.**
  - *`ReadingSource`* (`services/moodboard_reader.py`): `identity`, `priced`, `streams`, `thoughts`, `read(task, sink) -> ReadOutcome(closed, truncated, cause?)`, `sort(task, sink) -> SortOutcome(value | cause, truncated)`, plus `can_widen(task)`, `spent()`, and for a priced source `estimate()` and `spend_items()`.
  - *Tasks are shared.* `build_read_task` and `build_sort_task` make frozen `ReadTask` / `SortTask` (labels, system prompt, instructions, schema, image parts, notes per `sendNotes`). `phase1_parts` is now `gemini_parts(phase1_instructions, phase1_image_parts)`, byte for byte the old parts. Image parts are `{"image": {mimeType, data}}`; only `GeminiSource` turns them into `inline_data`.
  - *The sink is the item check.* `_TaskSink.focus` / `.item` hold what `_attempt`'s closures did (refs, duplicates, schema failures as missing, the reading and its lines); `item` returns the label it accepted. `_SortSink` carries thoughts only.
  - *`GeminiSource`* wraps `GeminiTransport`, `gemini_body` and the stream parser, and holds the level, time bounds, caps, the 20 MB inline limit and the usage. It reports `truncated` when the cause is `MAX_TOKENS`. `model_source(entry)` makes it, and refuses a non-Google provider.
  - *The look-name check* (`check_look_name`, in `enforce_sort` for every source): 1 to 60 characters, at most 4 words, letters, digits, spaces and `&-'`, at least one letter or digit, no `#n`, batch label (`names_a_label`, new in the stream module), sort label `R\d+`, `http(s)`/`www` or `@`. A refused best look sends the image to Unsorted ("its look's name was refused"), not to its second look; a refused second look gives no suggestion. Frame names already on the board aren't checked.
  - *Readings* carry `reader` (identity id without `reader:`) and `readerName`; `model` is the identity's model (the same `gemini-4-argon` as before). The run's `reader` is `source.identity`, which adds `source: "model"`.
  - *Routes.* `_reader_plan` builds a keyless source and calls `read_estimate`; `_reader_spend_hold(source, …)` calls `gate_items`, which is None for an unpriced source, so no `decide` and no hold. The read route builds the keyed source and passes it to `MoodboardRead(source=…)`.
- **Decisions not in the spec.**
  - *The lone-image raised cap is a source capability* (`can_widen` plus `task.wider`), not hidden in the source. Whether that retry goes out at all shows in the trace (a `retry` line or a `Couldn't read` line) and in the hold (`retry:N`), so the shared retry decides it. Only the source knows whether "more room" exists: Argon's cap can double up to 65,536; an agent has no cap and never reports `truncated`, so it never sees `wider`. The same capability covers the sort's retry at twice its cap.
  - *`sort` takes a sink* (the plan has `sort(task)`) so Argon's thought summaries for the sort still reach the trace. The sink's `focus` and `item` do nothing there.
  - *`reader_identity` is unchanged* (the estimate shows it, and an existing test pins it); `model_identity` adds `source`. So the estimate's `reader` has no `source` key and the run's does. One identity for both would change the estimate's output, which this step had to keep.
  - *The sort's look names are no longer cut to 60 characters* before the check (`_looks(…, cut=False)`), so a longer name is refused instead of truncated. A reading's own looks are still cut (they are reading fields), so the sort-failed fallback, which uses them, can carry a cut name that then passes the check.
  - *The dry run sets no `lastRead`*, as before (it saves nothing). The result's `runId`, `reader`, `requestedBy`, `estimate` and `spent` are what PR10's `lastRead` will take. No `billedTo` is added to Argon's estimate or result; an unpriced source's estimate says `billedTo: "agent"`.
  - *`_Cause` is now public `Cause`* (frozen); `_cause` returns None for an answer that ended cleanly, and the shared core reads "missing" from that.
- **Behaviour for Argon unchanged, checked.** A scratch script (not in the repo) ran 15 fixture reads through `MoodboardRead` with a fixed run id, clock and timestamps, including the hand-written SSE fixture, the `MAX_TOKENS` split, a lone image at a raised cap and at the model limit, the sort at the limit, wrong refs, 503 and 403, thoughts on and off, non-streaming and the 8-new-looks cap. It also ran three estimates, an unpriced one and their `spend_check`. Before and after the change: every trace identical, every request body identical, every estimate and spend item identical. The only differences are `result.reader.source` (15) and `readings.*.reader` and `readerName` (59 each). The route, CLI and MCP tests (`test_moodboard_reader_routes.py`, 23) pass unchanged.
- **Tests.** `tests/test_moodboard_reader_source.py`, 47 cases, written first: it failed at collection (`ReadingSource` missing) before the change. They cover the plan's members, the shared task Argon sends exactly, Argon's body equal to the pre-source builder, frozen tasks, a non-streaming fake giving Argon's lines and results, readings' `reader`/`readerName`, an unpriced fake with no `spent` and no thoughts, wrong and duplicate refs, a never-truncated fake whose retry is one task, a truncated fake split in halves, a lone cut-off image with and without `can_widen`, a non-retryable cause, a cut-off sort that can't widen, the name check (26 names), a refused name sending its members to Unsorted with nothing of it in a Nebula line, Argon's bad names, frame names exempt, an unpriced source's estimate with no maths and no gate (`estimate` and `spend_check` patched to fail), Argon with no list price still priced and refused, Argon's estimate and gate equal to PR4's, and `main._reader_spend_hold` skipping `decide` for an unpriced source and returning 403 for unpriced Argon. Every existing PR4 test passes unchanged (104).
- **Review (2026-10-20).** Two holes in the look-name check, each with a failing case first in `test_the_look_name_check`: a name that is only a batch label (`"B"`) passed, though §5.6.2 says no label ("Plan B" still passes); and `str.isalnum` let numerals that aren't digits in (`"½ tone"`, `"Ⅻ"`), so the check now takes `isalpha() or isdigit()`. Argon's fixture snapshot is unchanged by both. Left as is and flagged: a curly apostrophe or an en dash (`Women’s wear`, `Mid–century`) fails the plan's `&-'`, so those images go to Unsorted; normalising them to `'` and `-` first is Justin's call.
- **Look-name follow-ups (2026-10-20).** Four loose ends from the review, each with failing tests first in `tests/test_moodboard_reader_source.py` (23 failed before the change). *Typography:* `normalize_look_name` maps only ’ ‘ ʼ to `'` and – — ‐ ‑ to `-` (what autocorrect and models write for those two keys; primes, minus, bars and double quotes stay refused), `check_look_name` returns that form, and it is what `enforce_sort` stores as the look's name, so frames, `result` lines, suggestions and `newLooks` all carry the plain form. Frames are matched on the normalized name too (`_look_key`), so a person's "Mid–century" frame takes the sort's "Mid-century" and keeps the person's spelling. *Reading line:* `_TaskSink.item` names the reading's first look only through `_checked_look_ref` (the board's frame, or the checked name); a refused one leaves the line with no arrow and no `look`/`fit` keys. The reading's own `looks` stay as stored. *Labels:* `_SORT_LABEL_OR_LINK` is case-insensitive (`r3`, `r12`, a bare `b`), with word boundaries so `Grainr3` and `Color3 film` pass. *Fallback:* a reading's look names are cut at `READING_LOOK_LIMIT` (120) instead of 60, so a cut name is always over 60 and refused; the fallback draft runs the full check on the whole normalized name. *Found and fixed while testing:* two spellings of one new look (`Women's wear`, `Women's Wear`) gave each image its own spelling in its result while the frame took the first; now every look takes the first spelling given. *Where a reading's own look reaches output:* the `reading` trace line (`moodboard_reader.py` `_TaskSink.item`), which the CLI prints (`cli/commands/moodboard.py` `_print_read_line`) and MCP returns (`mcp_server.py` `_read_answer`'s `lines`); the fallback draft (`MoodboardRead._sort`), which reaches `results`, `result` lines and suggestions through `enforce_sort`. Not changed: the result's `readings` (CLI `--json`, the route) and the side panel show the reading's checked fields as data, as the plan allows; the sort prompt (`_reading_for_sort`) still sends each reading's looks to the sort request, which the plan's "never a prompt sent to another model" needs settling for PR10c's agent source. Argon's 19 fixture snapshots are byte-identical before and after.
- **Look-name review (2026-10-20).** An adversarial pass on the follow-ups found four holes, each with failing cases first in `tests/test_moodboard_reader_source.py` (21 failed before the fix). *Compatibility characters:* fullwidth `Ｒ３`, mathematical `𝐑𝟑`, `R³`, `ｗｗｗ site`, `ｈｔｔｐｓ x`, `①` and `ﬁ` passed, spelling a sort label or link the regex couldn't see; `check_look_name` now refuses a name whose NFKC form differs from it (refused rather than folded, like the other look-alikes), and `_look_char` takes `isdecimal` instead of `isdigit` (`⓵` is NFKC-stable but isn't a digit). *Composition:* a decomposed `Café` was refused (the combining accent isn't a letter) and didn't match a person's composed frame; `normalize_look_name` composes to NFC first, and `_looks` composes a reading's look before cutting it at 120, so composing can't shrink a cut name back under 60 (`test_a_cut_reading_look_cannot_shrink_under_the_limit_by_composing` guards that). *Bare labels:* `'B'`, `‘B’`, `-B-`, `B&`, `A & C` passed; a name whose every word is an A to F letter is now refused (`B&W film`, `B-movie glow`, `Plan B` pass). *Lowercase labels:* `image b`, `ref c`, `Images b and c` passed, though the prompt calls images "Image A" and the docs said labels are refused in any case; lone a to f letters are raised to capitals before `names_a_label`, so a name like "Photo a day" is refused too (its images go to Unsorted). Argon's 19 snapshots are byte-identical to the follow-ups' snapshot. Left for Justin: homoglyphs from other scripts (Cyrillic `Р3`, Greek `Ρ3`) still pass, since a confusables skeleton is more than this check needs today; `R 3` with a space passes (the `#n` rule allows `# 18`); `&` and `-` count as words, so "Black & white film grain" (4 words, 5 tokens) is refused.
- **Look-name hardening (2026-10-20).** Seven gaps closed, each with failing tests first (36 failed before the fix: `test_the_look_name_check_hardened`, the frame-collision, reading-line, sort-guard, thought and reason tests in `tests/test_moodboard_reader_source.py`, and `test_reason_cleaning_keeps_glued_letters_and_sees_look_alikes` in `tests/test_moodboard_reader_stream.py`). *Words:* the 4-word limit counts runs with a letter or digit (`_look_words`), so "Black & white film grain" passes. *Sort labels:* `R 3` is one (`\bR\s*\d+\b`, any case), "Color 3" isn't. *Article:* the old pass raised every lone a to f to a capital, so "Photo a day" was refused; `names_a_label_any_case` now matches the label in either case and counts a run only when one of its letters isn't a lowercase `a` ("Images a and b" still refused). *`B&B`* passes, decided: a batch never lists one image twice, so a repeated letter can only be the phrase; `A&E` and `A & C` stay refused, since those can't be told from a list. *Look-alikes:* `skeleton()` in the stream module maps, one character for one, every UTS #39 confusable (confusables.txt 18.0.0, 2026-08-06) whose prototype is a character the label and link checks match (A to F, R, digits, the noun and `https`/`www` letters), kept only for non-ASCII letters and decimal digits that survive NFKC (anything else was already refused): 392 code points, 42 prototypes, written out in `_CONFUSABLES`. It is used only to look; names and reasons keep their letters, and `clean_model_text` cuts the match out of the original text. UTS #39 gives `I` no prototype (Cyrillic І, Greek Ι map to `l`), so the nouns accept `l` in Image's place. Surprise: Cyrillic Р and Greek Ρ are P's look-alikes, not R's, so `Р3` reads "P3" and passes (Cyrillic г is UTS #39's r: `г3` is refused). The @ and # look-alikes in UTS #39 are all compatibility characters, already refused. *Frame collisions:* `_frames_by_key` keeps every frame per key in board order and `_frame_named` takes the exact name given, else the first; the sort and the `reading` line use the same function. *One reader per sort:* `build_sort_task` takes `reader=` and raises `MixedReadersError` (a `RuntimeError`, not a `ReaderError`, since no person or provider can cause it) for a reading by another reader or none. *Glued letters:* a label letter followed by `&`, `-`, `–`, `—`, `'` or `’` and then a word character is part of a word unless that next thing is a label letter or `'s` (`B&W`, `B-movie`, `D'Arcy` kept; `A&B`, `A-C`, `B's`, `(A–C)` still stripped), for unit letters too ("Image B&W grain" is kept whole). Reasons and thoughts share `clean_model_text`. Argon's 19 fixture snapshots are byte-identical before and after.
- **Hardening review (2026-10-20).** An adversarial pass found three holes, each with failing cases first (16 failed: `test_the_sort_label_check_reads_digits_and_their_look_alikes` in `tests/test_moodboard_reader_source.py`, `test_reason_cleaning_keeps_other_digits_and_slashed_words` in `tests/test_moodboard_reader_stream.py`). *A regression from the look-alike map:* UTS #39 reads 27 decimal digits as letters (Arabic-Indic `١` as `l`, `٥` and Devanagari `०` as `o`), and the sort-label check ran only on the skeleton, so `R١`, `R١٢`, `R٥` and `R०`, refused before, passed, and `#١٨` was no longer stripped from a reason. `skeletons()` now gives a second, digit reading (`_DIGIT_SKELETON`): every decimal digit is its own value, and a look-alike of 1 or 0 from another script (UTS #39's `l` and `O`, which are what 1 and 0 map to: Cyrillic `Ӏ`, Greek `Ι`, Cyrillic `О`, Greek `Ο`) is that digit, so `RӀ2` and `R1О` are refused as `г3` already was; Latin `RIO` and `Rl` still pass, since the map holds only non-ASCII sources. Both readings are one for one with the text; `_cut` strips the union of their matches. *`B/W`:* `/` glues a letter to a word like `&` and `-` do, so "Image A - B/W grain" keeps "B/W grain" (it lost the B before, and it is the common photo term); "Images A/B" is still stripped. *A stranded join:* "Images A & B-movie glow" left "& B-movie glow"; the join (`&`, `/`, dashes, and, or; not a comma) before a glued word now goes with the label. Left as they were and open: `R-3`, `Image-B` and `ImageB` pass (the rule names R with spaces, and a noun followed by a space). The 4 moodboard_reader test files pass (316); Argon's 19 fixture snapshots are byte-identical.

## 2026-10-20 — Moodboard canvas PR4: review fixes (labels, one-image retry, spent minimum, MCP `only`, `--quiet`)

Five review findings on the PR4 reader, all confirmed and fixed; each behaviour fix has a test. No paid API was called.

- **Label stripping missed ranges and bare labels** (`services/moodboard_reader_stream.py`). "images A–C", "B-D", "Image A to C" and "#3 through #5" kept the second label; "(B)" with no noun survived. The joins now take `-`, `–`, `—`, `to`, `through` and `thru` as well as `,` `/` `&` `and` `or`; a bracketed bare label list ("(B)", "(B, C)", "[A–C]") goes; an "and"/"or" left dangling before punctuation or the end goes, but only when a label was removed ("Rock and" stays). Same function cleans thought text, so both get it. Known edge left: "Image A - B&W" also eats the "B".
- **A one-image retry after `MAX_TOKENS` was the same request again** (`services/moodboard_reader.py`). One ref can't be halved, so its retry now goes at `raised_cap` (twice the cap, bounded by `GEMINI_CHAT_MAX_OUTPUT`, 65,536 for Argon). If it was the whole batch and the cap can't grow, the retry isn't sent: the image is couldn't read with the cut-off reason and `retry:N` isn't in `sent` (so its hold share comes back). The estimate's retry share for a one-image batch is priced at the raised cap. *Out of the finding's scope, same bug:* the sort's retry after `MAX_TOKENS` already doubled its cap, but at the model limit it re-sent the same body; it now stops with `sortError` instead. Plan §5.6 and contract 07 §1.13 say so.
- **The CLI spent line hid requests without a token count.** `spent.usd` is now documented as a minimum (MCP docstring, contract 07 §1.13, MCP-SETUP, SKILL.md), and the CLI adds "N request(s) stopped without a token count, so they aren't in this figure; Google may still bill them, so read it as a minimum." No upper bound printed: which request lacked usage isn't known to the CLI, and the hold already keeps the high share.
- **MCP `only=[3, 5]` was refused by pydantic** (`only: list[str]`). Now `list[str | int]`; `moodboard_client` already `str()`s each item. The new test goes through `mcp._tool_manager.call_tool`, so FastMCP's validation runs (it failed with `string_type` on the old type).
- **`--quiet` printed the estimate block first.** Chose to match the docs and the plan ("summary only"): the quiet branch no longer prints the estimate. The contract now says the non-quiet CLI prints the estimate first.
- **Re-fetched 2026-10-20.** Pricing: Argon $2.00 / $10.00 through Nov 30 2026, $4.00 / $20.00 from Dec 1 ("Output price (including thinking tokens)"). Thinking: `max_output_tokens` includes thinking, hard cutoff, sync cap 65,536 (above it is a 400). The thinking page now describes the cut-off in Interactions API terms (status "incomplete"), not `finishReason: MAX_TOKENS`; the reader uses `generateContent`/`streamGenerateContent`, where the plan's quoted `MAX_TOKENS` applies; the probe should confirm. Structured output: chunks are valid partial JSON; strings take `enum` and `format`, `maxLength` ignored; nothing on key order (as already noted).

## 2026-10-20 — Moodboard canvas PR4: reader dry run, price and spend gate

Branch `feat/moodboard-reader-dry-run` (from origin/main 26572670). Spec: `docs/moodboard-canvas-plan.md` v2.4, the PR4 section, §5.6, §5.6.1, §4.1, Q11, Q16, Q17, Q29. No paid API was called: Google is mocked in every test and in the live check.

- **What.**
  - *Readers file.* `backend/data/moodboard_reader_models.json`: `gemini-4-argon` with dated price rows ($2.00 / $10.00 per 1M through 2026-11-30, $4.00 / $20.00 from 2026-12-01), thinking allowances per level, answer and sort token budgets, image tokens (1120), time bounds, sources with quotes, `checked` 2026-10-20. `validate_models` checks it at load (dates, gaps between rows, levels against `GEMINI_CHAT_THINKING_LEVELS`, caps against `GEMINI_CHAT_MAX_OUTPUT`, `thoughtSummaries` a bool or exactly `"unconfirmed"`).
  - *Stream parser.* `services/moodboard_reader_stream.py`: an incremental SSE decoder (UTF-8 and CR/LF split across chunks, comments, a last event without a blank line), `read_payload` over every part of `candidates[0]` (thought parts kept apart), and `ItemScanner`, a JSON scanner that fires `focus(ref)` when an item's `ref` string closes and `item(obj)` when the item closes. Also `clean_model_text` (drops "Image B", "refs A and C", `#18`, "B's") and `trim_reason` (120 characters, at a word).
  - *Reader.* `services/moodboard_reader.py`: targets, batches of 6 (2 in flight), A to F labels, phase 1 prompt and schema (`ref` first, `reason` last) in `responseFormat.text`, phase 2 sort with Nebula enforcing the rules (fit < 0.5 Unsorted, 8 new looks at most, "Unsorted" never a look, frames matched ignoring case, `alsoIn` at 0.5, hybrids from 3 images), one retry for missing refs (split in two after `MAX_TOKENS`, none after 400/401/403/404), time bounds per level, the trace (`seq` without gaps, 200-character text, thoughts merged to 250 ms), the estimate and `spend_check`. `call_text` is the text-call helper PR19 will use.
  - *Routes.* `POST /api/moodboards/{id}/read/estimate` and `POST /api/moodboards/{id}/read?dryRun=1[&stream=1]` (NDJSON). `_reader_spend_hold` gates agents through `agent_spend.decide`; `_settle_reader_hold` gives back unstarted requests' shares.
  - *CLI and MCP.* `nebula moodboard analyze <board> --read-with gemini-4-argon --dry-run|--estimate [--only] [--thinking-level] [--quiet] [--json]`; `moodboard_analyze(read_with, dry_run, estimate_only, only, thinking_level, include_thoughts)`. `nebula_api.stream_lines` and `moodboard_client.estimate_read` / `dry_read`.
  - *Probe.* `backend/scripts/moodboard_reader_probe.py` (paid, refuses without `--yes-spend`).
  - *Docs.* Contract 07 §1.13 "Reading references", Oracle line and changelog; `skills/nebula/SKILL.md`; `docs/MCP-SETUP.md` (tools list and the moodboard section); the plan's "what Google documents" and "not verified" lists.
- **Fetched facts (2026-10-20).**
  - Google's structured-output guide now leads with the Interactions API, and the sentence "the model will produce outputs in the same order as the keys in the schema" is gone. "The streamed chunks will be valid partial JSON strings…" is still there. So the scanner finds `ref` and the item's end wherever they fall, and doesn't count on `ref` coming first (the schema still asks for it first).
  - The API reference marks `responseSchema` and `_responseJsonSchema` deprecated ("Use responseFormat instead"). Strings take only `enum` and `format`.
  - Pricing page: Gemini 4 Argon Standard input $2.00 and output $10.00 per 1M tokens (thinking included) through November 30, 2026; $4.00 and $20.00 from December 1, 2026. Batch tier is half; not used.
  - Media resolution: 1120 tokens for an image at the default on Gemini 4. Thinking guide: `max_output_tokens` includes thinking and is a hard cutoff; 65,536 is the sync cap; Argon takes low, medium (default) and high.
- **Decisions not in the spec.**
  - *The spend gate's item is `_moodboard-read` on `gemini-chat`, priced by a one-off entry `{per: "request", rows: [{match: {}, price: [low, high]}]}`.* An id starting with `_` makes a refusal name the node ("Gemini chat") instead of an odd id, and the Gemini chat per-model limit in Settings applies, as Q11 asks. With no price the entry is left out, so any USD limit refuses it, like an unpriced node.
  - *The hold is split per request (`shares`), rounding on the first share.* Unstarted requests are given back; a started one stays held at its high estimate, because whether an aborted stream is billed is unconfirmed. A missing key gives the whole hold back before anything is sent.
  - *The high estimate is priced at the higher of today's and the next row.* A read that starts on November 30 and finishes after midnight can't go over it. `spent` uses today's row.
  - *`thoughtSummaries: "unconfirmed"` asks for no thoughts.* Only `true` sends `includeThoughts`, so Argon runs as Q29 b until the probe says the schema holds with summaries on.
  - *No `temperature` in the body.* Argon ignores sampling settings (`GEMINI_CHAT_NO_SAMPLING`), so the reader sends none, like the chat node.
  - *A sort that fails after its retry doesn't fail the read.* Each image falls back to its reading's own look and `sortError` says why, so a paid phase 1 is never thrown away.
  - *An `alsoIn` to a look with no members is dropped.* It would suggest moving an image into an empty, unmade look.
  - *An image whose best look was cut by the 8-new-looks cap goes to Unsorted*, with the reason "already 8 new looks".
  - *Images that aren't files on this computer are skipped* (`unreadable` in the estimate, a `skipped` line) rather than fetched: a dry run should never download.
- **Fixture.** `tests/fixtures/moodboard_reader/argon_batch_sse.txt` is synthetic (5151 bytes), written by hand from the documented shapes, not recorded: thought parts, a chunk with two parts, escapes, multibyte text, `usageMetadata`. The probe's real stream should replace or join it.
- **Tests.** 89 new: `test_moodboard_reader_stream.py` (22: every byte-offset split of the fixture, thoughts out of the answer, parts after the first, cleaning, trim, SSE CR/LF and multibyte), `test_moodboard_reader.py` (44: model file and validator, estimate maths and the price boundary, unpriced, `decide` with the one-off price, 14 images as 6/6/2 with at most 2 in flight, schema, line order, wrong and repeated refs, malformed JSON retry, `MAX_TOKENS` split, partial failure, no retry on 403, quiet and first-byte bounds, reason cleaning, non-streaming reader, interleaved batches, thoughts for false/unconfirmed/true, 250 ms merge, notes opt-in and private notes, sort rules, hybrids, the cap, sort fallback, usage, missing key), `test_moodboard_reader_routes.py` (23: routes, gate, holds, NDJSON, CLI, MCP). Eight mutations (hold give-back on a missing key, settle give-back, thought filtering, parts after the first, `includeThoughts` gating, the `MAX_TOKENS` split, notes opt-in, first ref wins) were each caught, then reverted.
- **Live check (isolated backend, Google mocked, the real CLI over HTTP).** Port 8790 was already held by another agent's harness (a `node .../pf-live/harness.mjs`), and my first CLI attempt reached it (two requests, answered non-JSON); I left it alone and ran uvicorn on a Unix socket instead (`/private/tmp/claude-501/pr4-live.sock`, base URL `http://localhost`). On a 14-image board: the estimate printed "$0.37 to $1.02" at medium; the dry run streamed lines as they came (two batches interleaving, the sort, results, a hybrid suggestion, the done line, spent); `--only 3,5 --json` gave 11 rows; no `--dry-run` was refused; with the per-run limit at $0.05 the refusal gave the full sentence. The board's `version` and `updatedAt` didn't move, and `readings` stayed `{}`.
- **The probe (needs Justin's spend OK; not run).** `cd backend && .venv/bin/python scripts/moodboard_reader_probe.py --board <id> --only 1-6 --level medium --yes-spend` (or up to 6 files instead of `--board`). Two requests on one batch of 6: at most about $0.13 at low, $0.21 at medium, $0.42 at high, at today's prices; input alone is about $0.03, the rest is whatever output and thinking Argon uses. Its JSON sets `thoughtSummaries` (Q29 c; above 10% more output, ask Justin) and the thinking allowances (then clear `allowancesUnconfirmed`).
- **Surprises.** `iso.sh` `cd`s into a worktree that no longer exists; it fails harmlessly and the isolation still applies.

## 2026-10-20 — MCP tools no longer block each other (a wait froze every other call)

Branch `fix/mcp-tools-nonblocking` (from origin/main `87a9ed33`). Found by the subagent research the same day.

- **The bug.** `backend/mcp_server.py` is a FastMCP server (mcp 1.27.0). The low-level server handles each request in its own task, but FastMCP calls a plain `def` tool inline on the event loop (`mcp/server/fastmcp/utilities/func_metadata.py` ~92-95). 32 of the 36 tools were plain functions doing blocking httpx calls. All of a client's calls share one server process (Claude Code subagents share the parent's connection), so a `wait_for_canvas_change` long-poll froze every other call from that client, including a single agent's own parallel calls. Measured on main: in the t2 lab run the main agent's `look_at_canvas` waited 82.6 s behind a watcher subagent's 90 s wait, and the chat message took 85.0 s to its first reply; in T1 a two-node task deadlocked for about 180 s; in a fake-backend repro a `look_at_canvas` sent 0.5 s into a 6 s wait finished at 6.03 s.
- **The fix: offload, don't go async.** Every tool is registered through a new `_tool(annotations=..., waits=...)` decorator (`mcp_server.py` ~119). A plain function is registered as an async wrapper (`functools.wraps`, so FastMCP reads the same signature) that runs it on a worker thread with `_offload` (~113); the module keeps the plain function, so the CLI-style direct calls in the tests are unchanged. `async def` tools are registered as they are and send their blocking work through `_offload` (`run_nodes`, `get_run`, `moodboard_create`, `moodboard_add`, which used `anyio.to_thread.run_sync` directly before). The tools/list output (names, schemas, annotations, descriptions) is byte-identical to main's, checked by dumping both.
  - *Why not an async HTTP client.* `nebula_api.NebulaAPI` and `moodboard_client` are shared with the `nebula` CLI, which is sync, and `moodboard_client` also reads files and downloads links. Making them async would mean two copies or an async CLI, a far larger change than the bug needs. Offloading is the pattern `run_nodes` already used, and it is one mechanical change in one file.
- **Thread pools.** Two limiters of our own: `_CALL_LIMITER` (16) for short calls and `_WAIT_LIMITER` (32) for calls that can hold a thread for minutes (`wait_for_canvas_change`, `get_proposal`, the run call of `run_nodes`/`get_run`, the board downloads). Never anyio's default limiter (40): the stdio transport reads stdin and writes stdout through it (`anyio.wrap_file` in `mcp/server/stdio.py`), so 40 long waits on it would stall the server's own I/O, which is a deadlock. With separate pools, any number of waits leaves the short calls 16 threads. A wait past 32 queues until one returns; events are cursor-based, so it misses nothing.
- **Shared state, audited for concurrent calls.**
  - HTTP: each call builds its own `NebulaAPI` and sends a one-shot `httpx.request`. There is no shared client, session or pool. Safe.
  - `_base_url`: set once by `--url`/`NEBULA_URL` before `mcp.run()`, only read after. `NEBULA_URL_FILE` is re-read and re-verified on every call (`services/backend_address.verified_url`) with no cache. Safe.
  - Token and cursor name: read from `os.environ` (`with_identity`, `_cursor_name`), which nothing writes after startup (the token files are loaded before `mcp.run()`). Safe.
  - `ctx`: only read (`ctx.session.client_params.clientInfo.name`). No tool calls ctx's async methods from a thread. Safe.
  - Agent workspace: a ContextVar (`services/agent_workspaces._workspace`) set before `mcp.run()`. anyio's `to_thread.run_sync` runs the function in a copy of the caller's context, so the threads see it (`test_offloaded_tools_keep_the_callers_context`).
  - `moodboard_client._run` starts its own event loop (`asyncio.run`) when none is running in its thread; on a worker thread none is, so each call gets its own loop. Module globals there and in `character_client` are constants.
  - Not made safe here: two agents editing the same node still race (last write wins). That is the canvas's missing base-revision check (lab T5), not this server.
- **Cancellation (found in review, fixed).** Claude Code sends `notifications/cancelled` when a call is interrupted. The SDK answers "Request cancelled" at once and cancels the call's scope, but anyio doesn't abandon a worker thread, so the call waits for it. Two problems came out of that, both new with the offloading (on main the loop was blocked, so a cancel was only read after the call had answered):
  - *The server crashed.* When the thread returned, nothing awaited between it and the SDK's `respond()` (`mcp/server/lowlevel/server.py` ~800), so the call ended normally instead of as cancelled, the SDK responded a second time, failed `assert not self._completed` and the exception took down the server's task group: every agent's tools gone. Any offloaded tool did it, even a 1 s `describe_node`. Fix: `_offload` ends with `anyio.lowlevel.checkpoint_if_cancelled()`, so a cancelled call raises there and the SDK suppresses the duplicate.
  - *A cancelled wait kept polling* to its own deadline (up to 300 s), holding a wait-pool slot. Fix: `wait_for_canvas_change` and `get_proposal` call `_stop_if_cancelled()` (`anyio.from_thread.check_cancelled()`, a no-op off a worker thread, so the CLI and direct calls are unchanged) before each poll, so they stop within one poll (25 s at most).
  - Not changed: a single long request (`run_nodes`, `get_run` with a long `wait_seconds`, a board link download) holds its thread until Nebula answers, at most its `wait` + 30 s. The run itself keeps going either way, as before.
- **Tests (failed first on main).** New `backend/tests/test_mcp_nonblocking.py`, 5 tests at first (9 after review), through the MCP protocol (an in-memory client session) against a fake Nebula on an ephemeral port, adapted from the lab's `blocktest/`: a `look_at_canvas` 0.3 s into a 3 s wait answers in under 1.5 s (on main it landed at 3.02 s, with the wait); 3 waits against a wait pool shrunk to 2 still leave `look_at_canvas` prompt; a guard that every registered tool is async and either carries the `_tool` offload marker or is one of the four named async tools whose source calls `_offload(`; the ContextVar reaches the thread; the plain functions stay callable directly. On main 4 of the 5 failed; the last pins behaviour that must not move. Added in review, failing before their fix: a cancelled `wait_for_canvas_change`, `get_proposal` and slow `describe_node` each answer "Request cancelled", give their thread back within 1.5 s and leave the server answering (before: all three crashed it); a direct `wait_for_canvas_change` call still waits its full timeout. The guard also covers resources and prompts (there are none today).
- **Live check (lab t2, rerun).** Same scenario, `claude -p --model claude-sonnet-5-5`, subscription login (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset), `--max-budget-usd 0.5`, one run. Backend from this worktree on 127.0.0.1:8797 with a fresh isolated state dir, deleted afterwards. Main agent's `look_at_canvas`: 82.6 s before, about 20 ms after (sent 21.44 s, answered 21.46 s, while the watcher's 90 s wait was in flight from 10.80 s to 101.10 s). Chat message to first reply text: 85.0 s before, 5.2 s after. Cost $0.152 (higher than the first t2's $0.051 because the prompt cache started cold). Isolation: 69 lsof samples of the MCP server process during the run showed only connections to 127.0.0.1:8797, none to 8000-8010.
  - *Review rerun* (same scenario, one run, with the cancellation fix): the main agent's `look_at_canvas` took 11 ms (sent 18.13 s, answered 18.15 s) while the watcher's first 90 s wait ran from 10.23 s to 100.31 s; chat message to first reply 3.0 s; $0.090. 82 lsof samples of the lab's MCP server showed 77 connections, all to 127.0.0.1:8797. The isolated state dir was deleted afterwards.
  - *Real stdio server, cancel probe:* a `describe_node` cancelled 0.3 s into a 1 s request. The pre-review offloading build answered "Request cancelled", then exited with code 1 (`AssertionError: Request already responded to`) before the next call; this build answers the next call and keeps running; main (87a9ed33) never sees the cancel, because its blocked loop reads it only after answering.
- **Docs.** `docs/MCP-SETUP.md`, the `wait_for_canvas_change` bullet: a wait holds only its own call, other calls on the same server answer meanwhile, the pool sizes, and that a cancelled wait stops at its next poll.

## 2026-10-20 — Q38 answered: the Agent log shows by default and can be hidden

Branch `fix/agentlog-mcp-actions` (HEAD 7b8fd709, uncommitted). Justin, relayed by GM: "no but it can be toggled off to get out of the way." GM's reading, built here: shown by default, no Settings switch needed and no chat-open requirement; the person can hide it when it's in the way.

- **Default on.** `uiStore.loadAgentLogEnabled` reads a missing preference as on; an explicit `'0'` stays off (`uiStore.ts:120-130`, storage reads and writes now in try/catch). `AgentLog.tsx`: `visible = enabled`, the chat half of the gate is gone.
- **Hide from the log.** An eye-off button on the log's row (`agent-log__hide`, "Hide agent log") sets the same preference as Settings. It leaves "Agent log hidden · Show again" in the log's spot for 6 s (`AGENT_LOG_HIDDEN_NOTICE_MS`), held while hovered or keyboard-focused, Escape dismisses. Keyboard path: hidden with Enter/Space (`click.detail === 0`), focus moves to "Show again", then back to the log's header. A mouse hide leaves focus alone so the notice can time out. Settings > Preferences > "Agent log" ("Every agent's actions, bottom right") stays the lasting way back; turning it on there drops the notice. Connect your agent untouched.
- **Layout.** New tokens `--chat-launcher-bottom` / `--chat-launcher-size` (layouts.css; Slava 24 px / 48 px), used by the launcher, the log and the chat. Stack: launcher, 8 px, log, 8 px, chat. The chat reserves `--agent-log-h` (collapsed 44, open `--agent-h-open`, Slava empty `--agent-h-empty`) while the log or its notice shows (`body.agent-log-reserved`, was `agent-log-enabled` with a fixed collapsed height that the 80 px min-height overran). The chat's height now subtracts its own bottom, so it no longer runs 8 px past the top gutter. Collapsed log: one centred row, no resize grip, no 80 px floor.
- **Drag.** `agentLogLayout.ts` (pure helpers moved out of `AgentLog.tsx` for the react-refresh lint rule): `keepClearOfRect` lifts a log that would cover the launcher, applied while dragging, on resize, and on load (a saved position is also pulled back on screen). Sizes come from `offsetWidth/Height` so the entry spring's scale doesn't skew them.
- **Motion.** The log and the notice spring in (the undo notice's `linear()` spring, 420 ms); the buttons press with it; reduced motion turns both off.
- **Decisions not in the brief.**

  - *The reservation holds for a dragged log too.* A first version dropped it once the log was dragged; live, a log dragged a few px then sat on the chat's bottom. Reserving always costs a dragged-away log's 52 px of chat height, which is what the branch did before.
  - *AgentLog is lazy-loaded* (`App.tsx:51`, Suspense at `:312`), with `store/agentLogStore` imported eagerly at `App.tsx:17` so entries still collect from page load. The change put the entry at 513,770 B raw, over the 512,000 budget (main had about 1.3 KB headroom); now 504,864 B raw / 145,824 B gzip. Limit not raised.
  - *Empty open log height* `--agent-h-empty` 108 → 154 px: its "standby" line was clipped (worse before, when the drag row and header both had padding).
  - *Divider* under the open log's header moved to the whole row so it runs under the hide button.
  - *"Default skin" is reachable only by removing `app-slava-restraint`* (`lib/skins.ts` forces Slava); the live check did that by hand.
- **Tests (failed first):** `src/store/uiStore.agentLog.test.ts` (missing pref reads on; `'0'` stays off), `src/components/panels/AgentLog.test.tsx` (chat closed shows; hide sets `'0'`, notice, focus, Show again; timeout; keyboard hold + Escape; Settings round trip; `keepClearOfRect`). 8 of 14 failed before the change. The "chat keeps its room while the notice shows" assertion came with its fix and was checked to fail without it. Updated: `tests/agentLog.test.tsx` (the gate test now says the opposite), `tests/Settings.test.tsx` (the switch starts on; new description).
- **Docs.** Plan §7.6 (answered), header bullet, §3.5, §5.9 "See all actions →" and PR9a (no chat-first), §7 intro; `docs/MCP-SETUP.md`.

The person's writes, refusals and the dry run send nothing. Contract 07 §1.12.

That is a layout choice, not only "the log held chat lines", so it stays. **Question for Justin:** the chat starts closed (`DEFAULT_PANELS.chat.visible: false`), so an MCP-only person with the log switched on sees nothing until they open the chat. Show it with the switch alone?

  - *A board write moves no cursor.* Pointing at a Moodboard node showing that board was possible but would pre-empt the Studio cursor work in the moodboard plan (PR for `moodboard_edit`).

  - **Not done, needs a rebase:** this branch is on 26572670; origin/main has since taken #94 (checked board edits: `store.update_with_before`, the `/edits` route with the agent's own `say`, `board.*` journal summaries) and #95. A merge conflicts in `main.py` (update, keep, analyze), contract 07 and these notes, and an agent's `/edits` batch (on main, the path for `moodboard_add`, `nebula moodboard add` and an update's undo) sends no log line. On rebase: take `before` from `update_with_before` instead of the extra read, and send one line per `/edits` batch (its `say`, else the board journal's summary), so the log has one source of words per change.

## 2026-10-20 — Agent runs and proposals show failures; arranged nodes and Fit view stay in sight

Branch `fix/agent-run-errors-proposals` (from origin/main 26572670). Found in the Thursday demo dry run (steps 7, 9, 11, 12): an agent's `run_nodes` on GPT Image 2 with no key came back `finished` with the error beside it while the card stayed idle; `look_at_canvas` and `view_output` hid the message; a proposal whose run couldn't start had no warning until after Accept; `arrange: true` landed nodes under the top bar; Fit view left the ghost off screen; the bar cut the agent's note to one line.

- **Why the two paths differed.** The canvas runs through `/api/execute`, whose `validate_graph` pre-call check broadcasts `validationError` (Krea's "Missing API key: KREA_API_TOKEN"), and `_emit_and_sync` broadcasts each node's events. The agent's path (`POST /api/graph/run`, `run_graph` → `_execute_cli_run`) skipped `validate_graph` and kept every per-node event to itself (journal only), so GPT Image 2's handler raised `MissingCredentialError` that only the HTTP reply carried. On top of that, the frontend's `graphSync` merge set `state` to the backend's "complete" for any node with outputs, so even a broadcast error on a node with an older image vanished with the sync that ends every CLI run.
- **What.**
  - *Backend.* `run_graph` runs `validate_graph` (and the cycle check) before the spending check; a refusal returns `_refused_cli_run`'s reply (`status: "failed"`, `error: "Nothing ran, so nothing was spent. …"`, `errors`, empty `results`), announces it exactly as `/api/execute` does (`_announce_validation_errors`, shared by `/api/execute`, `/api/execute-node` and cinema generate-shot: `validationError` broadcast, `run.failed` journal lines, the node's error recorded), and is kept in `_cli_runs` so `get_run` / `nebula result` repeat it. `_execute_cli_run` sends every event through `_emit_and_sync`. `_cli_run_response` reports `failed` whenever any node errored (as `execution_runs` already did for canvas runs), naming the node(s) in `error`, with `results` of what finished. `services/node_errors.py` keeps each node's last error (set by an ErrorEvent or a refusal, cleared when the node runs again, pruned with the graph, cleared on graph replace); the snapshot carries `error`/`errorHint`; `/preview` and `/path` answer 409 "has no output: its last run failed: …" (and `X-Nebula-Last-Run-Error` beside an older output).
  - *Agents.* `look_at_canvas` and `nebula look` show the error under the node; `view_output` returns the error (or the older output with a note); `nebula run` prints each failed node and exits 1; `nebula path` prints the 409 detail. `propose_change` and `nebula propose` add a `warning` naming the run's nodes that can't run here (`cost.notReady`, built by `_not_ready_nodes` with `node_readiness.instance_missing`, the words `find_nodes`/`describe_node` use, read at the values Accept would write; route-table nodes get `node_route`'s own message, Krea nodes their saved `_kreaAuth`); `nebula propose`/`proposals` print a `can't` row per node.
  - *Canvas.* `graphStore`: nodes a foreign run (an agent's, another tab's) put in queued/executing go back to idle when that run ends (`foreignRunNodes`, `settleForeignRun`), and a graphSync over unchanged outputs keeps `error`, `skipped`, `queued` and `executing` (`RUN_HELD_STATES`); new outputs still replace them. Ghosts show the real node's ⚠ with its title (`ghostKeyWarning`), or the backend's reason when the canvas can't check it; the bar lists not-ready nodes under the summary (`useProposalNotReady`, three lines, the rest in the details), re-checked live against the saved keys. The note wraps to three lines (`line-clamp`), and when clamped, "Read the whole note" opens it in the details. `arrangeNewNodes` takes the uncovered area (`visibleFlowBox`) and lands the block inside it when it fits, clear of other nodes when there's room (`freeSpotInside`); otherwise `ArrangeController` springs the view to it (`viewportRevealing` + `springViewport` on `AGENT_CURSOR_SPRING`). `useFitCanvasView` (Shift+1, the toolbar button, the command palette) frames open proposals' ghosts with the nodes.
- **Judgment calls.**
  - *Accept stays enabled for a run that can't start, label unchanged.* That is exactly what the canvas Run button does for a node with a missing key: it stays enabled, the backend's `validate_graph` refuses the run before any provider call, and the node shows "Missing API key". Disabling Accept would also block the non-running parts of the proposal (new nodes, wires) and diverge from Run. The warning sits above the button instead.
  - *Ghost ⚠ uses the canvas's live key check; the bar uses the backend's list, filtered live.* The ghost must look like a real node, so it uses the same `nodeKeyStatus` + title. The bar shows the backend's reasons (wired-route blockers the canvas can't see) but drops a "needs …" row once the person's saved keys pass the live check, so a key added while the proposal is open clears it. Route reasons stay until the proposal is remade.
  - *Readiness covers upstream nodes with outputs too*, since the run reads them and a cached ancestor that can't run is still "set up wrong"; the proposal's `upTo` count already treats them the same way.
  - *`failed` when any node fails*, even if others finished: the existing contract (`get_run` documents running/finished/cancelled/failed; `execution_runs` marks a canvas run failed on any node error). `results` still has what finished.
  - *The refused CLI run returns 200 with `status: "failed"`*, not 4xx, so the reply has the run shape every client already parses (`_report`, MCP `run_nodes`).
  - *Arrange is clamped into view first, then panned as a fallback*, instead of always panning: the person's view doesn't move when the block fits.
  - *Fit-padding selector.* `computeCanvasFitPadding` looked for `.canvas-tabs`, which the floating top bar lost when it became the workspace header; it now also reads `.canvas-tabs-wrap`. This is why Fit view and the canvas's own auto-pan for new nodes let nodes sit under the top bar.
  - *Settings unchanged.* Nothing in Settings changed, including Preferences > Agent spending > "Connect your agent".
- **Tests changed beside the code.** `test_agent_spend.py`, `test_mcp_tools.py` and `test_provider_start_admission.py` stub `validate_graph` where they run keyless paid nodes through `/api/graph/run` to test spending (one test that relies on the real check restores it). Five frontend test files gained a `useStoreApi` mock (Fit view reads the canvas size), and two `wsClient` mocks now fan each event out to every subscriber, since Fit view imports the proposals store, which subscribes too.
- **Live check (isolated backend 8791, Vite 5791, Puppeteer 1440x900, real stdio MCP client as `claude-code` with an app token).** `edit_canvas` with `arrange: true`, including nodes moved to just under the top bar: every node landed with its top at or below 88 px (bar bottom 64). `run_nodes` n2 (GPT Image 2, no key): `status: "failed"`, "Nothing ran, so nothing was spent", the card shows "Missing API key: OPENAI_API_KEY", `look_at_canvas` and `view_output` give the text, `get_run` repeats the reply. Proposing Krea 2: ghost ⚠ "Needs KREA_API_TOKEN", the bar line, the `warning` in the reply; the note wraps to three lines and "Read the whole note" shows it all; after zooming the ghost off screen, Shift+1 brought it back; Accept ran and Krea 2 showed "Missing API key: KREA_API_TOKEN". CLI: `nebula run` exit 1 with the node line, `look`, `path`, `propose` (`can't` row and `warning:`). 0 requests to 8000-8010 or 5173; canary 0 hits; no keys anywhere.
- **Review pass (same day).** Re-ran the dry run's steps live (isolated backend 8791, Vite 5791, real stdio MCP client, a Moodboard node made to fail in its handler by deleting its board, so the handler-error path ran too, not only the pre-call check). Three fixes, each with a test that fails without it: Fit view and arrange now also clear the proposal bar (`.proposal-bar-panel` in `computeCanvasFitPadding`; with a proposal open, Fit view had left a node under the bar); `view_output` on a node whose output is a value (text, a Moodboard), not a picture, now carries the same "from before its last run, which failed" note (the preview's 415 sends `X-Nebula-Last-Run-Error`, and `NebulaAPIError` keeps the response headers); `node_errors` drops an `errorHint` that only repeats the error less its full stop (`classify_error`'s fallback). Still open: a reload repaints a failed node from the backend's export, which has no error state, so the card shows "complete" (or idle) while `look_at_canvas` still says error; the same is true of the person's own failed runs on main.
- **Surprises.** The canvas already pans to an agent's new nodes on its own (node-added auto-fit); it measures the chrome with `computeCanvasFitPadding`, so with the stale top-bar selector it would leave them just under the bar, which likely explains shot 13 (not re-run on main). `find_nodes "krea 2"` lists nothing without a Krea key or sign-in, since it lists only nodes that can run.
- **Follow-up (2026-10-20): the review's three open items.**
  - *A failed node keeps its error through a reload, a project switch and a restart.* `services/node_errors.py` now keeps errors per project (node ids restart in each project) in `node-errors.json` in the state dir, and stores the card's `category` too. `main._cli_node_to_rf` gives such a node `state: "error"`, `error`, `errorFriendly`, `errorCategory`, so graphSync, `GET /api/projects/{id}` (the reload path, via `_overlay_live_project`) and the snapshot saved on a switch all carry it, for the person's own canvas runs as well as agents'. The store follows the open project (`use_project` in `export_graph_for_frontend` and `_commit_project_workspace`, `_restore_node_errors` at boot); loading a graph over the project or clearing it forgets its errors; deleting a project for good (purge, Empty trash) forgets them; Recently deleted keeps them for a restore. Frontend: a graphSync whose node says `error` now shows it on a node with no output too (it used to keep the tab's own state), unless the tab has queued or started that node since. **Restart decision:** keep them on disk. Run history can't seed them (a record says a run failed, not each node's message, and agents' runs aren't in it; the journal is memory-only), and the card should not tell a different story from `look_at_canvas` after a restart. The Electron app runs the same bundle against its sidecar with `NEBULA_STATE_DIR=<app data>/state`, so it reads the same data from the same file. Not migrated from `~/.nebula` by `desktop/migration.mjs`, but neither are projects (see questions).
  - *Readiness warning per surface.* `canvas_proposals.readiness_warning(cost, lister=...)`: the HTTP reply says "GET /api/agent/nodes lists them", `propose_change` rewords it from `cost.notReady` with "find_nodes", `nebula propose` with "`nebula context`" (plain and `--json`). The only other place the text appeared was `describe_node`'s 404, which only MCP calls. Docs: MCP-SETUP, SKILL.md.
  - *Accept that took ~20 s: reproduced and fixed.* Live harness (isolated backend 8781, Vite 5781), 16 Accepts mixing MCP and HTTP proposals of 1-6 nodes: first event after the click went 183 ms, 252, 574 ... 24,167 ms, one `propose_change` timed out and one run never started within 40 s. The backend log showed every stalled Accept and run finishing right after a `PUT /api/projects/{id}` (the canvas autosave) that took 10-35 s. Root cause: `save_project` ran `validate_file_references` on the event loop over the whole snapshot, run history included: 2,505 strings, 125 distinct, each through `require_allowed_path` (~4 ms of path resolving and protected-root stats). Everything else (the Accept reply, `execute-node`, every canvas event) waited behind it, which is why the run started only once that request finished. Fixes, each with a test that failed first (`tests/test_project_save_event_loop.py`): `validate_file_references` checks each distinct reference once (10.6 s to 0.73 s offline for that snapshot); `save_project` runs the check in a worker thread before taking the catalog lock (`_stage_project_snapshot(ingress_checked=True)`); `_workspace_context`, read on every canvas event, uses `ProjectStore.workspace()` (the two fields, cached on the catalog file's inode/mtime/size) instead of parsing, upgrading and deep-copying every project. After: 22 Accepts, all started, median first event 779 ms; backend ping from outside during Accepts p95 138 ms, max 428 ms. What remains is the page: a CPU profile shows React re-rendering every ModelNode on each store change (each subscribes to the whole `nodes` array), which in dev mode with ~100 nodes kept the page busy for seconds (one Accept at 28 s first event, with the backend answering in under 2 s). Not fixed here (see questions).
- **Follow-up review (2026-10-20).** Re-ran each item live (isolated backend 8781, Vite 5781, real stdio MCP client and the real `nebula` CLI, Puppeteer; 0 blocked requests outside the canary step, 0 canary hits, no keys). Item 2 held: MCP said `find_nodes`, `nebula propose` said `` `nebula context` ``. Item 3 held: 18 Accepts (MCP and CLI, 1-6 nodes, a third with a keyless GPT Image 2) on a 107-125 node canvas with 59 run records all started; click to first run event median 1.4 s, max 4.5 s; backend ping p50 4 ms, p95 74 ms, max 325 ms. Ids aren't handed out again in a project (`CLIGraph.add_node`: the counter moves past them), so `node_errors.prune` is gone and a deleted node's error waits for the undo; an empty canvas forgets errors only when it was cleared (`cli_graph._counter == 0`), not when emptied node by node.
