## 2026-10-20 — The Projects screen follows projects made elsewhere

Branch `fix/projects-follow-agent` (from origin/main 26572670). The Thursday demo dry run's step 1: MCP `new_project "Summer campaign"` while the person sat on Projects made the project, but the screen didn't change or list it until a reload.

- **Why.** The tab follows an agent's switch only from the project it holds (`switchedAwayFrom` needs a project context). A tab on Projects with nothing open (a first run, or after deleting the open project) has none, so it dropped the graphSync. With a project still loaded, it followed but stayed on Projects. And nothing told Projects about renames, deletes, restores or saves made by another writer: only a switch of the open project sends graphSync.
- **What.**
  - *Backend:* `projectsChanged` ({change, projectId}) goes out over the socket after every change to the saved-project list: create, open, save or rename (`PUT`), cover, delete, restore, delete for good, emptying Recently deleted (both trash routes), and a recovered copy. graphSync didn't fit (it carries the open project's graph and moves the canvas), and `storedAssetChanged` is for moodboards and Characters, so this is a new event. `save_project` became a thin route around `_save_project` (the old body, unchanged) so the broadcast follows the commit.
  - *Frontend (`projectStore`):* on Projects, `projectsChanged` lists again (`relistProjects`: one request at a time, a newer listing never replaced by an older one, the new workspace revision taken only when no project is open). Off Projects it marks the list stale, and `goHome` lists again. An agent's switch is followed with no project loaded too, when it was made from the revision this tab listed, and following now opens the canvas from Projects (as `new_project` / `open_project` document: "open it on the canvas"; the canvas follows).
- **Decisions not in the brief.**
  - *Projects goes to the canvas on an agent's switch.* The toast's comment said it showed "on the canvas and on Projects", so staying on Projects may have been meant. But the tools say the project opens on the canvas, and the dry run expected the screen to change. The toast keeps its Back button. With nothing open before, there's nothing to go back to and it names the agent only.
  - *On Projects, a switch the person made in another window, or a delete of the loaded project, no longer stops the screen with "The active project changed in another window".* With nothing unsaved and no run going, the tab lets go of the project it still had loaded (`releaseLoadedProject`, shared with deleting the open project) and lists again. With unsaved work, it is still the conflict that offers a recovered copy. On the canvas nothing changed.
  - *The toast's way back follows the list:* renamed there, gone once that project is deleted (found live: it offered "Back to" a deleted project).
- **Not changed.** Settings (including Agent spending > Connect your agent) and the desktop shell: Electron loads the same bundle, and its startup socket probe only reads graphSync, proposalSync and personRequired frames, so a new event type passes it by.
- **Tests.** `backend/tests/test_projects_changed.py` (4: the agent's new project on an empty workspace, every list change announced in order, the shared trash routes, a refused change announces nothing). 3 fail on main; the refusal guard passes there by construction. `projectStore.switch.test.ts` (+9: follow from Projects with nothing open, Projects to the canvas with a project loaded, no follow from a revision it never listed, relist on Projects, revision kept with a project open, relist deferred to goHome, the toast's way back kept current, letting go on Projects, unsaved work still a conflict). 6 fail on main's store; the way-back test was added after that run. Two existing tests changed with the behaviour: `test_projects.py` asserted `canvasPins` was the very last broadcast of an open (now graphSync, canvasPins, projectsChanged); `paramsVersionReload.test.ts` "ignores a sync with another revision" stayed on Projects after `initialize` (where the app starts), so it now sets the canvas, and a new case pins the Projects behaviour (let go, no merge, nothing saved).
- **Live check** (isolated `devserver.py` on 8793 with the person link, Vite on 5793, Puppeteer 1440x900, a real stdio MCP client as `claude-code` with a connected-app token, CDP blocking 8000-8010 and 5173, dead proxy, no interception). `new_project "Summer campaign"` from an empty Projects screen showed its canvas and the toast within 594 ms. From Projects with it loaded, `new_project "Autumn launch"` opened the canvas with "Back to “Summer campaign”". A CLI-style writer's rename, delete (into Recently deleted) and restore showed on Projects with no reload. A second tab's New project: the first tab, on Projects, listed it with no conflict message. Then `open_project` from that first tab (nothing loaded) opened the canvas in both tabs with "Back to “Untitled project”". 0 blocked attempts.
- **Review fixes (same day).**
  - *A reconnect lists again.* Events aren't replayed after a socket drops, and a tab on Projects with nothing loaded dropped the first sync after reconnecting (no `projectSwitch`), so a project made meanwhile stayed missing and the tab kept a stale revision (its next New project refused). Now a sync with a revision that tab never listed lists again. The "switch from a workspace it never listed" case still doesn't follow, but lists too.
  - *The way back on the canvas.* The "Back to …" fix only ran on Projects, but after a follow the toast is on the canvas. A `projectsChanged` for the way-back project now lists on any screen, so deleting it elsewhere drops the button there too (live: gone in 105 ms).
  - *The toast's timer.* `wayBackIn` built a new notice on every listing, which restarted the toast's 15 s timer; it now keeps the same notice when nothing changed.
  - Tests: 3 new cases in `projectStore.switch.test.ts` (reconnect lists again, way back dropped on the canvas, toast left alone) and one changed (the unlisted-revision case now expects a listing); all four fail on the builder's store.
  - `docs/projects-implementation-notes.md` said deleting an inactive project broadcasts nothing; amended, with a dated section for this change.
  - Seen live, not changed: with Settings open on Projects (shot `02-projects-settings-open`), an agent's `new_project` takes the person to the canvas and the Settings dock closes, as opening any project from Projects does. Relevant if a demo starts on Settings and then calls `new_project`.
- **Follow-up (2026-10-20): "Unsaved changes" on open, and relist retries.** The review's two open items.
  - *Root cause of the flash.* A project saved without a view (every new project, and any an agent filled with no canvas open) has `viewport: null`, and `applyProject` records that as saved (`lastSaved`, projectStore.ts). When the canvas then mounts, React Flow places its own first camera: `onViewportInitialized` remembers its starting view on an empty canvas (Canvas.tsx, `rememberViewport(instance.getViewport())`), and on a graph the `fitView` prop's first fit arrives through `onMove`. Both went through `setCanvasViewport` to the autosave subscription, which called `markDirty`, so the person's tab showed "Unsaved changes" and autosaved `{x:0,y:0,zoom:1}` (or the fit) about 600 ms later. Not a params normalization, a node measure pass or a hydrate: the snapshot leaves measurements out, and `executionStatuses`/the params read the same before and after. Only from a mount: opening or following from Projects, a reload, a follow while in a studio. A follow on the canvas keeps the mounted canvas, so it showed it only when that canvas had mounted empty (see the review bullet below). A tab without the person's credential never saves its camera, so it never showed it either.
  - *Fix.* Canvas marks the camera it places itself (`setCanvasViewport(viewport, { initial: true })`: onInit's start, and the first `onMove` with no input event when the mount fit a graph with no saved view; the person's wheel, drag or pinch ends that). `uiStore.canvasViewportInitial` carries the mark, and `adoptCanvasCamera` folds that camera into `lastSaved` when it is the only difference from the last save; otherwise it is `markDirty` as before. So the project reads "Saved", nothing is sent, and the camera goes out with the next real change. A pan, zoom or edit right after opening still shows "Unsaved changes" and autosaves (tests and live).
  - *Params that need migrating.* Not unsaved, on purpose. The backend upgrades every read and commits the upgrade when the project opens (live: the catalog on disk went from 4,096 to 64,000 and `_paramsVersion` 1 on Open), so what the canvas shows is what is stored. Marking it unsaved would only send the same values back and blame the person for a change Nebula made.
  - *Relist retry.* A failed listing on Projects is tried again quietly 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 s later (6 requests at most), then on window `focus`, `online` or the socket's first sync after a reconnect. Each retry goes through `relistProjects`, so it is still one request at a time and an older reply never wins. Off Projects nothing is scheduled and a pending retry sends nothing; `goHome` lists again with a fresh count. Not cleared by a store subscription when leaving, to save entry bytes: a leftover timer fires once and does nothing.
  - *Tests.* `projectStore.opensSaved.test.ts` (10: open from Projects, with nodes and a fit, `new_project` followed from Projects with nothing open, followed with a project loaded, followed from a studio, open after a reload, upgraded params; and three real changes right after opening still save). The 7 "reads as saved" cases failed before the fix; the 3 real-change cases passed before and after. `projectStore.relistRetry.test.ts` (6: a blip, the bounded backoff, focus/online after the retries ran out, a reconnect's sync, stopping off Projects and listing on return, one request at a time with the newer list winning). 5 failed before; the stop-off-Projects case held already.
  - *Live* (isolated backend 8771, Vite 5771, canary 8772, control 8773, CDP block on 8000-8010 and 5173, dead proxy). Before: `new_project` from Projects read Saved, then "Unsaved changes" at +70 ms for ~600 ms, then autosaved `viewport {0,0,1}`; opening a no-view project with 2 nodes after a reload went straight to "Unsaved changes". After: every case reads "Saved" with no save sent (`new_project` from Projects, open from Projects, follow from Projects and from the canvas, reload then open, upgraded params), the label watched by a MutationObserver and screenshots every 100 ms; a scroll right after opening shows "Unsaved changes" and autosaves the new view. Relist: one 502 retried after 1.1 s with no error shown; with every listing failing, 6 requests (0, 1.2, 3.4, 7.6, 15.8, 32.2 s) then none, and `online` listed again; leaving Projects stopped them (no request in 20 s), and coming back listed.
  - *Build budget.* The entry is now 512,551 bytes raw (147,715 gzip), 551 over the 512,000 limit (it had ~56 bytes of headroom). Left over on purpose: a separate PR frees room.
- **Follow-up review (2026-10-20): two fixes.**
  - *A follow on a canvas that mounted empty still flashed "Unsaved changes".* Repro (live, before this fix): from Projects an agent's `new_project` mounts an empty canvas; its next `open_project` of a project with nodes and no saved view showed "Unsaved changes" at +971 ms and sent a PUT. React Flow's `fitView` prop queues one fit and runs it once the canvas has nodes, so on an empty mount it fires when the followed graph arrives, but Canvas only marked the first fit when the mount already had nodes. It now marks the first move with no input event whenever the mount had a fit queued (`fitEnabled`). New `components/Canvas.firstCamera.test.tsx` (React Flow's props captured): the empty-mount case failed before, the four others (a graph's first fit, a person's move and everything after it, a later programmatic move, a saved view) pass. Live after: Saved only, no PUT, the canvas fitted.
  - *Try again could lose to an older quiet retry.* `retry()` listed without the listing generation, so a backoff retry sent before it and answered after it replaced its newer list. It now takes a generation like `relistProjects`. Test in `projectStore.relistRetry.test.ts` (failed before).
  - Build budget after these two fixes: 512,537 bytes raw (147,733 gzip), 537 over the 512,000 limit; left for the separate PR.
  - Seen live, not changed: an agent's edit right after `new_project` shows "Unsaved changes" (~0.6-1.9 s, the fit animation re-arms the 600 ms timer) and then saves, because the tab saves back the agent's nodes and the fit camera; that is an agent change, as the brief allows, but the Thursday recording will show it whenever the agent adds nodes. A follow on a canvas that already fitted keeps the old camera (no refit, and a target's saved view isn't applied), as before this branch.

## 2026-10-20 — Review of the first-load split: World fallback face, load-failure boundary

Adversarial review of the entry split below. Rebuilt and re-measured; checked the split modules are absent from the entry, the desktop build, the CSS move and the first opens.

- **Verified, no change needed:** none of the six split modules (nor PaperRunInspection / BatchRunInspection) has a byte in `assets/index-*.js` (source-map attribution with bud-sizes.cjs). A desktop build (`NEBULA_DESKTOP_BUILD=1`, base `./`) loaded over `file://` fetches all six chunks and both CSS files by relative URL (`import(`./RunHistoryPanel-*.js`)` with `import.meta.url`), with no failed request. Moving `run-history.css` and `onboarding.css` into their chunks changed nothing: computed styles and boxes of every element in the open Run History panel (20) and the tour (11) are identical between a main build and this branch, in vite preview. The tour opened from the keyboard with focus on Take the tour, and Escape returned focus to Help. The entry-split guard also catches a re-export (`export { WorldPreview } from …` in a startup helper).
- **Fixed: the World fallback was not the viewer's face.** It drew the placeholder without the globe, the World badge, the Explore label or the thumbnail, so all four popped in when the chunk landed (same height, visibly different card). The face now lives in `components/nodes/WorldPreviewFace.tsx` (helpers in `lib/worldCard.ts`), and both WorldPreview's button and the fallback draw it. `tests/components/DeferredPanels.test.tsx` now asserts the fallback's class and inner HTML equal the arrived viewer's, for the mesh card and for a World with a thumbnail. Before the fix the World case failed. Live, with the viewer chunks held: identical cards and heights before and after.
- **Fixed: a chunk that fails to load took the whole app down.** These pieces used to be in the entry and could not fail to load. Now a rejected `import()` (web build replaced under an open tab, a flaky disk) throws out of `React.lazy`, and with no error boundary in the app that unmounts everything. `components/DeferredBoundary.tsx` wraps each deferred piece: the viewers keep their idle face, the panels draw nothing, and the mask painter shows its shell with "Could not load the mask painter" and a working Close (the loading shell has the painter's Close too now). `tests/components/DeferredLoadFailure.test.tsx` fails without it.
- **Numbers after the review:** entry 472,693 raw / 136,915 gzip (39,307 under the limit; main 510,678 / 147,182). The review's additions in the entry: WorldPreviewFace 866, DeferredBoundary 282, worldCard 183, the earth icon 329, the painter shell about 570.

## 2026-10-20 — First-load headroom: six pieces moved out of the startup entry

`scripts/check-build-budget.mjs` caps the startup entry (`assets/index-*.js`) at 512,000 bytes raw / 160,000 gzip. Main (a3694264) was at 510,678 raw / 147,182 gzip, so any PR adding first-load code failed CI (#99 hit 517,346). This branch moves code that the first paint never draws out of the entry with dynamic `import()`. It does not raise the limit.

- **Why not raise the limit:** the budget is the guard on first-paint parse cost. Raising it fixes nothing and makes the same failure come back with the next feature. These pieces only draw after a click, a wire drop or a run output, so they never belonged in the entry.
- **What moved** (all registered in `src/lib/deferredChunks.ts`):
  - `RunHistoryPanel` (App.tsx), `OnboardingOverlay` (App.tsx), `ConnectionPopup` (Canvas.tsx, import line only): mounted the first time they open (`components/DeferredPanels.tsx`), then kept mounted, so exit animations, focus return and Escape work as before. Fallback: nothing, which is what the closed panel draws anyway.
  - `MaskPainterModal` (Inspector.tsx): same wrapper; fallback is the painter's own overlay and header with "Loading the mask painter…". Preloaded on hover/focus of Paint Mask, and on idle.
  - `MeshPreview` (ModelNode, DynamicNode, create-studio OutputRenderer) and `WorldPreview` (RepresentationViewer): `components/nodes/DeferredViewers.tsx`. Each fallback is the idle card the viewer draws first (same classes, same min-height, the same absolutely placed layers; the mesh HUD label comes from the new shared `lib/meshFormat.ts`), so a node card keeps its height.
- **Preload choice:** App runs one idle task after the first frame (`whenIdle` in `lib/lazyWithPreload.ts`: rAF, then a timer, then `requestIdleCallback`, 2 s cap) that fetches all six chunks (about 48 kB raw together). `lazyWithPreload` hands React a synchronous thenable once a chunk is in, so after the preload nothing suspends and no fallback renders. Chosen over intent-only preloading because Run History, the tour and the popup also open from the command palette, onboarding steps and wire drops, and all of them must open on the first try.
- **Not moved, on purpose:** `JevResult` (11.2 kB) and `RepresentationViewer` (8.6 kB). Their height depends on the result (questions, bars, chips, asset lists), so no fallback can hold the box without rendering the content itself, and they appear with saved results at graph load, before an idle preload is guaranteed. `WorldPreview` was split out of `RepresentationViewer` instead. `lib/representationViewerRegistry.ts` and `lib/structuredValue.ts` are unchanged and stay static.
- **Numbers** (plain `vite build`, same toolchain): entry 510,678 → 470,716 raw (−39,962; 41,284 under the limit), 147,182 → 136,331 gzip (−10,851). Per module in the entry before → after (source-map attribution): WorldPreview 9,465 → 0, ConnectionPopup 7,557 → 0, RunHistoryPanel 6,624 → 0 (plus PaperRunInspection 2,192 and BatchRunInspection 1,150, which only it uses), MeshPreview 6,331 → 0, OnboardingOverlay 5,864 → 0, MaskPainterModal 4,385 → 0, worldDownload 2,622 → 1,437, four lucide icons ~1.2 kB. Added to the entry: lazyWithPreload about 1.9 kB (with the after-paint idle helper), DeferredViewers 1,573, DeferredPanels 961, deferredChunks 803, meshFormat 327. New chunks (raw / gzip): RunHistoryPanel 10,410 / 3,544, WorldPreview 11,790 / 4,125, ConnectionPopup 7,961 / 2,995, MeshPreview 7,128 / 2,932, OnboardingOverlay 6,182 / 2,300, MaskPainterModal 4,913 / 2,004. `run-history.css` and `onboarding.css` moved into their chunks' CSS (no class from them is used elsewhere; Vite loads the CSS before the module resolves).
- **Guard:** `tests/entrySplit.test.ts` walks the static import graph from `src/main.tsx` with the TypeScript parser (`import type` erased, `import()` a split point, `import { type X }` counted as an edge because verbatimModuleSyntax keeps it) and fails with the importer chain if any `DEFERRED_MODULES` entry is reachable. Checked by adding `import '../components/nodes/WorldPreview'` to structuredValue.ts: it failed with `main.tsx -> App.tsx -> … -> lib/structuredValue.ts -> components/nodes/WorldPreview.tsx`.
- **Live check** (production build, `vite preview` on 5787, isolated backend 8787, dead proxy + canary, CDP block on 8000-8010/5173): chunks are fetched after the first frame. With the viewer chunks held for 6 s, both nodes showed the fallback and kept their exact heights when the viewers arrived (mesh node 344 px / viewer 172, world node 430 / 168, before and after). Run History clicked while its chunk was held opened when the chunk arrived (first click). The tour opened from the keyboard with focus on Take the tour, and Escape returned focus to the Help button. A wire drop opened the connection popup with its search focused, and Escape closed it. Paint Mask opened the real painter.
- **Surprise:** navigating the harness page away from the app hangs Puppeteer on the unsaved-work `beforeunload` prompt (projectStore). Open a new tab instead of navigating away.
- **2026-10-20, a failed chunk retries without a reload.** React.lazy keeps a rejection for good, so after the web build was replaced under an open tab (or a fetch failed offline) a piece came back only after a full reload. Now:
  - *`lib/lazyWithPreload.ts`.* The returned component renders the current `lazy()` instance, and a new load attempt replaces an instance that holds a rejection. The swap happens when an attempt starts, not on the rejection: the first version swapped in the rejection handler, and since React re-renders the suspended piece right after a rejection, every re-render fetched again (an infinite loop the old failure tests caught by timing out). New `retry(trigger)`, `failures()`, `isLoaded()`, `subscribe()`, and `isChunkLoadError()` (load errors are tagged in a WeakSet). Focus and mount retries are skipped while `navigator.onLine` is false, and focus retries are at most one per `FOCUS_RETRY_GAP_MS` (10 s) per chunk. Concurrent retries share one fetch. The sync thenable after a load is unchanged, so nothing suspends after a preload.
  - *`components/DeferredBoundary.tsx`.* Takes the `chunk`. While failed it makes one attempt per trigger: a new `retryKey` (each open), `retry` from `failed` (a render prop), a new mount that meets a failure from before it mounted (the next Paint Mask), window `online`, window `focus`. It clears its error only once the chunk is in, from its own attempt or any other (the idle preload, the Paint Mask hover, another card with the same viewer), so recovery renders with no loading fallback. A failed attempt changes nothing and schedules nothing. An error thrown by the loaded component is not retried, since a retry would loop.
  - *`components/DeferredPanels.tsx`.* Run History, the tour and the connection popup pass an open count as `retryKey`, and a failed load closes them again (`onChunkError`): Run History toggles off, the tour sets `onboardingActive` false without marking it done, the popup hides. *Judgment call:* without the close, the rail's next click toggles off a dock that draws nothing, so the user would need two clicks. The mask painter's failed shell now says "Could not load the mask painter. Check your connection and try again." with Close and Try again ("Trying again…" while in flight) in the painter's own toolbar classes.
  - *Tests.* New `tests/components/DeferredRetry.test.tsx` (11: online, focus, intent key, fresh mount, no fallback flash, two pieces with one fetch, recovery from another preload, one fetch per trigger, spaced focus, offline focus and remount, no retry of a render error) and `DeferredRetryPanels.test.tsx` (6, with `deferredChunks` mocked to stubs behind a loader that fails N times: Run History's next toggle, the tour's next start, the next wire drop, Paint Mask remount and Try again, a mesh card via `online`, a World card via focus). Before the fix 16 of the 17 failed; the render-error guard passed, as it should. `DeferredLoadFailure.test.tsx` now checks both Close buttons and Try again.
  - *Size.* Entry 472,771 → 475,864 raw (+3,093), 136,941 → 138,023 gzip (+1,082); 36,136 under the limit.
- **2026-10-20, adversarial review of the retry: in Chromium it fetched nothing.**
  - *Surprise.* Chromium keeps a failed dynamic import in its module map: a second `import()` of the same URL rejects at once with no request. Checked in headless Chrome 147 and 150 for offline (CDP), an aborted request and an HTTP 503 (whatwg/html#6768 only changed the spec in July 2026). Vite's preload helper also skips a stylesheet it already tried. So calling the same loader again, which is all the retry did, could never recover in Chrome or the Electron app; the unit tests passed because their loaders were mocks. In a Vite harness built from this branch's `lazyWithPreload` and `DeferredBoundary` (chunk JS and CSS aborted on the idle preload, then the network back), the earlier version showed Failed after three opens with zero requests.
  - *Fix (`lib/lazyWithPreload.ts`).* An attempt after a failure first adds again any stylesheet a failed attempt named ("Unable to preload CSS for …", from Vite), then calls the loader, and if that rejects naming the chunk URL ("…dynamically imported module: URL", Chromium and Firefox) imports the chunk once from that URL with a fresh `?retry=` query. Only same-origin URLs. Safari names no URL and refetches anyway, so it gets the plain loader. At most one extra request per attempt, none on the first failure. Same harness after the fix: the first open renders the piece with its CSS applied, one request each for the JS and CSS. A redeploy that deleted the old chunk still fails (404 on the fresh URL too); only a reload helps there.
  - *Loops found and closed.* (1) A loaded piece rendering another deferred piece without its own boundary: the outer boundary took the inner load error for its own, saw its chunk loaded, recovered, caught it again: "Maximum update depth exceeded". Load errors now carry their chunk and a boundary only retries its own. (2) A caller that preloads again inside a failed preload's `catch` started the next attempt before the failed lazy instance was marked, so the boundary later drew the stale rejected instance in a loop. The instance is now marked in the attempt's own rejection handler (before any other caller runs), and the wrapper never draws a failed instance once the chunk is in.
  - *Other fixes.* StrictMode's replayed mount removed the boundary's listeners in development (it now re-listens on mount while waiting). A retry that failed too left Run History marked open with nothing drawn; `onChunkError` now runs on a failed retry as well. The painter's Try again uses `aria-disabled` while trying, since a disabled button drops keyboard focus to the page.
  - *Size.* Entry 475,864 → 477,132 raw (+1,268), 138,023 → 138,493 gzip (+470); 34,868 under the 512,000 limit.
  - *Tests.* `tests/components/DeferredRetryHardening.test.tsx` (7) and `DeferredRetryPanelsRepeat.test.tsx` (2, own file so its chunks start unloaded). 8 of the 9 failed against the earlier version (checked by reversing the patch); the ninth, the same-origin guard, passed there because nothing was refetched at all.
- **2026-10-20, merging main after #104 (the Agent log).** #104 made the Agent log a deferred piece too, behind `DeferredBoundary` with no `chunk`. Here `chunk` is required, so the log passes `DeferredAgentLog`. It has no open to retry on, so a failed chunk comes back on `online` or window focus. New test in `DeferredRetryPanels.test.tsx`; it fails without the `chunk`.

## 2026-10-20 — Board strength 0 turns the whole board off (Q36 a), and Q37 a in the plan

Branch `feat/moodboard-strength-zero-off` (from origin/main `38f9fa3a`, PR13a merged as #96). Justin's answers, relayed by GM - Design: Q36 a ("Strength 0 turns the whole board off for that node, text included. The run note becomes "Board strength is 0: board not sent". For images off with text on, use the node's existing "Send board images" switch.") and Q37 a ("Always ask, in the bar").

- **What.**
  - *One drop, before the fold.* `services/moodboard_brief.py`: `BOARD_STRENGTH_ZERO_NOTE` (moved here from `handlers/krea.py`, new wording), `board_is_off` and `_without_off_boards`, called first in `apply_to_generator`. A strength-0 bundle leaves the `moodboard` input before anything reads it, so no brief, Avoid, negatives or images reach any node, Krea 2 included (its handler gets the input after the drop). The port goes when no bundle is left, so the node runs exactly as with no board. A second board on the same input still goes.
  - *The note reaches the run.* `apply_to_generator` ran outside the handler's `execution_notes` context, so `add_run_note` there was a no-op. `engine.py` now sets the context around the call (`board_notes`) and seeds `run_notes` with it, so the note is on the executed event and in the cache entry.
  - *Cache replay.* With the board off, the request equals the no-board request, so the cache key can match an entry a run without the board left, whose notes don't say it. The replay adds `board_notes` in front of the stored ones. `test_a_cache_hit_still_says_the_board_was_not_sent` fails without that line (checked by reverting it). The cache entry stores only the handler's notes (`run_notes[len(board_notes):]`): the review found that storing `board_notes` too made a later run with the board unwired replay "Board strength is 0: board not sent" with no board in the graph (`test_a_cache_hit_without_the_board_does_not_say_it`, failed first).
  - *`nebula moodboard show` at strength 0* (review): it said "Brief sent to generators" for a board that now sends nothing. It now heads the brief "Brief (generated), not sent: board strength is 0, …" (`cli/commands/moodboard.py`, `board_is_off`), `set --strength`'s help says 0 turns the board off, and `moodboard_get`'s MCP description says so (`test_show_says_a_board_at_strength_zero_sends_nothing`, failed first).
  - *Krea 2's own check stays as a guard* for a direct call, with the shared note.
  - *Studio.* The strength slider at 0 reads "Strength 0.00 · board off: wired nodes get none of it"; above 0 it keeps PR13a's copy.
  - *Docs.* Contract 02 §7a (a "Strength 0" step and changelog row), contract 07 §1.4 (the rule, the outputs, the slider), §1.11 (notes go nowhere at 0) and changelog; `docs/MCP-SETUP.md`; `skills/nebula/SKILL.md`; `.agents/skills/krea/SKILL.md`; the plan (header, §5.6.2, §5.7.3 step 1, §5.7.4, §5.7.8, PR10c, PR13a, PR14, §7, §7.5, §9, §10.7, Not verified).
- **Decisions not in the spec.**
  - *The Moodboard node's own outputs don't change at 0 (judgment call).* Q36 says "off for that node", and the plan's step 1 drops the bundle at a generator's Moodboard input. Wiring the Brief, Negative, Palette or Images output into something is the person's explicit choice, like typing the text; emptying them would also blank what an LLM node reads off the Any port. The bundle keeps its `strength`, which is what the drop reads. If Justin wants 0 to empty those outputs too, it is a few lines in `handlers/moodboard.py`.
  - *A missing or unreadable `strength` is on (0.7),* as Krea 2's `_float_value` reads it. A bool is treated as unreadable, not as 0/1. Negative values are off.
  - *One note per node,* however many boards are off (`add_run_note` dedupes by text).
  - *"Send board images" doesn't exist yet.* `_boardImages` is PR14 (§5.7.8). On main every content-slot node is already images off, text on, so `test_board_images_off_still_sends_the_text` pins that path on GPT Image edit; PR14's test list gains the `_boardImages: "off"` case.
  - *Q37 a needs no code now.* It confirms PR10c's design; only the plan changed.
- **Tests.** New `backend/tests/test_moodboard_strength_zero.py` (20 after review): strength 0 on GPT Image, Nano Banana, FLUX.2, SDXL and Krea 2 sends no text, Avoid, negatives or port, with the note; 0.01 still sends; no strength key still sends; two boards; images off with text on; the engine end to end with Krea 2's real handler on mocked HTTP (no `image_style_references`, no uploads, the note on all five nodes, none on the Moodboard node); the Moodboard node's outputs at 0; the cache replay. On main, 12 of the 20 fail (the note, the five strength-0 cases, the three two-board cases, the engine case and both cache cases; rechecked in review by reverse-applying the code diff); the other 8 pin behaviour that must not move. `tests/test_moodboard_cli.py` gains the strength-0 `show` case. `test_board_strength_zero_sends_no_board_refs` now expects the new note. The golden file is unchanged. Frontend: one new case in `MoodboardStudioView.test.tsx`, failed first; only that file was run, not the full suite.
- **Size.** About 70 lines of code and 290 of tests, against the plan's booked 50 and 100 (inside PR13a's row; no total moves).

## 2026-10-20 — Moodboard clash reasons quote whole words; image counts name the set-aside ones

Branch `fix/moodboard-clash-wording` (from origin/main 26572670). Two defects from the Thursday demo dry run (shots 06 and 14).

- **What.**
  - *Clash reasons (`services/moodboard_colour_words.py`, `LEXICON_VERSION` 2 → 3).* For "Warm late-summer light for a sunscreen campaign: soft, sun-faded, optimistic" four colours read "Direction: sun-faded. The Direction allows Warm for the late, but this one is more saturated." `_allows` built "allows <term> for the <first noun>", and the first noun of "late-summer" was its first half (a hyphenated word that isn't in the lexicon became one noun item per part). It now quotes the Direction's own words through the allowance's noun phrase (`_noun_end`: the nouns after the first, and "light" or another modifier that leads to no colour), and a list item that takes its head's noun adds "in the <noun phrase>", lower-cased when only a sentence start capitalised it. The two sentences: "Direction: sun-faded. This color is more saturated than that, though the Direction also asks for “Warm late-summer light”." and "Avoid: blue flowers. The Direction also asks for “cornflower blue”, so it may clash."
  - *Three more bugs the table of Directions found, all fixed in the same module.* (1) Words were `[A-Za-z]+`, so "café" read "caf" and "19th-century" read "th-century": a reason could quote "for the caf". Words are now any letters and digits. (2) A second "no" in one clause moved the first one's start, so "no blue glass, no red flowers" gave the blue the reason "Direction: " with nothing after it; each item now keeps its own negation start. (3) A Direction exclusion stopped at its first noun, so "without blue-tinted glass" was quoted "without blue-tinted"; it now runs to the end of the noun phrase.
  - *Quotes never hold half a bracket or quotation mark.* `_quote` takes the longest run of words around the colour with only spaces between them (a list's commas and "and" count as words); `_tidy` drops a bracket or quotation mark a clause's span cut in half. A quote longer than 80 characters falls back to the colour's own words.
  - *Set-aside count.* `frontend/src/lib/moodboardCount.ts` (new): `isSetAside` (moved from `steering.ts`, which re-exports it), `setAsideCount`, `moodboardImagesLabel` ("5 images · 1 set aside", "1 image"). The Moodboard node card, the Studio's left list and the Assets panel read "5 images · 1 set aside · look"; `storedAssetsStore`'s summary carries `setAsideCount`, and the Assets panel's Add and drag pass it so a new card starts right. `nebula moodboard list` reads "(5 images, 1 set aside, look, ...)".
  - *Docs.* Contract 07 (the check's `reason` wording; the counts beside 1.3a's CLI paragraph), `docs/MCP-SETUP.md` and `skills/nebula/SKILL.md` (set-aside paragraphs).
- **Decisions not in the brief.**
  - *The lexicon version moved, so every saved check runs again.* `current_colour_check` returns a saved check whose basis matches, and the basis hashes `LEXICON_VERSION`; without the bump every board analyzed before this (Justin's demo board included) would keep its "Warm for the late" reasons until its Direction or colours changed. Startup refreshes stale checks (contract 07). The golden file moved only `colorCheck.basis` and `colorCheck.checks.words.version` on its 7 boards (scripted diff; no old board clashes, so every finding list is still empty), listed in the golden test's docstring. Its rule is "fix the change, not expected.json", but the bump is this change's point, and the docstring keeps a list of deliberate moves for this case.
  - *"asks for", not "allows".* A Direction is what the person wants; "allows" read as a permission rule. "This color is more saturated than that" names what the ceiling words ("sun-faded") rule out before saying why it's only a warning.
  - *The quote keeps the person's capitals* ("“Warm late-summer light”", "“WARM LATE-SUMMER LIGHT”"); only the "in the <noun>" part is lower-cased, and only a sentence-start capital.
  - *The count includes set-aside images and names them*, as the Studio's "Images (5)" does; weight 0 counts as set aside (Studio rule). The Preview still counts what the run sent ("4 images"), which leaves out switched-aside images but keeps weight-0 ones (the handler filters `excluded` only), so with a weight-0 image the card reads "5 images · 1 set aside" and the Preview "5 images". Left as it is: the Preview reports the bundle.
  - *`isSetAside` reads an image with no weight as full weight* (the backend's `steers` default), so a loosely shaped image (`{}` in old tests, an agent-written board) isn't counted as set aside. Studio images always carry a weight, so the Studio is unchanged.
  - *No Settings change.* Settings > Preferences > Agent spending > "Connect your agent" untouched.
- **Live check (isolated backend 8792, Vite 5792, Puppeteer 1440x900, real stdio MCP client as claude-code; CDP blocks 8000-8010 and 5173, dead proxy, canary 8781 with 0 hits, 0 blocked attempts during the run).** The demo's 5 images and Direction through `moodboard_create`/`moodboard_update`/`moodboard_analyze`: Left out #640c5a and #0f2875 ("Avoid: harsh magenta · Direction: sun-faded"), May clash #f7b550, #f7c762, #f69c7a, #faad63 with the new sentence. With #4 set aside, an added Avoid "red-orange flowers" and Keep anyway on #eb5e40, the Studio's Left out, Kept anyway and May clash rows and the Preview Inspector's "Why these are left out" / "Why these may clash" rows all read the new sentences. The card read "5 images · 1 set aside · look" on one line (142 of 180 px in Inter at 11 px) beside the Preview's "4 images"; the Studio rail read the same. Using #4 again in the Studio changed the rail and the card to "5 images · look"; Claude setting it aside again over MCP changed the card back without a reload. Screenshots: scratchpad `wording-check/shots/` (kept for the demo prep; the harness and its temp state were deleted).
- **Review (same day).** `_as_place` found the head's noun with `text.find(phrase)`, so the same words earlier in the Direction decided its capital: "Garden Flowers everywhere. Flowers: cornflower blue" read "in the Flowers", and "Flowers. Bright Flowers: ..." lower-cased a mid-sentence capital. It now reads the text right before the noun's own position, and a line break counts as a sentence start. Test: `test_an_inherited_noun_reads_its_own_capital` (3 cases, all failed before). Re-ran the dry run (8792/5792, real stdio MCP client): card and rail "5 images · 1 set aside · look" beside the Preview's "4 images", live through MCP set-aside, use-again and weight 0 ("2 set aside", one line); Studio Left out, Kept anyway, May clash and the Preview Inspector rows read the new sentences.
- **Surprises.** The "Faded palette" + "warm café" case shows the old regex bug could quote a word fragment for any non-English Direction, not only hyphenated ones.
- **Follow-up (2026-10-20, PR #100 review items).**
  - *Weight 0 in the Preview.* The plan says weight 0 is set aside (§4.4: "Set aside = `excluded || weight == 0`"; `steers` needs weight > 0; §5.7.4's candidates and PR13a's test: "weight 0 and set-aside images are still never sent"). What each generator gets today for a weight-0 image: Krea 2 skips it (`handlers/krea.py` `_collect_native_moodboard_style_references`, `weight <= 0: continue`, before `native_strengths`); `representativeImages` and the `representative_images` port leave it out (`rank_representative_images`); GPT Image, Nano Banana and FLUX get only the brief text (no board images until PR14), and the brief's palette, accents and cues come from steering images only. So no generator gets it. The bundle itself still lists it in `images` and `analysis.images` (with its colours) and counts it in `analysis.summary` ("4 reference image(s)"), as PR2 built on purpose to keep the golden file. The Preview counted the bundle's `images` less switched-aside ones, so a weight-0 image read "5 images · 1 set aside" on the card and "5 images" in the Preview, and its thumbnail showed. `lib/moodboardBundle.ts` `parseMoodboardBundle` now leaves out every image `isSetAside` names (and a stale representative hint naming one), so the Preview counts and draws the images that steer: card "5 images · 2 set aside", Preview "3 images". ## 2026-10-20 — Unmocked requests now fail their test; applyProject supersedes a params stop

Third pass over `fix/autosave-test-flake` (still uncommitted). Before it, `tests/setup.ts` refused loopback requests quietly, which hid tests that forgot a mock. (Justin's dev backend log showed earlier full runs had sent about 100 `PUT /api/settings` and 12 `POST /api/projects/recover` to his Nebula on :8000.)

- **`tests/setup.ts`: an unmocked request fails the test that sent it.** The setup fetch still refuses any request to localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] (a relative URL too) at once, with a `TypeError` naming the method and URL, so nothing reaches the network. It also records the request with `expect.getState().currentTestName`. An `afterEach` in setup throws `N unmocked request(s) to a local server by the end of this test (refused, never sent):` with one `METHOD URL` line each, and that fails the current test. An `afterAll` catches requests sent after a file's last test. A request recorded in another test, or between tests, is labeled with where it was sent. A probe file (deleted afterwards) checked the cases: `apiFetch`, a relative `POST`, a test that stubs fetch with `vi.stubGlobal` (passes), and a timer that fires in the next test (fails that test, the one running when the request was sent). Tests that stub fetch themselves replace this fetch and are unaffected.
- **Mocks added, each in its file's own idiom.** None of these tests relied on the request failing (each passes with a success answer), so no assertion changed.
  - `App.workspaceNavigation` and `App.canvasFocus`: the mocked `getSettings` answers `runCostConfirmUsd: 1` (a backend that already holds the threshold, so `applySavedRunCostConfirm` sends no migration `PUT`). `beforeEach` sets `usePricingStore` to a loaded empty table, so `load()` sends no `GET /api/pricing`.
  - `InspectorParams`: `fetchCharacters: vi.fn(async () => [])` in the api mock (the character node's `StoredAssetPicker`).
  - `MoodboardStudioAnalysis`: `vi.mock('../../src/lib/trash')` with `fetchTrash` from the hoisted `api` (the Studio's Recently deleted list).
  - Whole suite after: 0 unmocked requests. A throwaway run that also refused every non-loopback fetch found only Spark's wasm init (`tests/lib/worldSplat.test.ts`), which fetches a `data:application/wasm` URL, never the network.
- **`applyProject` supersedes a params stop (the reviewer's leftover race).** Loading a project now does what Retry does: when not `reloadingForParams`, it clears `paramsVersionChange` and bumps `paramsHandling`, so a stop whose recovered copy is still unanswered can't put its error, `dirty: false`, relabel or reload onto the loaded tab. It also clears `pendingRecovery`. Reached by: a params stop, then the backend restarts at a matching version, then an agent switches projects and the tab follows (`followProjectSwitch` → `loadWorkspace` → `applyProject`).
  - *Why clear `pendingRecovery`:* every way into `applyProject` with a copy still pending has already saved that canvas. `followProjectSwitch` saves it to the project it came from, or recovers it as a new copy. `initialize` loads only after `recoverPendingWork` succeeded, and `activate` needs `initialized`, which a pending copy never has. Left in place, the copy was the old canvas: the next params stop on the new project skipped capturing (`if (!pendingRecovery)`) and sent that old canvas instead of the new edits.
  - *Why clear `paramsVersionChange`:* the superseded promise would otherwise swallow every later version change (`if (paramsVersionChange) return it`).
  - *Also covered:* a matching activation answer that lands after a mid-`activate` stop now wins over that stop. Latest answer wins.
- **Tests (`tests/paramsVersionReload.test.ts`, "a params stop that an agent switch already moved past", 3).** Late failure: no error on the working tab. Late success: no reload, no `dirty: false`, and edits save to the new project. A later params change still stops the tab and sends the new project's edit. Without the change all 3 fail ("couldn't be saved as a recovered project yet (the backend restarted)" on the working tab). With only the counter, the third fails. With only `pendingRecovery` cleared, all 3 fail. The late success's `lastSaved` write can't do harm on this path: the old canvas's `createSessionId` (`project:alpha:create`) never matches the new project's, so no assertion pretends to catch it.
- **Checks.** Full frontend suite twice in a row: 265 files / 3316 tests, both exit 0, 0 unmocked requests. `tsc -b` exit 0. `npm run lint` exit 0. Nothing touched :8000-8010, :5173, tmux or the main checkout.

## 2026-10-20 — Autosave test flake: a real request to :8000 answered into the next test, plus a Retry race

Branch `fix/autosave-test-flake` (from origin/main cb3bf987). The flake: in a full run, `projectStore.autosave.test.ts` "shows the retry state when a save fails, and Retry saves it" got "Nebula was updated while this tab was open. Your unsaved edits couldn't be saved as a recovered project yet (Invalid project ID)..." instead of "Disk full".

- **Root cause (test isolation, with a live-backend side effect).**
  - *The previous test no longer tested what it says.* "stops after an in-flight save when another window takes over the project" sends `graphSync` with `workspaceRevision: 'r2'` and no `paramsVersion`. Since 26bb962b (2026-10-17, a sync without a version is a backend from before the gate, version 0), that sync takes the params-version path (`handleParamsVersionChange(0)`), not the "another window" conflict the test was written for on 2026-10-16. It still passed because its assertions hold on both paths.
  - *That path sent a real request.* The file didn't mock `recoverProject`, and in test mode `apiFetch` goes to `http://localhost:8000`: every run POSTed `/api/projects/recover` (source `p1`) to whatever runs there, a developer's own Nebula included. The backend refused it (`validate_project_id` → "Invalid project ID", so nothing was written), and that answer arrived on real I/O time, outside fake timers. On an idle machine it landed inside test 4; on a busy one after test 5's save had failed, overwriting `error` ('Disk full') with the params message. `pendingRecovery` and `paramsVersionChange` also stayed set across tests (no module reset; `resetParamsVersionChangeForTests` existed but only `paramsVersionReload.test.ts` called it).
  - *Wider:* a loopback-logging fetch in `tests/setup.ts` over the whole suite found 32 unmocked requests to :8000 in five files: `App.workspaceNavigation` and `App.canvasFocus` (14 `GET /api/pricing`, 14 `PUT /api/settings` `{"runCostConfirmUsd":1}`, refused by `require_person` on a real backend), `MoodboardStudioAnalysis` (2 `GET /api/trash`), `InspectorParams` (1 `GET /api/characters`), and this one.
- **Fixes.**
  - *Test 4* sends the sync at `GRAPH_PARAMS_VERSION`, so it takes the conflict path again; it now asserts the "another window" error and that no recovered copy is sent before Try again.
  - *`resetProjectStoreForTests()`* (replaces `resetParamsVersionChangeForTests`) resets all module state: `initializing`, `saveQueue`, `saveTimer`, `lastSaved`, `applying`, `projectViewport`, `pendingRecovery`, `canvasParamsVersion`, `paramsVersionChange`, `reloadingForParams`, and supersedes any params handling in flight (below), so a late answer from an earlier test writes nothing. The autosave file calls it first in `beforeEach` and mocks `recoverProject`; `paramsVersionReload.test.ts` uses the new name.
  - *`tests/setup.ts` fails loopback requests at once* (`TypeError: fetch failed: tests never reach a local server (...)`), as on a machine with no backend; tests that stub fetch replace it. Chosen over failing the test loudly, which would have meant fixing the four other files here (out of scope; listed above for a follow-up: they should mock pricing, settings, trash and characters).
- **Real race found on the way, fixed (`projectStore.ts`).** A params stop shows its error (with Try again) before its recovered copy is answered. If the person restarts the backend and clicks Try again, Retry sends the same copy again and loads the project; the first request's late answer then (a) on failure, put "couldn't be saved as a recovered project yet" on the working tab, (b) on success, set `dirty: false` (no leave-page prompt for edits made since), said "frontend is newer ... Restart the backend" on a working tab, or reloaded it, and (c) set `lastSaved` to the old canvas, so going back to exactly that content was never saved (silent loss). Fix: a `paramsHandling` counter; Retry (and the test reset) bumps it, and a superseded handling returns after its await without writing. `recoverPendingWork` only clears `pendingRecovery` and sets `lastSaved` when its recovery is still the pending one (another send already finished it otherwise). Tests: `tests/paramsVersionReload.test.ts` "a params stop that Retry already moved past" (2): both failed before the fix (the wrong error; `dirty: false` and the "newer frontend" error), and the `lastSaved` assertion still failed with only the counter in.
- **Proof.** Reproduction (session scratchpad `make_repro.py`): the test file with `recoverProject` as a deferred and fetch blocked, rejected with "Invalid project ID" after test 5's save fails. Main's test file on main's store: fails 5 of 5 with the exact reported message. The fixed test file with test 4 forced back to the version-less sync (so a handling is left in flight) on the fixed store: 5 of 5 pass. Then the autosave and params files together, 50 runs in a row with `--sequence.shuffle --sequence.seed=1..50` under 8 extra busy loops (load 44 on 18 cores): 50 of 50. Full suite 265 files / 3313 tests, `tsc -b`, `npm run lint`: clean. No request reached :8000 in any of this (fetch blocked or mocked before any run of the old file).

## 2026-10-20 — PR13a review fixes: light strengths in the note, replay line through reroutes, a behaviour stamp instead of a date

Three low findings from the PR13a review, all confirmed and fixed.

- **A light image read as 0.00 in the run note.** Nine cards at 1.0 and one at the card minimum (0.05) send #10 at 0.0039, but the note said "#10 0.00". `handlers/krea.py` gains `_sent_strength_text`: 2 decimals as the plan's example has them, or the 4 decimals the request carries when 2 would read 0.00. Test: `test_a_light_image_that_went_never_reads_as_zero_in_the_note` (failed before the fix). *Not changed:* the 2-decimal values listed can still differ from the stated total by a cent or two (nine 0.0777s show as 0.08 each). That is rounding for display, the plan's chosen format; the request itself adds up exactly. Making the display add up would need a second apportionment at 2 decimals, which would put 0.00 back for light images.
- **No replay line for a board wired through a reroute or router.** The engine passes both through unchanged (`engine.py` `router`, `reroute`), so the replay does send the new strengths. `runReplayNotes` now walks back from Krea 2's `moodboard` port through `reroute`/`router` `input` edges to a `nebula-moodboard`, with a seen-set so a loop of reroutes ends. Tests: one reroute, router then reroute, a Krea moodboard through a reroute (no line), and a reroute loop.
- **The "before the change" cut-off was a calendar date.** Runs made on main between that date and the merge would have used the old strengths without getting the line. Every new run record now carries `behaviourVersion` (`RUN_BEHAVIOUR_VERSION = 1` in `savedParamsUpgrades.ts`, stamped in `openRunRecord`, kept through `loadRunHistory` when it's a non-negative integer, read through `runBehaviourVersion`; missing or malformed is 0). `runReplayNotes(snapshot, behaviourVersion)` gives the line when the stamp is below 1. This follows the `paramsVersion` pattern but doesn't touch `GRAPH_PARAMS_VERSION`, so nothing reloads and no recipe is upgraded. Project files store run records opaquely (`main.py` deep-copies `runHistory`), so the stamp survives there with no backend change. The date in the line ("changed 2026-10-20") is now copy only. *Worth a look at merge:* if this ships much later, change that string so the line reads right. Nothing depends on it. Tests: a new record is stamped; an unstamped record and one with a malformed stamp load without one; a replay of an unstamped record dated after 2026-10-20 still gets the line, and a stamped one doesn't.
- The isolation script handed to this lane (`scratchpad/iso.sh`) `cd`s into the `nebula_nodes-checked-edits` worktree, so it would have tested another branch. I ran a copy that differs only in that path (`scratchpad/iso-weights.sh`).

## 2026-10-20 — Moodboard canvas PR13a: Krea 2's board strengths add up to the board's strength (Q21 b, Q32 a)

Branch `feat/moodboard-weights-helper` (from origin/main 26572670). Spec: `docs/moodboard-canvas-plan.md` PR13a, sections 4.8 items 5 and 7, 5.7.2, 5.7.4 (native weights), Q21 and Q32.

  - *Helper.* New `backend/services/moodboard_weights.py`: `native_strengths(S, weights, *, normalize, range, precision)` returns `NativeStrengths(strengths, clamped)`. `sum-to-strength` is `S x w / sum(w)`, `sum-to-one` gives shares (for PR24), `none` is the raw `S x w` (fixtures only), and `rank` raises because it has no numbers. Rounding is 4 decimals by largest remainder, with ties to the earlier (heavier) image, so the sum is exactly `S` as a decimal. The clamp to `range` is only a guard, and `clamped` reports it. Negative values raise. `weight_view(weights)` gives `{w, share, rel}` for the planner (PR15) and the legend words.
  - *Krea handler.* `_collect_native_moodboard_style_references` picks first (hints, else bundle, else ranked; deduped; capped at `remaining_slots`), then scales each board's picked images with the helper, then resolves URLs. Only images that go get uploaded. A board at strength 0 is skipped with the note "Board strength is 0: no board images sent" (Justin's wording) and takes no slots. An image whose share rounds to 0 is left out ("Board 'X': #n is too light to steer at this board strength, so it wasn't sent."). The run note lists each image ("Board 'Dusk' sent 5 images; their strengths add up to the board's 0.70 (#1 0.19, ...)."). With wired references it adds "Your N references add T on top of the board's S.". The new `wired=` kwarg carries the person's references for that note. Their strengths, plus `styles` and Krea `moodboards`, are untouched. Both routes build the same body.
  - *Replay line (canvas).* `runReplayNotes(snapshot, startedAt)` and `KREA2_BOARD_STRENGTHS_REPLAY_NOTE` live in `frontend/src/lib/savedParamsUpgrades.ts` (still import-free). It gives the line "Krea 2 board strengths now add up to the board's strength (changed 2026-10-20), so this replay can differ from the original." to each `krea-2-generate` node that a `nebula-moodboard` feeds on its `moodboard` port, when the record started before the change. graphStore's `executed` handler looks up the replay's source record (`sourceRunId`) and puts the line after the backend's run notes, so it shows in the Inspector's run notes. No `GRAPH_PARAMS_VERSION` or `PARAMS_VERSION` bump.
  - *Studio copy.* The slider reads "Strength 0.70 · the total the board's images share on Krea 2".
  - *Golden file (deliberate).* Only `kreaStyleReferences` changed: 29 paths, every one a `[i].strength` on the 7 boards, with URLs and order unchanged. I rewrote it with a scratch script that recomputed that key alone, asserted the URLs matched and kept the file's format, then reviewed it path by path. There is a dated "Deliberate changes" entry in the docstring. `test_q21b_changed_only_the_krea_style_references` pins a sha256 of the pre-change file minus that key (canonical JSON) and checks that each board's refs add up to its strength. `prebrief_v2_plain` is now 0.1892, 0.1892, 0.1513, 0.1135, 0.0568 (the plan's "about 0.189, 0.189, 0.151, 0.114, 0.057").
  - *Docs.* `skills/nebula/SKILL.md` (weights/strength bullet), `.agents/skills/krea/SKILL.md` (Legacy Krea 2 moodboard port), contract 07 section 1.4 and its changelog, and the plan's open question about the backend seeing a record's date (answered, see below). I also changed one line in `.claude/skills/krea/SKILL.md`, the older copy, which said "default strength 0.7" for board refs.
- **Decisions not in the spec.**
  - *The backend can't see a replayed record's date, and there's no CLI or MCP replay to note.* Run records exist only in the canvas `runHistory`. The backend stores them in projects but never runs one. A canvas replay is a plain `POST /api/execute` with nodes and edges and no record, and neither the CLI nor MCP has a replay command. So the line is canvas-only. I recorded this in the plan's open questions.
  - *The line lives beside `upgradeRunSnapshot`, not inside it.* `upgradeRunSnapshot` returns a recipe and is also used by "Reuse settings" and Paper freshness, where a replay line doesn't belong. Changing what it returns would ripple through all three.
  - ~~*The change counts from the end of 2026-10-20 UTC.*~~ Superseded by the review fixes above: records carry a `behaviourVersion` stamp instead, so the merge date no longer matters.
  - *Scaling is per board.* With two Nebula boards wired (the port allows it), each board's images add up to that board's strength, after one shared slot cap and dedupe.
  - *A weight-0 image in a stale `providerHints` list is never sent.* Before this change it went at strength 0. That is a quiet change to old behaviour, but the golden boards' hints never held one, so the golden file shows no effect.
  - *No refill.* An image that rounds to 0 leaves its slot empty instead of pulling in the next candidate. It needs a weight ratio of about 1:14,000 at strength 0.7, so it shouldn't happen in practice.
  - *"#n" in notes is the board number.* That is `analysis.images[].number` by URL (set-aside images keep their place in it), or else the position in the bundle's images, or else the URL.
  - *The wired note counts only image references*: `style_images` plus `image_style_references`. Styles (−2..2) and Krea moodboards use different scales.
- **Existing tests changed on purpose.** `test_krea_handler.py`: 0.3/0.6 became 0.2/0.4, and 1.0/0.5 became 0.6667/0.3333. Also `test_moodboard_set_aside.py::test_krea_references_never_include_a_set_aside_image`: 0.56/0.35 became 0.4308/0.2692. The plan didn't list that one.
- **Tests first.** `tests/test_krea_board_strengths.py` (13 tests) failed on main: 12 on behaviour and 1 on the new `wired=` kwarg (I checked again with the kwarg passed only when set). `test_moodboard_weights.py` failed at import, the two golden checks failed, the Studio copy test failed, and 4 of the 6 in `tests/kreaBoardStrengthsReplay.test.ts` failed. The two that passed on main were "after the change: no line" and "no params bump". The mocked live check is `test_a_five_image_board_through_the_engine_sends_strengths_that_add_up`. It runs a real saved board with 5 local images through `execute_graph`, with uploads and generate mocked by respx: the body's strengths add up to 0.7 and the run note reaches the executed event. No paid call.

## 2026-10-20 — Moodboard canvas PR3: checked board edits, journal and live Studio

Branch `feat/moodboard-checked-edits`, stacked on `feat/moodboard-set-aside` (PR #92). Spec: `docs/moodboard-canvas-plan.md` v2.4 sections 5.1 to 5.3 and the PR3 section. As built: contract 07 section 1.12.

- **What.**
  - *Edits (`services/moodboard_edits.py`).* `POST /api/moodboards/{id}/edits` with `{ops, baseVersion?, say?}`: every op in 5.1 except `arrange`, `look.*`, the suggestion ops and `realPerson` (refused by name: "isn't in this version of Nebula"). Ops are staged on a copy, checked as they apply, and the store saves once with `version + 1` under a per-board lock (`moodboard_store.apply_edits`). Each batch answers `undo`: one `restore` built from the before/after diff (frame, image, settings and card slices, each with `expect`), so any batch, a `restore` too, has an inverse, and a slice changed since is skipped and reported. The same diff gives the broadcast's `touched` and the journal entry, for `PUT`s too.
  - *`baseVersion`* on `/edits` and `PUT`: 409 `{detail, code: version_conflict, version, board}`. `PUT` refuses layout keys with a 422 that names `/edits`.
  - *Broadcast.* `storedAssetChanged` adds `version`, `edit` (`_graph_edit_origin`), `touched`, `undo` (null for a `PUT` or a batch over 200 ops). Keep and Analyze send `version` and `edit` with nothing touched.
  - *Journal.* `board.*` kinds in `EVENT_KINDS`; one event per write in the actor's name, first kind of added, removed, frame, grouped, setAside, resized, noted, moved; `data.kinds`, `refs`, board id/name/scope. No note text ever; a private note reads "private note changed".
  - *Clients.* `moodboard_client.edit_board` (409 in the client's words); `add_to_board` is one `add` op with `unique` (PUT fallback on an older backend) and returns a 4-tuple with the route's `undo`; `added_ids`. `moodboard_add` and `add --json` return `addedIds` and `undo`; the CLI prints the `set --remove` line.
  - *Studio.* `lib/moodboardEdits.ts`: op types, `queueOps`, `imagePatchOps`, `applyOps`, `fieldChanges`, `mergeFields`, `rebaseDraft`, `MoodboardVersionConflict`. `api.editMoodboard`; `updateMoodboard` throws the conflict on 409. The draft carries `pendingOps`, `base` (board fields as last read) and `version`. Image changes (weight, Set aside, notes, private note, add, remove) apply at once and queue; the autosave (600 ms, or blur on the text fields) sends the queue as one batch, then a `PUT` of only the changed board fields, both with `baseVersion`. A foreign `storedAssetChanged` (newer version, not this tab's) refetches and rebases; a 409 rebases and resends (three tries). Keep moves the draft onto the board it answers.
- **Decisions not in the spec.**
  - *The queue lives in the draft store entry*, not a separate store, so a kept draft (leaving and reopening the Studio) keeps its unconfirmed ops and base, and one `setDraft` changes images and queue together.
  - *Coalescing.* One op per (image, setting): typing a note queues one op, moved to the end so the latest order holds; adds and removes always stay.
  - *Rebase merges board fields three-way*: a field keeps the person's value when it differs from `base`, else takes the board's. After a successful save the person's sent fields keep the draft's value (not the server's normalized one), so a name being typed with a trailing space isn't trimmed under the cursor, and `base` takes those sent values too (see Review fixes).
  - *Set aside off on a weight-0 image sends only `setAside`*: the server sets the card's weight, the same rule the Studio applies locally.
  - *The analysis goes on `PUT` only as `null`*, and only when the person changed a steering board field; a steering op clears it on the server itself.
  - *A save in flight defers a foreign refetch*: the announced version is remembered and read once the save lands, so a rebase never races the save's own bookkeeping.
  - *Numbers in a batch name images as the board was before it*, so removing #2 and weighting #3 in one batch don't shift.
  - *`add` also takes `images` with ids and `unique`*; the Studio sends its own ids, so a replayed add is skipped, not doubled.
  - *Without this launch's person token the tab isn't trusted* (as on the graph), so the Studio can't tell its own echo by tab; it then reads the board once and drops it because the version isn't newer. One extra GET, no rebase.
  - *Departures from 5.1 are listed* in the worktree plan's "As built (PR3)" bullets (5.1 and 5.3).
- **Existing tests changed on purpose.** `test_asset_reference_params::test_moodboard_changes_reach_the_canvas` (the broadcast has new keys; checks a subset and the versions); `test_moodboard_board_model` and `test_moodboard_cli` unpack `add_to_board`'s 4-tuple. `MoodboardStudioView.test.tsx`: five tests asserted the whole-draft PUT (`body.images`, `body.analysis`); they now assert the ops sent to `editMoodboard`, the board-field-only PUT with `baseVersion`, and that the analysis isn't sent. The mock `editMoodboard` applies the ops with the real `applyOps`.

After a `PUT` (and a create), `base` now holds each sent field as the draft sent it; `fieldChanges` compares trimmed names on both sides. Chosen over normalizing in the client because the server's rules (avoid, pins, override stamping) would have to be copied.
  - *Queued ops on a removed image are dropped on rebase* (replayed in order, so an op on an image the queue itself adds stays). The server refuses a whole batch for one such op, and the Studio would have retried the same 422 forever.

If the `PUT` then fails, the error carries `previous` ("The image changes were saved"). Board fields then went without `baseVersion`; the next bullet closes that. `test_put_diffs_show_up_in_the_journal` now sends raw `PUT`s (an older client), and the CLI path has its own test, which now journals the image edit and the board-notes `PUT` as two events.

On a 409 it reads the board again (`get_board`; `NebulaAPIError` has no body) and builds the body again, at most `BOARD_WRITE_TRIES` (3) sends: values given outright go as given, list changes (`avoid_add`/`avoid_remove`, `pin_colors`/`keep_out_colors`/`unpin_colors`, `keep_anyway`/`leave_out`/`reset_colors`) go on the list as it is now. **The rule for one field written by both:** a field given outright (name, notes, mode, strength, direction, `avoid=`, `pinned_colors=`, clash mode, `color_choices=`, `send_notes`, the override) that someone else changed since the read, to anything but what this call sets, is never sent over theirs: the call stops with "<field> was changed by someone else after this call read the board, so it wasn't set. Nothing more was written: ... run the change again to set it over theirs" (plus `previous` and "The image changes were saved" when the batch already landed). Running it again reads their value and then wins: the later explicit write wins only through a fresh read. Chosen over "re-send it anyway and report it", because that still overwrites a value the caller never saw. Three 409s in a row: "The board kept changing while this ran (3 tries) ... Nothing more was written". `previous` now holds the board this write replaced (images still as read, before the call's own image ops), so undoing it never reverts the other writer's edit; before, it was the stale read. The code was already right (it rebases on the board the 409 carries rather than a separate GET; same board); the test fails with the rebase taken out and with sent ops left queued.

The Studio's new 409 test was checked to fail with the rebase removed (temp copy).

(2) Analyze saves with the `base_version` it read; on `VersionConflict` it keeps its analysis when `analysis_is_current` on the new board (a rename, a brief field) and analyses the new board again when not, at most `MOODBOARD_ANALYZE_TRIES` (3) saves, then `_moodboard_conflict`. Before, `previous` was replayed as `update_board(**previous)`, so a setting the call changed and someone changed again went back over theirs. Now `previous` also carries `undo`: one `restore` of the batch's own `undo` slices (settings, the cards the weight op rescaled, removed images whole) plus a `fields` slice for the fields the `PUT` changed (`before` as the board it replaced had them, `expect` as the `PUT` saved them, both read with `moodboard_edits.field_value`, which the client's `_field_value` now calls). `undo_board(api, ref, undo, fallback=)` sends it as one `/edits` batch and returns `(board, removed, previous, skipped)`, `skipped` being the route's plain messages; `update_board(undo=...)` delegates to it (so old callers' `update_board(**previous)` gets the checked undo, minus the report); `moodboard_update` takes `undo` and returns `skipped`; `set --restore` uses it when the file has `undo`, prints each skipped line, and `--json` adds `skipped`. **Server side, not client compare:** `restore` takes a `fields` slice (`FIELD_KEYS`: name, notes, mode, strength, the brief fields, clash mode, colour choices, sendNotes, the override as text), checked up front (a `before` a `PUT` would refuse is a 422), each field compared and set on its own through the new `moodboard_store.apply_fields` (the `PUT`'s own loop, extracted; `_update` calls it), applied last so an override is stamped on the board as it ends up. Image settings now go back one key at a time ("#1's weight changed since, left as is", `settings` names the keys), and an image whose settings were reported doesn't get a second report for its rescaled cards. `diff` adds a `fields` slice whenever board fields differ, so a restore of fields has an undo of its own; restoring mode, strength or notes clears the analysis (as the `PUT` does).
