  - *Review of the undo pass (2026-10-20).* Five fixes, each with a test that fails without it. (1) The client's `fields` slice now covers every field that differs between the board the `PUT` replaced and what it saved, not just the keys in its body: with `baseVersion` taken, all of that difference is this `PUT`'s, side effects included (a colour pinned out also leaves Keep anyway, so undoing the keep-out brings the Keep anyway back) — `test_undoing_a_keep_out_brings_back_the_keep_anyway_it_dropped`. (2) `_restore_fields` judges each field by the board as the restore found it, and a field whose going back would also change `colorChoices` (a pin back on drops a Keep anyway colour) is put back as it was and skipped ("The pinned colours would undo a colour choice made since, left as is") unless the same slice puts `colorChoices` back itself — `test_undoing_an_unpin_leaves_a_keep_anyway_chosen_since`. (3) A `restore`'s applied entry has `removed` (the image ids it took off), and `undo_board` reports `removed` URLs from that, so a redo whose image the person already took off doesn't say "Took … off" — `test_a_redo_reports_only_the_images_it_took_off`. (4) `moodboard_update` with `undo` refuses `remove`, `avoid_add`, `avoid_remove`, `pin_colors`, `keep_out_colors`, `unpin_colors`, `keep_brief`, `keep_anyway`, `leave_out`, `leave_out_flagged` and `reset_colors` beside it (nothing written), as `set --restore` does — `test_mcp_undo_refuses_a_second_change_beside_it`. (5) Test gap: `test_the_fields_go_back_last_so_a_brief_is_stamped_with_the_board_as_it_ends_up` fails if the `fields` slice runs first. **Left as is:** an agent's brief that goes back is stamped fresh (the slice holds only its text), so a "changed since you edited this" notice on the agent's own text is cleared by the undo; the person's brief is never touched.
  - *`restore` checks what it writes*: a slice's `before` must name its own image/frame/card, an image record needs a url, settings go through the op checks (weight 0 to 1, text notes, private note at most 2,000, bool switch); frames are already covered by the final `check_frames`. Unknown image keys are still allowed in a restored record, since the store keeps keys it doesn't know and an undo of such an image must still work. A `KeyError` inside a batch is now a 500 (RuntimeError), not "Moodboard not found".
  - *A frame a restore touched grows to hold its cards* (its rect slice applied, or a card or image of its members put back), rather than skipping the frame slice: the undo then does as much as it can and the frame still holds every card.
  - *Private-note text stays off CLI/MCP sockets*: an `undo` holding one (a settings slice naming `privateNote`, or an image record with a non-empty one) is sent whole by `broadcast_browser` and as `undo: null` by the new `ConnectionManager.broadcast_others`.
  - *Tests added:* backend `test_cli_set_keeps_an_edit_saved_between_its_read_and_its_write`, `test_cli_set_journals_its_image_changes_as_board_edits`, `test_a_restore_is_checked_like_the_ops`, `test_a_partial_restore_never_leaves_a_frame_smaller_than_its_cards`, `test_a_private_note_reaches_only_the_persons_tabs`, `test_a_bug_inside_a_batch_is_not_a_missing_board`; frontend three in `MoodboardStudioEdits.test.tsx` (a cleaned field still takes the next outside edit; a pending edit on a removed image is dropped; a save held in flight) and one `rebaseDraft` unit test. The fake server now trims name and Direction and refuses an op on a missing image. Each behaviour test failed with its fix taken out, except the in-flight one, which covers existing code.
- **Surprises.** The `board.*` kinds had to be in `EVENT_KINDS` or `publish` raised and the error was swallowed, so events silently vanished. `NebulaAPIError` has no body, so `edit_board` reads the version from the 409's detail. A weight change journals as `board.resized`, since the diff sees the cards scale.

## 2026-10-20 — Moodboard canvas PR2: one "Set aside" switch (C3, analysis version 5)

Branch `feat/moodboard-set-aside` (from origin/main 173d9289: #87 board model v2, #89, #90 brief precedence). Spec: `docs/moodboard-canvas-plan.md` section 4.4, C3, Q7 (yes), Q8, and the PR2 section.

- **What.**
  - *Analysis (version 5).* `excluded` keeps its key and its place in `source_hash`, and now means "read, never steers". A set-aside image is measured and listed in `analysis.images` with `setAside: true` and its colours; it adds nothing to the palette, accents, `sources`, keywords, summary, `styleBrief`, negatives, lighting, composition or representative images. `steers(weight)` became `steers(image)` (not excluded and weight > 0) for the roll-up, `rank_representative_images` and the cue inputs; `set_aside(image)` is the switch. The all-weight-0 warning became `ALL_SET_ASIDE_WARNING`, "Every reference is set aside, so none of them shapes the board.", and now also fires when every image is switched aside (before, such a board had no entries and no warning).
  - *Bundle.* `generator_analysis` drops `setAside` entries from `analysis.images`, so the node's bundle carries no set-aside image anywhere (its `images` already left them out); Krea 2's references come from `representativeImages` or the bundle images, so they never include one. The handler filters with `set_aside()` instead of reading `excluded` itself.
  - *CLI and MCP.* `brief()` gives every image `setAside` (`excluded` or weight 0). `nebula moodboard set --set-aside N` / `--use N`, with `--exclude` / `--include` as argparse aliases of the same options; one image in both is refused. `show` prints "set aside", or "set aside (weight 0)". `moodboard_update` image edits accept `setAside` as the same key as `excluded` (they must agree). Docstrings of `moodboard_get` and `moodboard_update`, and the INSTRUCTIONS moodboard paragraph, say what Set aside does.
  - *Studio.* The List view's "Exclude" is "Set aside" (with a tooltip, "Still read for its colors; never steers"); a tile dims (`moodboard-tile--set-aside`, was `--excluded`) when `isSetAside` (switch or weight 0) and its checkbox reads checked. `setAsidePatch` (in `steering.ts`): on sets `excluded: true` and keeps weight and card; off sets `excluded: false`, and for a weight-0 image also `weight: cardWeight(image)`.
  - *Docs.* Contract 07 sections 1.1 (`images[].excluded` row), 1.3a (version 5), 1.4 and 1.6, changelog; `skills/nebula/SKILL.md`; `docs/MCP-SETUP.md` moodboard section.
- **Decisions not in the spec.**
  - *`analysis.images[].setAside` marks the switch only, not weight 0.* The spec's Set aside is `excluded || weight == 0` for display, but the pinned "brand" board has a weight-0 image whose colours are in the pin's steering view, and its summary ("4 reference image(s)") counts it. Marking weight 0 too would have moved that entry out of the steering view and changed the summary of every board with a weight-0 image, against "byte-identical". So the analysis keeps weight 0 exactly as version 4 wrote it (entry, colours, counted in the summary), and only the new state gets the new key; the CLI/MCP view (`setAside` per image) and the Studio show both as set aside. "The summary leaves out set-aside images" is pinned for the switch; weight 0 still counts, with a comment saying why.
  - *A set-aside image that can't be read gets no board warning.* Its entry says `status: unresolved` / `error`; `warnings` stay those of the images that count. Otherwise an unreadable set-aside image (an external URL) would add "Could not resolve image" to the bundle's analysis and so to generator output.
  - *Turning the switch off on a weight-0 image takes its card weight in every client, not only the Studio.* `moodboard_client.update_board` does it for `--use`, `--include` and `excluded: false` / `setAside: false` when the same edit gives no weight (so `previous`, which always carries the weight, restores exactly). The card weight is the largest placement's `weight` (Q4: the board weight is the largest copy's), else 1 (a weight-0 card is laid out full size). The List view has the cards in its draft (`moodboardToDraft` keeps placements), so it uses the same rule; no List-view size is needed.
  - *`setAside` on a board image and in `analysis.images` are not the same set*, and every reader-facing description says so (the `moodboard_get` and `brief()` docstrings, SKILL.md, MCP-SETUP): the board view's `setAside` is "doesn't steer" (switch or weight 0); the analysis marks only the switch, and a weight-0 image keeps its ordinary entry (measured, in no colour's `sources`). Found in review: the docstrings first said the analysis lists every `setAside` image with the key.
  - *"Set aside and use the same image" is refused by the image, not by the text typed.* `update_board` resolves each edit to its image and refuses two edits that pull one image's switch both ways ("image N is both set aside and used in this change: pick one"), so `--set-aside 1 --use <id of 1>` and the same pair in `moodboard_update` fail with nothing written; the CLI's own string check stays as the early, cheap case. Found in review.
  - *`setAside` is accepted in `moodboard_update` edits* because agents now read `setAside` on every image; an agent writing it back would otherwise get "unknown image setting".
  - *The defaults pin fixture is unchanged, byte for byte.* `pinned_view` filters `setAside` entries; the new `test_set_aside_colours_match_the_pin` pins them in their own fixture (`moodboard_set_aside_pin.json`) and checks they equal the image's colours measured as if it steered.
- **Golden file (deliberate, reviewed with a scripted diff).** Exactly two kinds of change and nothing else: `setAside` on each image of the CLI's `brief()` view (7 true, 32 false), and `sourceHash.version` 4 → 5 for the never-analyzed `prebrief_unanalyzed` (that label is today's analyzer version; the hash is the same). Listed in the golden test's docstring.
- **Live check, run as a script instead of on Justin's app.** Every golden board and every pinned board, re-analyzed with origin/main's analyzer (an archive copy in the scratchpad) and with PR2's: the analysis (less `version` and the new `setAside` entries), `compose`, the node's bundle and outputs, Krea 2's style references and both generator prompts are identical; the three golden boards with an excluded image now list it with its colours (3, 3 and 4 colours).
- **Live check against running backends (isolated state, 2026-10-20).** A board was made and analyzed the old way on origin/main's backend (8795): four generated PNGs, gold `excluded`, violet weight 0. Then PR2's backend (8794) ran on the same state and re-analyzed it. Palette, accents, colours, `styleBrief`, negatives, summary, representative images, the composed brief, the node's outputs, Krea 2's references (teal 0.7, coral 0.42) and both generator prompts were byte-identical. The node's bundle differed only in `analysis.version` (4 to 5). `sourceHash` stayed `aab47bceb4c010b2`. Gold is now in `analysis.images` with `setAside: true` and `#d4af37`/`#5a1428`, and appears in no palette, `colors` or brief. In the Studio's List view (Puppeteer, 1440x900) both set-aside tiles were dimmed (opacity 0.48), their switches were checked and labelled "Set aside", and gold showed its colour swatches. Clicking the switches stored coral as `excluded` with its weight 0.6 kept, gold as in use at weight 1, and violet (weight 0) at its card's weight of 1.0. The CLI's `--set-aside`, `--exclude`, `--use` (weight 0 back to 1.0) and the refusal for "set aside and use the same image", by number or by id, all behaved as specified. No request reached ports 8000-8010 or 5173.
- **Surprises.** Krea's references and the bundle images already left excluded images out on main, so the Krea test passes on main for the bundle and guards it; what failed on main was the saved analysis listing the set-aside image.

## 2026-10-19 — Moodboard brief conflicts: the colour-word check, clash modes, notes on opt-in (gap 18)

Branch `fix/moodboard-brief-precedence` (from origin/main 12257250). Spec `docs/brief-precedence-plan.md` (2be39987), built with Justin's answers P1-P4 and the plan's open-question recommendations.

- **What.**
  - *Precedence.* Higher wins, lower fills in: the hand-written brief (as is, no check); pinned colours ("must appear" always go, even against Avoid, with the clash listed; "keep out" as before); Direction and Avoid through the check; board notes only on opt-in; what Nebula measured. Written down in the `moodboard_brief.py` docstring and contract 07 section 1.11.
  - *The check.* New `services/moodboard_colour_words.py`: deterministic, no model, no cost. Parses Direction and Avoid into colour terms with modifiers, negation (no/not/without/never/avoid/minus, up to "but") and scope (object, cast, whole palette; a list item with no noun inherits the head's), then matches in OKLab/OKLCH by hue arcs and chroma gates; a hex in the text matches within dE00 5. Every number is in one table (`HUE_FLOOR` 0.03, `CONFLICT_CHROMA` 0.08, `LARGE_SHARE` 0.10, `CAST_MEAN_CHROMA` 0.015, `CAST_COLOUR_CHROMA` 0.04, `CAST_WARNING_CHROMA` 0.08, `REFERENCE_HEADROOM` 0.04, `HEX_DELTA_E` 5, `NEUTRAL_CEILING` 0.04, `MUTED_CEILING` 0.08), retuned by bumping `LEXICON_VERSION`. The lexicon is our own (the module docstring names the research note `Research/topics/colour-text-contradiction-detection-2026-10.md`, and why XKCD, LUX, c3 and the Colour Thesaurus weren't used: licences unconfirmed or non-commercial). Findings carry `foundBy: "words"`.
  - *Board fields.* `clashMode` (leave-out default, flag, no-measured, keep-all), `colorChoices` {keep, leaveOut}, `sendNotes` (off), `colorCheck` (the store's). Old boards read with defaults and are never rewritten on read. `brief_basis` counts the new fields only when they differ from the defaults, so overrides written on main stay current.
  - *compose.* Adds `leftOut`, `mayClash`, `kept`, `pinnedClashes`, `paletteClashes`, `clashMode`, `notesSent`; each item `{hex, role, share, level, reason, reasons, foundBy[], why: check|choice|mode}`. `palette`/`accents` and the brief text are what generators get. Notes and the cues lifted from them (`MEASURED_CUES` filter) go only when sent.
  - *Store and routes.* New fields on create/update (422 for bad values); `colorCheck` saved by the store on every create and update whose basis moved (Analyze included), a sent one ignored. Turning `sendNotes` on is the person's: `NotesOptInProtected` → the person gate's 403 (`agent_refused` / `person_required`), before anything is written. Node param `send_notes` (board/yes/no) is gated in `_refuse_agent_billing_change`, which every agent node edit, create and apply path already calls.
  - *Node.* `nebula-moodboard` gains `send_notes` (TS and JSON by hand, in sync; checked with a bundled compare). Its bundle carries no notes or image notes unless sent, the new lists, and `analysis` as a generator view (`generator_analysis`): measured keywords, summary and taste profile rebuilt from the brief's colours without notes, `subjectBias` [], `styleBrief` without notes, `providerHints.generic` palette/accents the brief's.
  - *CLI/MCP.* `show` lists Left out (with the `--keep-anyway` command; a colour the person left out offers `--reset-color`), Kept anyway, May clash, pinned clashes, whole-palette findings, `Notes: ...`, and the mode when not the default. `set` gains `--keep-anyway`, `--leave-out`, `--leave-out-flagged`, `--reset-color`, `--clash-mode`, `--send-notes`/`--no-send-notes`; `moodboard_update` the same plus `color_choices` for restore. INSTRUCTIONS' moodboard paragraph says what was left out and that notes are for the person, their team and agents.
  - *Studio.* The lists under "Brief sent to generators" (Keep anyway, Undo, Leave out, Leave out all flagged in flag mode, "Clash check is off for this board."), dimmed left-out swatches with the reason in the tooltip, an Advanced disclosure with the four modes, and the "Send these notes to generators" switch under Notes. The Studio shows the backend's lists and never recomputes them. Rows, the Advanced options and the switch thumb move on the provider switcher's spring (`linear()`, k 500, c 36), none under reduced motion.
- **Decisions not in the spec.**
  - *A temperature allowance never exempts a colour.* "cool jewel tones" in the Direction doesn't protect a cool colour from an Avoid; only hue and reference allowances ("cornflower blue") downgrade an Avoid conflict to a warning, and the reason cites both.
  - *Head-noun inheritance.* "Flowers in cool jewel tones: cornflower blue, violet, lilac" gives each item the head's scope; a head with a style word ("silver tonalist palette: ...") makes the list global.
  - *A term with an upper chroma gate* (sage, lilac, pale, muted, a hue-grey compound's grey) conflicts from C 0.03, so a saturated colour can't hide under "sage".
  - *`foundBy` is a list on merged items* (one colour can be found by two checks), plus `why`. Whole-palette findings (a cast) are their own list, `paletteClashes`.
  - *`no-measured` without a Direction acts as `leave-out`*: with no words, "send no measured colours" would send nothing at all.
  - *With an override active* the lists are still computed and shown: they shape `palette`, the node's palette output and the bundle.
  - *The bundle's colour lists are the brief's* (changed in review, below): `analysis.palette`/`accents`/`colors` hold what generators get and per-image colours drop left-out and keep-out colours; `leftOut` names what went. (The first build kept the measured lists, which let an LLM node put a left-out colour back.)
  - *`with_brief` returns the check it used* (`colorCheck`: the saved one at its basis, else run in memory, never saved on read; the startup pass saves it for boards that lack one).
  - *Agents may close a node's notes, never open them*: `no` → `board` is refused too, since `board` can send. A new node may start on `board`.
  - *`previous` has `send_notes` only when the call touched it*, as with `brief_override`: undoing another change never asks to send notes the person has since turned on. The spec said "all go into previous"; this narrows one key for the same reason the override is narrowed.
  - *Pinning a colour to keep out drops it from Keep anyway* when `colorChoices` isn't sent (the pin is the stronger choice); sent together, the clash is a 422.
  - *The CLI's `--reset-color` matches a choice within dE00 5*, as compose does, so the hex `show` prints finds a choice made on an earlier analysis.
- **Tradeoffs.** Words only (P2): style terms the lexicon doesn't know ("Hudson River School") say nothing. The design keeps a second check open: findings carry `foundBy`, the saved check has `checks.<name>`, and compose honours any finding saved at the current basis (a test saves a fake `foundBy: "reader"` finding). Leaving rows aren't animated.
- **Surprises.** A pearl #eae0c8 board alone averages warm yellow (C 0.034) and would trip the 0.015 cast line; the research case passes with silver leading (0.4 / 0.15 / 0.15). That's a tuning case for GM's labels. On the live GM-like board the blue accent comes out as "may clash" (allowed hue, more saturated than cornflower), as labelled.
- **What changes for existing boards' generator output** (no opt-in set):
  1. `styleBrief` / `generatedStyleBrief`: no `Notes: ...` sentence; `Visual cues:` keeps only measured cues, dropped when none remain.
  2. Boards whose Direction or Avoid names colours: conflicting measured colours leave the brief's colour sentences, `brief.palette`/`accents`, the node's `palette` output and the bundle's `palette`/`accents`.
  3. The node bundle: `notes` and `images[].notes` are `""`; `analysis` is the generator view; `providerHints.generic.palette`/`accents` equal the brief's; new keys `notesSent`, `leftOut`, `mayClash`, `kept`, `pinnedClashes`, `paletteClashes`, `clashMode`.
  4. Unchanged: the saved analysis, `negativePrompt`, `avoidPrompt`, override text and existing overrides' basis.
  5. `fixtures/moodboard_defaults_pin.json` re-pinned: only `composed.styleBrief` of `brand` and `busy` changed (their notes sentence and note cues).
- **Existing tests changed.** `test_moodboard_private_note.py::test_the_moodboard_node_outputs_never_carry_it` now runs the node with `send_notes: "yes"`, so the image note is there beside the private one (by default no notes go at all). `test_reference_roles.py` approves the inserted `send_notes` param. The MCP INSTRUCTIONS line avoids snake_case words that aren't tools (a test checks that).
- **Docs.** Contract 07 new 1.11, pointers in 1.2 and 1.4, changelog; `skills/nebula/SKILL.md`; `docs/MCP-SETUP.md`; `.agents/skills/krea/SKILL.md` (bundle keys); MCP INSTRUCTIONS and the `moodboard_get` / `moodboard_update` docstrings. `docs/MODEL_REFERENCE.md` regenerated (no change: the node isn't listed); `check-node-contracts.mjs` passes for 308 definitions.
- **Tests.** New: `test_moodboard_colour_words.py` (30: the labelled GM table, the research cases, negation, reordering, plurals and capitals, warm vs warm yellow, cast on cool and warm boards, hex in text, words inside words, cornflower allowance, scope swap, pinned role), `test_moodboard_brief_precedence.py` (34: compose per mode, choices incl. a shifted re-analysis, notes off by default and on by board or node, basis and stale, a saved second-check finding honoured only at its basis, an old board read writes nothing, 422s, the check saved and a sent one ignored, Analyze refreshes it, the person gate for `sendNotes`, the node gate, the node def, CLI show/set/restore/refusal, MCP), 2 in `test_moodboard_handler.py`, 9 frontend tests in the three Studio files. On the base: both new backend files fail at import, the 2 handler tests fail, 9 of the frontend tests fail (2 pass by design as guards for an older backend).
  - *Runs.* 43 backend files that mention moodboard or brief, plus the billing, proposal, apply, CLI and agent-surface files: 1327 passed. Vitest on the three Studio files: 42 passed. `tsc -b --noEmit` clean; eslint clean on the changed files.
- **Live check** (isolated backend 8793 via `devserver.py` with the person link written to a scratch file, Vite 5793 pinned to it, Puppeteer; 8000-8010 and 5173 blocked by CDP and interception, zero requests reached them). 25/25: a GM-like board (Direction, Avoid, pin, notes, one image with brick, salmon, rust and blue accents) analyzed for real leaves out the three warm accents with "Avoid: red, orange or pink flowers", lists the pin and still sends it, keeps the blue as "may clash"; `nebula moodboard show` on that port prints the lists and the keep command; `--send-notes` from the CLI (not the person) is refused and saves nothing; in Studio the lists and dimmed swatches show, Keep anyway saves (colour back, not pinned) and Undo clears it, each of the four modes saves and applies, and the person's notes switch turns on (brief gets `Notes: ...`) and off. Every Studio PUT was 200. Screenshots in the session scratchpad, looked at; the switch's on state was too faint at first and now uses the accent tokens.
- **Review fixes (2026-10-19, second pass).**
  - *Negation ends with its noun phrase.* "No people, red flowers and a blue sky" excluded the red and blue the Direction asks for: `negated` ran to the clause's end. Now, once a noun (or palette word) follows the negator, the next comma, "and" or "&" closes it; "or" and "/" carry it on ("no people or red flowers"), "but" still closes it, and a list before the noun stays negated ("no red, orange or pink flowers, blue sky" excludes three, allows blue).
  - *Only an allowance that names the colour softens an Avoid.* `check()` downgraded on any allowance hit, so "Warm evening light" (a temperature word, always "arc") kept Avoid-listed reds as "may clash", and "pale blue sky" did the same for a C 0.21 blue. Exclusions now soften only on `cover` hits, as the ceiling loop already did.
  - *Brown isn't a soft colour.* Chroma-gated (conflict from C 0.03) is now an explicit `SOFT_HUES` set (sage, lilac, lavender, cream, ivory) plus modifiers and hue-grey compounds; brown's `cmax` only separates it from orange, so it conflicts from C 0.08 and near-black shadows are at most a warning. `LEXICON_VERSION` 1 → 2, so saved checks refresh.
  - *Repointing a "yes" node is opening notes.* The node gate compared only the `send_notes` rank, so an agent could point a node the person set to `yes` at another board. `_notes_opened` refuses that unless the same edit sets `send_notes` to `board` or `no`; a `board` node may be repointed (it follows the new board's own switch).
  - *colorCheck saved at startup.* Boards saved before gap 18 had no `colorCheck`, so the check ran on every generation and API read. `save_colour_checks` (in `_moodboard_brief_fields_startup`, after the brief-fields migration) writes only `colorCheck` on boards whose saved check is missing or stale, trash included, no backup (it's a cache). Idempotent. Boards copied in while running get one on their next save or the next start.
  - *Bundle colour lists*: see the decision above.
  - *Fixtures and tests.* `route_tables.json` regenerated (only `nebula-moodboard`'s `allParamKeys` gains `send_notes`). `StoredAssetNodes.test.tsx` now expects a new Moodboard node to carry `send_notes: 'board'`, as every node carries its definition defaults; harmless, the gate lets a new node start on `board`. New tests, each failing without its fix: negation and cover-only cases, near-black brown, compose for both, the gate repoint, the startup pass (no `check()` calls after it), the bundle's lists, `previous` without `send_notes` for a `--clash-mode` change, and three Studio view tests (a new board's `sendNotes` false, Undo keeping, pin-wins filter).
- **Merged with main (#87, board model v2) and checked again.**
  - *Conflicts* were side-by-side additions (layout fields beside gap 18's on create/PUT, the store, the types). The node's bundle images keep main's `output_image` whitelist and get `notes: ""` unless notes are sent. Contract 07's saved-fields table, split by a paragraph on main, is whole again.
  - *Golden file.* `expected.json` changed on purpose. Every differing path (268, in 52 kinds) was compared with gap 18's stated changes before the file was replaced, and the kinds are listed in `test_moodboard_golden.py`'s docstring. No old board clashes, so every list is empty. Nothing moved in source hashes, the brief basis, run notes, Krea style references, the brief's palette or the negative prompts.
  - *Every reason on a row.* In `no-measured` mode a colour that also clashes with Avoid showed only "Measured colors are off for this board", so Keep anyway hid the clash (found by the live check). Studio rows now join every reason with " · " and `show` with "; ". Tests: a Studio one and a CLI one, each failing without the change.
- **Found, not fixed.**
  1. The generator fold with a real model wasn't run live (no keys); the handler tests read the bundle and the existing fold tests cover the prompt join.
  2. Style words outside the lexicon are silent until a second check (P2's open vision/model check) adds findings.

## 2026-10-19 — Krea 2 prices (krea-2-generate and the three catalog nodes)

Branch `fix/krea-2-pricing`. Run estimates showed Krea 2 as unpriced, so agents were refused under any USD limit.

- **Why they were missing.** Krea's OpenAPI prices Krea 2 by `k2BillingTier` (`text-to-image`, `srefs`, `moodboards`), which isn't a request field. `scripts/sync-krea-catalog.py` keeps price points only when every dimension is a request field, so since the first price table (409e02fe, 2026-10-10) the pinned catalog held `pricingUnmapped: ["k2BillingTier"]` and the script skipped them. Nothing was ever removed. `krea-2-generate` is hand-written and nobody had added an entry.
- **Prices** (checked 2026-10-19). From `x-krea-pricing` in https://api.krea.ai/openapi.json (sha256 125dae8e751d): Medium 0.03 / 0.035 / 0.04, Large 0.06 / 0.065 / 0.07, Turbo 0.015 / 0.0175 / 0.02 (text to image / srefs / moodboards). The Krea 2 guide (https://www.krea.ai/docs/developers/krea-2/overview.md#pricing) states the same Medium and Large figures and "Combining moodboards with style references does not increase the price per generation — you pay the moodboard rate". It doesn't list Turbo. So the research note's "+$0.005 for style references" holds (Turbo: +$0.0025), and a moodboard adds $0.01 (Turbo $0.005).
- **How.** The generator now treats `k2BillingTier` as a derived dimension (`DERIVED_DIMENSIONS`) and maps tiers onto the inputs that set them (`K2_CATALOG_INPUTS`, `K2_NODE`). It also writes `krea-2-generate`'s entry from the same price points, so a refresh updates both. If the guide's Medium or Large figures stop matching the OpenAPI, the script stops (against the live guide since the review fixes below). The three endpoints were re-pinned with `--openapi <file> --only ...` (now repeatable). Only their catalog entries changed, and no node definition changed.
- **New price variable `(wired PORT)`** (model_pricing.py and pricing.ts). It is `yes` when that port has an edge in, else `no`. The tier inputs arrive either typed into a field or by wire, and the catalog nodes' ports share ids with their params. The old rule "a priced param that's wired is unknown" would have made every wired style reference unpriced. Now a param is exempt from that rule when every row and extra that reads it also reads `(wired X)`. A row that reads the param alone still makes a wired run unpriced (shared fixture case `loose`).
- **Judgment calls.**
  - LoRA `styles`/`style_id` and `image_url` (image to image): Krea doesn't say which tier they bill. They were priced at the tier their references give, on rows marked `unconfirmed`. The review fixes below changed that to a range.
  - On `krea-2-generate`, a wired `moodboard` is either a Nebula board (the handler sends it as `image_style_references`) or a Krea moodboard id (sent as `moodboards`). Only the wire's value tells them apart, so the price is the range $0.035-0.04 (Large $0.065-0.07). A Nebula board with no images would actually bill text to image, below that range. The case is too rare to model.
  - A typed field counts as set when it isn't empty, so a literal `[]` prices at the higher tier (an overestimate). Whitespace-only fields: see the review fixes.
- **Review fixes (same day).**
  - The LoRA and image-to-image rows were `unconfirmed: true`, but on an entry without routes nothing reads that flag (only the provider switcher's `*` does, for routes), so the Run chip, proposals and agent limits showed them as exact prices. Now they're a range from the tier the references give up to the moodboard tier, the highest of the three tiers in Krea's `x-krea-pricing` (Medium LoRA without references: $0.03-0.04). The range shows the uncertainty everywhere, and agent limits check the top, so they never count less than the bill. I chose that over leaving those runs unpriced, which would refuse every agent run with a LoRA under a USD limit. This assumes Krea bills every Krea 2 run at one of the three tiers its OpenAPI lists. No Krea 2 row carries `unconfirmed` now.
  - A whitespace-only tier field (`moodboard_id: "  "`, `image_style_references: " "`) priced the higher tier, but the handler strips it (`_clean_str`) and the gateway drops a whitespace-only jsonParams field, so the run bills text to image. There's a new entry field, `whitespaceUnset`: the params the handler strips, where a whitespace-only value prices as unset. It's scoped to those params, not global, because other entries match `""` on fields whose handlers I didn't check (Kling `multi_prompt`, `thinking_level`, ...). The generator writes it: `moodboard_id`/`style_id` on `krea-2-generate`, and the tier inputs among the jsonParams on the catalog nodes. `image_url` isn't on it, since a whitespace URL fails the gateway's `uri` check and the run never bills. The frontend matches Python's `str.strip()` whitespace set exactly (JS `trim()` differs on U+FEFF and U+001C-001F), and both sides run the shared cases.
  - The "guide drift" guard compared the OpenAPI against hard-coded copies of the guide's figures, so a change to the guide alone went unnoticed. Now every refresh (and `--refresh-guide`, `--guide <file>` for a saved copy) fetches the guide's markdown, parses the Pricing section strictly (header, rows, the one moodboard note, whose rates must match the table) and pins it in the catalog as `krea2Guide`. The sources quote is built from it. Any line it doesn't parse stops the refresh, so a new note (for example one about which tier a LoRA bills) gets a human re-read. A guide variant with no Krea 2 endpoint (a Turbo row) also stops it. Pinned 2026-10-19 from the live page: same figures and quote as before.
  - Tests: 8 new shared `shippedRunCases` (ranges, whitespace including U+001C and U+FEFF parity) and 1 synthetic case. In `test_model_pricing.py` the unconfirmed test became a range test, plus whitespace and `whitespaceUnset` validation tests. In `test_krea_catalog.py`: guide parsing, guide-only drift, an unmapped guide variant, and 5 kinds of guide change that stop the refresh. Results: 31 backend test files (model_pricing / agent_spend / estimate) 1679 passed, the full frontend vitest suite 3201 passed, `tsc -b` clean, `sync-krea-catalog.py --check` passed.
- **Fix on the way.** `krea_entry` stamped every entry with the catalog's top-level `fetchedAt`/sha even when an `--only` refresh had given the model its own. It now uses the model's.
- **Tests.** `test_model_pricing.py`: 11 new tests, which all fail on main (12257250). They cover each Krea 2 node at its defaults, style references wired or typed, moodboard plus references, the wired-board range, the unconfirmed LoRA/i2i rows, and the `(wired PORT)` mechanics and validation. `test_krea_catalog.py` checks that the generator prices all four and stops on drift from the guide. `pricing_cases.json` gets 4 `(wired PORT)` cases and 12 Krea 2 `shippedRunCases`, which the backend and runScope.test.ts both run. All 32 backend test files that mention model_pricing, agent_spend or estimate: 1658 passed. 24 frontend test files that touch pricing: 498 passed. `tsc` clean, `check-node-contracts` passed, `sync-krea-catalog.py --check` passed. MODEL_REFERENCE.md has no prices, so it was unchanged.

## 2026-10-19 — Moodboard canvas PR1: board model v2, lossless writes

Branch `feat/moodboard-canvas`, PR1 of `docs/moodboard-canvas-plan.md` (section 6). Backend only; nothing visible. Justin's values: full weight is a 480x270 card (`FULL_AREA = 129_600`, Q1 a), the smallest card is weight 0.05 (Q3 a).

- **What.**
  - *`services/moodboard_layout.py` (new).* `FULL_AREA`, `MIN_WEIGHT`, `weight_of`, `size_for`, `card_weight` (weight 0 shows at full size), `legacy_layout` (6-column grid in number order, 40 px gaps, columns as wide as their widest card, rows as tall as their tallest, cards centred in their cell), `place` ("after the last-added card" only: its row if there's room, else a new row under the board, 24 px from every card and frame), `normalize_placements` (a new image's requested cards), `rescale`, the aspect cache, and `check_board_layout` (section 4.10's limits on frames, suggestions, readings and placements).
  - *The store.* `_normalize_images(images, stored=..., board=..., by=...)` merges by id: a key left out keeps its saved value, a saved image keeps its `placements` (and any key this version doesn't know) whatever the client sends, a new image takes the cards it asks for or is placed by the server, and an image left out is removed. `get()` and `update()` lay an old board out in memory (`_migrated(board, layout_board=True)`); `list()` doesn't. `frames`, `suggestions` and `readings` read as empty. Every store edit (`create`, `update`, `keep_brief_override`) saves the layout and stamps `layoutVersion: 1`. `create`/`update` refuse the board-level layout keys.
  - *Routes.* `MoodboardImageModel.placements` (every key GET returns is accepted, so a client can send back what it read). PUT and POST use `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` per image. `frames`, `suggestions`, `readings`, `layoutVersion` and `lastRead` on POST or PUT are a 422 that says layout can't be set with PUT. The GET route reads off the event loop.
  - *Node outputs.* `handlers/moodboard.py` copies only `id, url, weight, notes, excluded` into `bundle.images` (`moodboard_store.output_image`, replacing `without_private`). That is exactly what every stored board gave before (the store kept only those keys plus `privateNote`, which the handler stripped), and the golden file is unchanged and passing.
  - *CLI and MCP.* `moodboard_client._steering` compares only `url, weight, notes, excluded` (`STEERING_KEYS`), the keys `source_hash` reads. `get_board` reads a board again by id after a name match. `brief(board, layout=True)` adds each image's `placements` and the board's `frames`; `nebula moodboard show --json` and `moodboard_get` use it.
  - *Frontend.* Optional `placements`, `layoutVersion`, `frames`, `suggestions`, `readings` in `types/index.ts`, and `MoodboardPlacement`, `MoodboardFrame`. The create/update input types leave the layout fields out. The Studio's `updateImage` clears the analysis only for `STEERING_KEYS` (`moodboard-studio/steering.ts`). `moodboardToDraft` already kept `placements` (it copies each image as sent); its save payload is an explicit list of board fields with no layout keys, and its image entries pass the new PUT model. Both are pinned by new Studio tests.
- **The PUT merge change.** Before, `PUT` rebuilt each image from a fixed key list and filled a left-out key with its default, so a client that didn't send `privateNote` erased it. Now a left-out key keeps its saved value. Callers that relied on "left out = default" must now send the default. The contract (07, 1.3) says so.
- **Decisions not in the plan.**
  - *`brief()` adds the layout only when asked (`layout=True`).* The plan says `brief()` adds `placements` and `frames`, and also that the golden file stays identical. The golden file pins `brief()` of every old board's GET, and an old board now reads with placements, so both can't hold. The default view stays as pinned; `show --json` and `moodboard_get` ask for the layout; lists and edit results don't (a 300-image board's cards would fill an agent's context on every edit). Open question for the coordinator.
  - *A weight set by PUT resizes the cards.* Section 4.3 says a weight edit that isn't a resize (CLI, MCP, the List slider) scales every card so the largest equals the weight. The plan puts that in PR3's `weight` op, but the CLI and MCP set weights through PUT today, so without it PR1 would save cards whose size disagrees with their weight. Weight 0 leaves the cards as they are (set aside at full size, Q8). Only a changed weight scales.
  - *A new image's weight.* With `placements` and no `weight` sent, the image weighs what its largest card shows. With both, the cards scale to the weight. POST now dumps only what was sent per image, so this works on create too.
  - *`placedBy` comes from who asked* (the person gate, as `briefOverride.by` does), never from the client. Cards Nebula places get the same stamp; a legacy grid's cards are `person` (the order was theirs).
  - *Aspect: the file first, upright, then the analysis.* The plan had the analysis's `width/height` first. The analysis measures stored pixels, so a phone photo with an EXIF quarter turn would lay out sideways, while thumbnails (`output_thumbnail.py`) show it upright. The header read applies the EXIF orientation. The analysis's size is used only when the file can't be read now.
  - *Card ids on old boards* are a hash of the board id, image id and number, so every read of an unedited board gives the same ids and an agent that read one can still name it after the first write.
  - *Images with the same id* (only possible in hand-edited files) are matched in order: the first incoming copy merges with the first saved one, and so on. Nothing is refused.
  - *`[]` or `null` placements on a new image* mean "place it for me", not an error.
  - *A saved layout that breaks 4.10's limits* (a hand edit, a newer Nebula) is logged on read and the board still opens as saved. Nothing writes frames, suggestions or readings in PR1, so they round-trip untouched.
  - *The node, Analyze and the dry run* read boards without laying them out (`get(laid_out=False)`), except that Analyze's own read is laid out in a worker thread so its save (which saves an old board's layout) finds the image headers already read.
- **Surprise: the path check is the cost.** Laying out an old board needs each image's aspect, which goes through `resolve_moodboard_image_path` and so `file_access.require_allowed_path`: about 1.7 ms an image, on every read. `file_aspect` now keeps the ratio per URL and agent workspace (`file_access.access_scope()`, new: the one input the check depends on besides the path) with the resolved file's device, inode, mtime and size; a later read reuses it only while one `os.stat` shows that same file unchanged with one link, and otherwise runs the full check again. Only the ratio is kept. Importing `agent_workspaces` directly from the layout module tripped the paid-API import walk in `test_node_readiness.py`, which is why the scope comes through `file_access`.
- **Measured** (generated 300-image old board, 5 aspect ratios, JPEG, isolated backend, TestClient): GET cold cache median 518 ms, warm 3.2 ms; the store's laid-out read 1.2 ms warm, unlaid 0.2 ms; list 0.2 ms. After its first write (layout saved), GET is 2.6 ms whether or not the cache is warm. Before the cache, warm was 567 ms.
- **Tradeoffs.**
  - The cold read still runs the path check once per image after a restart (about half a second at 300 images). It runs off the event loop for GET and Analyze. A first write by PUT on a board nobody has opened since the restart does it on the loop; the CLI, MCP and Studio all GET first.
  - No locking yet: concurrent writes are still last write wins on board fields (PR3). Images merge by id, so two writers no longer erase each other's per-image keys, but an image list sent from a stale read can still drop an image added since.
- **Writers checked** (each keeps unknown keys and none writes a layout for a board nobody edited): store `create`/`update`/`keep_brief_override` (save the layout: they are edits), the analysis save (`update`), `migrate_brief_fields` (deep-copies the board, adds brief fields only), `move` (#86) and the start-up re-home (`asset_project_rehome.move_asset`, a dict copy with a new `projectId`), Recently deleted and restore (`asset_trash`, `os.replace` of the file). Project duplicate/export/import and `.nebula.zip` restore don't touch moodboard files (grep). Commons intake only reads (`list`).
- **Docs.** Contract 07 (1.1, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, changelog), `skills/nebula/SKILL.md`, `docs/MCP-SETUP.md`, and two notes in the plan (the aspect order in 4.8 and `brief(layout=True)` in PR1).
- **Tests.** `backend/tests/test_moodboard_board_model.py` (32). The five the plan names fail on the base (8e14de37) for its reasons: the private note reset to `""`, saved placements dropped, the CLI `set` 422 on `placements`, `_steering` counting placements, and placements in the bundle images. New: an old board reads with the grid in number order (sizes, aspect, weight 0 at full size, nothing overlapping) and its file is unchanged after `get`, `list`, GET, the CLI by name and `moodboard_get`; the layout is the same on every read; the hash and brief basis are unchanged and the first write saves the layout it read; CLI `add` on an old board lands right after the last card; new images fill a row then start a new one with no overlap; requested placements (where, size from weight and aspect, server-stamped `placedBy`); five bad placements refused; the five layout keys refused on PUT and POST; a Studio round trip; a CLI weight resizes its card; trash and restore keep the bytes; a move copies the file as it was; the brief migration and an analysis save keep the layout; `show --json` and `moodboard_get` list it and lists don't; an EXIF-turned photo lays out upright; the aspect cache (one check per file, again for another workspace, a changed file or a second hard link). Frontend: 2 new in `MoodboardStudioView.test.tsx`. The golden file passes unchanged.
- **Runs.** Backend suite 7061 passed; the 30 backend test files that mention moodboard (733 tests, with `test_file_access.py` and `test_skill_install.py`) pass on the final code. Studio vitest files 33 passed; `tsc -b --noEmit` and eslint on the changed files clean.
- **Review fixes (8 findings).**
  - *An older Nebula's edit.* Base drops image keys it doesn't know (so every card) but keeps `layoutVersion`, and PR1 then placed the board with `place()`, not the grid. `ensure_layout` now uses `legacy_layout` when no image has a card, so a saved grid comes back unchanged. Cards placed or moved after the grid are still lost then. Open question: keep placements in a board-level map keyed by image id (base keeps unknown board keys), so an older writer can't drop them. Recommendation: decide before PR3, while nothing but PR1 writes placements and the move is cheap.
  - *Odd layout files.* `float(10**400)` raised OverflowError and non-list `placements`/`frames` raised TypeError, so the list, GET or an edit returned 500. Now `_finite` reads numbers (Overflow is "not a number"), `cards_of`/`frames_of` read only lists of objects, `_with_layout_fields` logs any exception from the check, and an image with no card that can be drawn is placed again (in memory on read, and on the next edit). `_weight` in the store treats an overflowing weight as 1.0 (base had the same 500 there).
  - *Unresolvable urls.* `resolve_moodboard_image_path` raises RuntimeError for an unknown `~user` and ValueError for a null byte. `file_aspect` now returns None for any exception, so the image lays out at the analysis size or 4:3. Also: a write stamps `layoutVersion` only when every image has a card (`_stamp_layout`), so a failed in-memory layout is retried on the next read rather than saved as "no cards".
  - *Row width.* `place()` let a 7th portrait or square card into an old grid's row (six 270 px cards are far under 3,080 px). A row now also holds at most six cards up to the anchor (cards overlapping its height, left of the spot). 16:9 rows are unchanged.
  - *Weight raised by PUT.* Kept as built: cards scale from their top-left corner and may cover a neighbour, like a drag resize. Moving a grown card to free space would break the person's arrangement and, from PR5, frame membership. Written into contract 07 (1.3) and plan 4.3, pinned by a test. Open question for the coordinator alongside "scaling on PUT".
  - *Tests the review asked for.* Keep on an old board saves the grid it read; PUT keeps unknown image keys; duplicate ids merge in order; POST with no weight weighs what the card shows (asserts `MIN_WEIGHT` for 999x1 and 0.25 for 240x135). Each was checked against the mutation the reviewer used (all fail under it).
  - 16 new test cases. The 11 for the code fixes fail on ea2f04d2.

## 2026-10-19 — Move to Global / Move to <project> for Moodboards and Characters (P4)

Branch `feat/move-asset-scope` (on `fix/project-scope-canvas`, PR #85). Justin's call P4: a board or Character can change scope after it's made, from the Studio, the Assets panel, the CLI and MCP.

- **What.**
  - *Routes.* `POST /api/moodboards/{id}/move` and `POST /api/characters/{id}/move` with `{projectId: string|null}` (null = Global; the key is required, extra keys are 422). Answer: `{status: moved|unchanged, kind, id, from, to, fromName, toName, asset, detail}`, plus `movedBy` when it moved. Refusals: an unsafe target id 400; an unknown asset 404; an asset in Recently deleted 409 `code: in_trash` "Restore it first ... then move it."; an unknown or trashed target project 422 (the same `_require_canvas_project` sentences as create); two live copies of the id (one per scope) 409, nothing changed. Already there is a 200 `unchanged` with no write and no broadcast.
  - *Store.* `MoodboardStore.move` / `CharacterStore.move` call the #85 seam `asset_project_rehome.move_asset`, which moves the file between scope folders and changes only `projectId`.
  - *Broadcast.* `storedAssetChanged` as for any edit, plus `projectId` on moves only, so open tabs can follow (below).
  - *Studio.* `components/asset-move/AssetMoveMenu.tsx`, a Move button in the toolbar's own button class just before Delete, with a portal menu (arrow keys, Home/End, Escape/Tab return focus, click outside closes, a short spring on open). Choices from `lib/assetMove.ts`: "Move to Global" when the asset is in a project (this one or another), "Move to <open project>" when it's Global or in another project, and with no project open "Move to a project", off, with the no-project sentence. `hooks/useStudioAssetMove.ts` does the move: save first, hold the save slot, move, set the draft's `projectId`, move the draft to its new-scope key (`copyTo`), reopen in the new scope so the rail switches tab and selects it, relist the rail.
  - *Assets panel.* The selected item's row now has Open, Add to canvas and Move (the same menu). The row is 326 px; three buttons fit on one line (checked live).
  - *CLI.* `nebula moodboard move <board> --to global|current|<project id or exact name> [--json]` and `nebula character move <character> --to ... [--json]`. Human output says where it went, that nodes keep working in every project, and the command to move it back. `moodboard_client.resolve_move_target` resolves `--to`: `global`; `current` (the open project, or "no project is open ..."); an exact id; else a case-insensitive exact name, refusing two projects with that name, a project in Recently deleted ("Restore it first") and an unknown one. An older backend without the route (404 "Not Found" or 405) gets "this version of Nebula can't move ..." and nothing changes. New `backend/character_client.py` finds a Character by id or exact name across Global and live projects.
  - *MCP.* `moodboard_move(board, to)` and `character_move(character, to)`, annotated `readOnlyHint=False, destructiveHint=False, idempotentHint=True, openWorldHint=False`, named in INSTRUCTIONS, and in `NEBULA_MCP_TOOLS`, so the in-app Claude allow-list has them.
- **Decisions not in the brief.**
  - *`version` and `updatedAt` are kept.* A move changes where the asset is filed, not what it is, and nothing reads them for stale-write checks (the PUTs don't compare versions). Bumping would make every node's cache and every "edited" sort treat a move as an edit.
  - *Unsaved edits: saved first, then moved* (the safer of the two, as Delete does). A failed save stops the move, so what moves is what the person sees saved. While the move is in flight the hook holds the draft's save slot (`beginSave`), so an autosave can't send the old `projectId` (the board PUT refuses a changed `projectId` with 422). Edits typed during the move stay in the draft and save to the new place after. Mutation checks: without the slot 1 Studio test fails; without patching the draft's `projectId` 4 fail.
  - *The broadcast can beat the answer.* The move's own `storedAssetChanged` can re-home the draft before `moveStoredAsset` resolves, so the hook resolves its key through aliases (`here()`) and checks the UI (`isOpen`) rather than the old key to decide whether to reopen. Without that, the race test fails.
  - *Kept drafts in other tabs follow.* `lib/keptDraftMoves.ts` subscribes once to the ws and calls the new `assetStudioDraftStore.rehome(kind, id, projectId)` on a move broadcast: each kept draft of that asset gets the new `projectId` and moves to its new-scope key. Otherwise a board moved from the CLI or the panel while its draft was kept would 422 on the next Studio save (checked live: an edit after a panel move saves).
  - *Characters' CLI is `nebula character move`.* `nebula move` already moves canvas nodes, and the Character verbs belong with the asset. There was no `character` command group, so this adds one with just `move`.
  - *Who moved it* is in the answer (`movedBy`, from the request's actor) only. Neither asset kind keeps an author or editor field, and the brief said not to invent a journal.
  - *Two live copies* (an id in two scopes, possible only from hand-copied files) are refused with 409 rather than picking one: which is "the" asset depends on folder listing order.
  - *The edit refusal now points at Move.* A PUT that changes a board's `projectId` used to say only that it can't change; it now names the move route.
  - *Menu layer.* The menu sits at `--sr-layer-workspace-overlay` (55). The first build used `--sr-layer-popover` (40), under the Studio (`--sr-layer-workspace`, 50): the DOM-driven checks passed, but the screenshots showed no menu. The live check now asserts the menu item is the top element at its own centre.
- **Docs.** Contract 07 new 1.10 and changelog; `skills/nebula/SKILL.md`; `docs/MCP-SETUP.md`; the `move_asset` docstring.
- **Tests.**
  - *Backend.* `tests/test_asset_move.py` (20): Global to project, project to Global and project to project for both kinds, with files, `version`, `updatedAt` and the broadcast; already there; each refusal; two copies; `movedBy` for an agent and anonymous; a Studio PUT with the old `projectId` 422 and without it 200; nodes in any project resolve a moved asset; CLI human, `--json`, refusals, `character move`, an older backend; MCP and its annotations; the allow-list. Two existing tests updated (`move` in the verb list, the new PUT message). On the base, 19 of the 20 fail; the one that passes checks that nodes resolve the asset, which holds there because nothing moves.
  - *Frontend.* `lib/assetMove.test.ts` (4), 8 in `MoodboardStudioView.test.tsx` (choices per state, Global to project, other project to Global, other project to the open one, save first with edits during the move kept, a failed save and a refused move, the broadcast arriving first), 4 in `CharacterStudioView.test.tsx`, 4 in `AssetsPanel.test.tsx`, `store/assetStudioDraftStore.rehome.test.ts` (3). The 11 new Studio tests fail on the base.
  - *Runs.* Backend suite 7020 passed on the final code. `tsc -b` clean, eslint clean on touched files. Full vitest: 3102 passed and 74 timed out under load in 27 files; each of the 27 passes alone (including MoodboardStudioView, AssetsPanel and AssetStudioDrafts).
- **Live check** (isolated backend 8841, Vite 5841, Puppeteer; 8000-8010 and 5173 blocked through CDP, zero requests reached them). 43/43 on fresh data: Studio in Shoot A, rename unsaved, Move to Global (rename saved first, file in `_global` only, rail on Global with the board selected, the panel's Global tab lists it, A's Project tab doesn't); Shoot B's node shows and runs it; Move back to Shoot A; from B the board in A offers Global and Shoot B, and Move to Shoot B clears the "This board is in Shoot A." notice; the real CLI `--to global`, `--to current --json` and an already-there run, with B's Project tab updating without a reload; Character Studio: Global Nari to Shoot B (version kept, rail on Project, the node still runs), then `nebula character move Nari --to global`; the panel's Move, and a Studio edit after it saves. Screenshots in the session scratchpad, looked at. The one console error is `PUT /api/settings` 403: the headless tab isn't linked to the person, so settings are locked. That's expected and unrelated.
- **Found, not fixed.**
  1. Styles have no Move. They have their own `scope`, so it's a follow-up.
  2. A kept draft follows a move only if this tab's socket was connected when the move happened. A tab offline at the time keeps the old `projectId` until it reloads the asset.

## 2026-10-19 — "Project" means the canvas project for Moodboards, Characters and Styles

Branch `fix/project-scope-canvas` (on `fix/moodboard-studio-open`, PR #84, since merged into main). Closes found-not-fixed (1) and (2) of the Moodboard Studio entry below.

- **What was wrong.** Project assets had two meanings of "this project". The app's Project tabs used `GET /api/project`, which returned the backend's working-folder name (`nebula_nodes`, or `NEBULA_PROJECT_ID`), the same for every canvas project. The CLI and MCP (`--project current`) used the open canvas project's id (`activeProjectId`). So a board an agent made "for this project" never showed in the person's Project tab, a board made in the Studio showed in every canvas project, and the Studio rail opened on an empty Project tab with the board open.
- **Cause.** `services/project_context.py` predates canvas projects and was never moved over; the CLI was written after them.
- **Fix.**
  - *One source of truth.* The canvas project. `GET /api/project` now returns the open canvas project `{id, name}` from the catalog, or 404 "No project is open." (`project_context.py` is gone). The create routes (`POST /api/moodboards`, `/api/characters`, `/api/presets` with `scope: project`) check `projectId` with `_require_canvas_project`: an unknown id or a project in Recently deleted is 422 with a sentence that says what to do; no `projectId` is Global, as before. Lists and updates take any safe id.
  - *Frontend.* `lib/currentProject.ts` is a small zustand store that `projectStore` publishes its open project into (`publishOpenProject`), so `lib/api` reads it without importing the project store (that import pulled `graphStore` and the ws client into every API test and broke 57 of them). With no project open it's null and `resolveProjectId()` throws `NoProjectOpenError`. The Assets panel, both Studio rails, Recently deleted, the Styles library and the node pickers list by the open project's id, keyed so a slow answer for the old project never shows in the new one, relist on a switch and on `storedAssetChanged`, and show "Open a project to see its …" with New off when none is open. The draft store no longer keeps its own `projectId`; a project draft saves only while the project it started in is still open.
  - *Rails.* Both Studios take the rail's tab from the open asset's own `projectId` (`lib/assetHome.ts`, replacing `moodboard-studio/railEmpty.ts`). An asset from another project opens on the Project tab with "This board is in Shoot A." (or "This Character is in …") above the open project's list. Character Studio had the kept-draft bug the Moodboard rail had (wrong tab when the draft was already loaded); fixed the same way.
  - *Cross-project use stays.* Justin: "As long as we can copy the node moodboards live in to a different project this should be fine." Nothing refuses another project's asset by id: a node copied or imported into another project shows the asset, runs, opens the Studio on it, and a save from there sends the asset's own `projectId`, so it stays home.
  - *Copy in one project, paste in another (his condition for R1).* `loadProjectGraph` used to set `clipboard: null` (from c76e4e3a, "project workspace isolation", which gives no reason for the clipboard), so Cmd+C in A then Cmd+V in B did nothing. Now the clipboard outlives a project load; undo and redo are still cleared. Why that's safe: paste builds each node's params with `providerSafeCloneParams`, which reads `providerStartAmbiguities` and `providerRecoveries`, and those are keyed by node id, belong to the open canvas, and are reset by every project load. Node ids restart per project, so after a switch they'd say nothing about A's nodes, or name B's node with the same id and put B's recovery checkpoint (a paid provider id) on A's node. So `copySelected` works out each node's provider-safe params at copy time against A's own lists and keeps them in the clipboard (`CanvasClipboard.params`), with `source: {projectId, load}`; `load` counts project loads. Paste on the same load re-checks against the canvas as before (a checkpoint or ambiguity may have arrived since the copy), so same-project paste is unchanged. Paste anywhere else (another project, or the same one opened again) uses the copy-time params: a node unsafe at copy time refuses with the same World Labs warning, and the node-local `runIncludesFreshPaidWorldLabsStart` check still runs, so a blank paid World Labs node never becomes a new paid start. Duplicate stays same-canvas only. The agent-driven switch the tab follows goes through the same `loadProjectGraph`. *Where it lands:* A's coordinates mean nothing in B (the first live run pasted the board on top of B's node), so a paste from another load is centred in the visible canvas, then moved to the nearest spot whose bounding box is clear of every node there (40 px gap), preferring one that fits in the view, and keeping the group's own layout (`findOpenGroupOffset` in `lib/nodePlacement.ts`, beside the `findAvailableNodePosition` the Assets and Nodes panels use, which places one slot-sized node and can't hold a group). When no clear spot fits in the view (zoomed in on a full canvas), it takes the nearest clear one and the canvas pans to it (`fitView` on the pasted nodes, never zooming in past the current zoom). The seam: the store doesn't know the viewport, so Canvas's Cmd+V handler passes `view`, its wrapper's box through `screenToFlowPosition`, into `pasteClipboard`, which now returns the pasted ids for that pan; with no view given it stays where it was copied, still clear of the nodes. Sizes are the canvas's measured ones, else 320x220. A same-load paste is still +20 px.
  - *Re-home (every start).* `services/asset_project_rehome.py`. Assets in folders that aren't `_global`, a canvas project or a trashed project are moved by use. **Justin picked R1 on 2026-10-19:** a Moodboard or Character used by nodes in exactly one canvas project goes there; used in none or in several goes to Global; Styles go to Global (P3). Use counts saved snapshots of live projects plus the open canvas. Trashed assets move too, with their trash record. It runs on every start, not once: an older build or the desktop app on the same `~/.nebula` can still write an old-style folder, and with a "done" marker those assets would vanish from every Project tab, silently and for good. Finding them is a listing of each root and its `.trash`. A start with nothing old-style writes no backup, no log and no startup line. Backups and `migration-log.json` go under `<root>/../<kind>-backups/project-rehome-<UTC>/` only when something moved or a new skip was found. The roots come from each store's own resolver (`moodboard_store.store_root()`, `character_store.store_root()`, `preset_store.store_root()`, new public wrappers of their private `_root` functions), so they can't drift from where the stores write. **Undo:** stop the backend, copy each backup folder's files back over its root (same relative paths), delete the moved copies named by `file` in the log, and start with `NEBULA_NO_ASSET_REHOME=1`; without it the next start moves them again. The test conftest sets it too.
- **Decisions not in the brief.**
  - A project in Recently deleted is refused on create (422), not accepted: a Project tab can't show it, so the asset would be invisible until a restore.
  - Folders named after trashed canvas projects aren't legacy: those assets are already filed right and come back with the project.
  - The state file (`<state>/migrations/asset-project-rehome.json`, `{version: 2, knownSkips}`) only remembers skips: each by file path, size and mtime, so the same collision is logged once, a changed file is logged again, and the move happens on the first start after the collision is gone. It's emptied once nothing old-style is left. A version-1 marker (run-once, from this branch's first commit) reads as no known skips.
  - The re-home changes nothing while the catalog can't be read, and waits while there are old-style assets and a live canvas but the catalog has no projects yet (an install that hasn't saved its canvas as a project). Otherwise every board would go to Global just because the first project didn't exist yet.
  - A collision (same id already in the target) is skipped and logged, never overwritten. A move stopped half-way (target written, source left) finishes on the next run.
  - "No project open" follows `initialized && activeProject`, not the Home screen: Home with a project still loaded in memory keeps it current, which matches the catalog's `activeProjectId` the CLI reads.
  - The ws `storedAssetChanged` relist was added to the Assets panel and both rails, so a board the CLI files into the open project shows without a reload.
  - P4 ("Move to Global / Move to <project>") isn't built here. Its seam is `asset_project_rehome.move_asset(kind, root, source, target)`: moves one asset file between scopes, refuses a collision, finishes a half-done move, changes only `projectId` (and a preset's `scope`).
- **Docs.** `docs/contracts/07-studios-and-resources.md` (new 1.9, after #83 took 1.8 for the dry run; changelog), `skills/nebula/SKILL.md`, `docs/MCP-SETUP.md`, the `moodboard_list` / `moodboard_create` descriptions and `nebula moodboard --project` help. `nebula moodboard list` and `show` (and `analyze`) now print a board's project by name with a short id, `project Shoot A (5f3c1a2b…)`, adding ", in Recently deleted" for a trashed project, and fall back to the id when the name isn't known (`moodboard_client.project_names`).
- **Tests.** Backend: `test_asset_project_rehome.py` (13, several cases each: R1 one/two/no/only-trashed project, Styles to Global, the open canvas counts, trashed asset and record re-homed and restorable, canvas and trashed-project folders untouched with nothing written, a collision skipped and logged once then moved when it clears, a later old-folder asset re-homed on the next start with no backup on the quiet start between, a run-once marker still re-homes, roots from the stores' own resolvers, unreadable catalog, waits for the first project, a fresh install writes nothing, half-done move, startup log line once). On the previous commit's module 7 of the 13 fail, `test_project_context.py` rewritten (10, including `test_a_node_copied_into_another_project_still_runs_and_edits_its_asset`: the Moodboard and Character handlers read Shoot A's assets with Shoot B open, and PUTs from B keep them in A), a `canvas_project` fixture for the route tests, `test_moodboard_cli.py::test_a_board_for_a_project_that_does_not_exist_is_refused` and `::test_list_and_show_name_the_boards_project`. Clipboard: 6 new in `tests/graphStore.projects.test.ts` (Cmd+C in A, load B, Cmd+V adds the nodes and their edge with params intact and outputs cleared, undo in B removes them; an ambiguity at copy time refuses after the switch; B's checkpoint for its own `n1` never lands on A's pasted `n1`; A's checkpoint travels; a blank paid World Labs node refuses here and after a switch; a round trip back to A uses the copy-time params), 3 placement tests there (a foreign paste lands in the view clear of B's nodes with its layout kept though the view's middle is taken; on a free centre exactly centred; a same-load paste is +20 px whatever the view; the first two fail with the old +20 offset) and 5 in `tests/lib/nodePlacement.group.test.ts` (centred when free, layout kept; clear and close by; empty canvas; a clear spot in view preferred to a nearer one outside; no spot in view gives the nearest clear one), and the existing load test now expects the clipboard kept. With paste re-checking against the open canvas after a switch (only `clipboard: null` removed), the ambiguity and same-id checkpoint tests fail; with the previous graphStore (clipboard cleared on load) 7 of the 18 tests in the file fail. On the base backend 5 of the 10 project-context tests fail (`/api/project` returns `{'id': 'base', 'name': 'base'}`; unknown and trashed ids save with 200); the re-home tests can't import there. Frontend: `CharacterStudioView.test.tsx` (5; with `shownRailScope` put back to `railScope` the kept-draft test fails), `StoredAssetCards.test.tsx` (another project's board and Character show on their cards and open the Studio), 4 new in `MoodboardStudioView.test.tsx` (other project's board, unknown project name, no project, a draft never saved into the newly opened project), 2 in `AssetsPanel.test.tsx` (relist on switch, no project), `currentProject.test.ts` rewritten. ## 2026-10-19 — Where a board's colours come from, and a dry-run analyze

- **What was wrong.** Each entry in `analysis.colors[]` said only `images: <count>`, so nobody (the person in Moodboard Studio, an agent through the CLI) could tell which image a palette colour or accent came from, and why the brand orange showed up or didn't. Trying other colour thresholds meant editing Commons' constants and analyzing for real, which saves.
- **Cause.** `_roll_up` kept `_Swatch.images` (index to the image's weight part) only to rank accents and threw away which image each colour came from. The thresholds were module constants read inside `commons/measure.py`.
- **Fix.**
  - *Provenance.* `_Swatch` has a separate `sources` (image index to the colour's share of that image), summed when two swatches from one image merge; `images` and the accent sort key are untouched. Each board colour lists `sources` (`number`, `id`, `share`, `contribution`), sorted by contribution then number. `number` counts every image in board order, excluded ones included, as `find_image` / `nebula moodboard show` / the Studio grid do. `analysis.images[]` gets `number`.
  - *Dry run.* `POST /api/moodboards/{id}/analyze/dry-run` with optional `{thresholds: {accentMinChroma, accentSeparation, mergeDeltaE}}` runs `moodboard_analysis.dry_run`: the analysis, `compose()` with it, and `changes` (palette and accents added, removed, nudged, reordered; the brief, generated brief and negatives before and after) against the saved analysis and brief, plus `saved: {analyzed, current}`. It never writes or broadcasts. `measure_image` takes the three thresholds as keyword overrides (None = the module constant, read at call time); `_measure_file`'s lru_cache key includes them; the roll-up's merge and accent-drop use the override `merge_delta_e`. `parse_thresholds` checks names and ranges (chroma 0-150, separation 0-100, merge 0-50; finite numbers only, no bools or strings).
  - CLI: `show` prints each palette/accent colour with share and sources (`#4 0.35%, #5 0.26%`); `analyze --dry-run [--accent-min-chroma N --accent-separation N --merge-delta-e N] [--json]` with a readable summary; thresholds without `--dry-run` are refused. MCP `moodboard_analyze(dry_run, accent_min_chroma, accent_separation, merge_delta_e)`.
  - Studio: `MoodboardColors.tsx` (`BoardSwatches`, `ImageColors`, `SourcesOutdated`; helpers in `colorSources.ts`). Board swatches show hex, share and "#3, #7 +2", with the full list (share of the image, share of the board) on hover or focus. Each image card shows its own colours with shares (accents as round swatches) and a `#N` badge so the numbers can be read off the grid.
- **Decisions not in the brief.**
  - *ANALYSIS_VERSION 3 to 4.* The shape changed (new fields), so the version says so; `source_hash` hashes the same payload for v2 on, so v3 analyses stay current and boards don't go stale. Without `sources`, the Studio shows the colours with their share and "Analyze again to see which images each color comes from"; the CLI prints the plain hex lists and the same advice with the command.
  - *A route of its own, not `dryRun` on `/analyze`.* An older backend ignores a body it doesn't know, so a flag sent there would analyze and save. The new route is a 404 there, and the client turns FastAPI's "Not Found" into "this version of Nebula has no dry run ... nothing was analyzed or saved" rather than falling back.
  - *`nudged`.* Thresholds move merged centres a little, so exact-hex diffs would read as remove + add. A removed and an added colour within dE00 2 pair up as `nudged` (closest first); `reordered` compares the lists with nudged colours standing for their old selves.
  - *What isn't a threshold.* `moodboard_brief.without_excluded` uses `MERGE_DELTA_E` for the pinned "keep out" rule; that's the person's colour rule, not the analysis, so the dry run leaves it alone.
  - *The tile number badge* is one line inside `.moodboard-tile__image`; the card colours are one `<ImageColors>` line after it, to keep the merge with the parallel note/autosize branch small.
- **Defaults unchanged (gap #20 on hold).** `tests/test_moodboard_defaults_pin.py` pins palette, accents, `colors` (hex, share, role, images), the analysis brief, negatives, keywords, summary, per-image colours and the composed brief on four generated boards (accent, brand with excluded and weight-0 images, near shades, busy). The fixture `tests/fixtures/moodboard_defaults_pin.json` was written by the old code (bf488a80) and passes unchanged on the new code. `NEBULA_REPIN_MOODBOARD=1` re-pins when gap #20 lands.

Backend suite 6955: 6949 passed, 6 failed under load (5 agent guardian/process timing tests, which pass alone, and `test_every_tool_is_annotated_and_the_instructions_name_real_tools`, which caught `dry_run` named in the MCP instructions; reworded).
