## 2026-10-19 — Moodboard Studio: links, opening without editing the canvas, private notes, growing notes, an honest rail

GM - Design's notes from a real board, and Justin's asks, in one PR (branch `fix/moodboard-studio-open`).

- **What was wrong.** (1) No way to link to a board. (2) In the Assets panel a single click on a Moodboard or Character *added a node*, and double-click (to open) fired two clicks first, so opening a board added two nodes. (3) The Moodboard node opened only from its Open button, shown while selected. (4) No place for the person's own labels ("PAINTERLY (liked)"): the image note steers the analysis, so using it for labels changed the brief. (5) The image note (`rows=2`) and board Notes (`rows=3`) clipped longer text. (6) The rail showed the Project tab with "No Moodboards yet." while a Global board was open.
- **Cause of (6).** `railScope` was a `useState` seeded from the scope the Studio was opened with, and only the fetch path set it to the board's real scope. When the board's draft was already in the draft store (a second visit this session), the Studio loaded it without a fetch and the rail kept the hint's scope. Repro: open a Global board, go back, open it again with a `project` hint (or a project board twice from a node, whose Open button always says Global): the rail shows the wrong tab, and the empty list says "No Moodboards yet.".
- **Fix.**
  - *Link:* `hooks/useMoodboardDeepLink.ts` (used in App.tsx after the `#brand` route): `#moodboard/<id>` opens the Studio with the default hint (the Studio moves to the board's scope); hashchange too; while the Studio shows a saved board the hash follows it with `replaceState`; leaving clears it; clearing the hash leaves the Studio. An unknown id gets the Studio's own "Moodboard not found" message.
  - *Assets panel:* one model for all three tabs (`AssetItem`): click / Enter / Space selects (`aria-pressed`, accent border, focus ring) and shows Open and Add to canvas; double-click opens; drag still adds. Add to canvas places the node at the middle of the view, clear of other nodes (`findAvailableNodePosition`, as the Nodes panel does) instead of the old fixed `{400,300}`.
  - *Node double-click:* `nodes/useOpenOnDoubleClick.ts`, used by MoodboardNode and CharacterNode (CharacterNode had the same selected-only Open button). A native `dblclick` listener on the card stops the event before React Flow's pane sees it: the pane zooms on double-click (`zoomOnDoubleClick` is on, default), and a React handler runs only after the pane's listener, so it couldn't stop that. Ports, buttons and inputs keep their own double-click. No `onNodeDoubleClick` exists in Canvas.tsx, and neither card uses `NodeLabel`, so rename-on-double-click doesn't apply.
  - *Private note:* `images[].privateNote` (store normalization, 2000-character limit, `""` for boards saved before it, `PRIVATE_IMAGE_KEYS` / `without_private`). `source_hash` and the analysis already listed their fields, so they never read it; the node handler strips it from the bundle's images (which also reach Krea 2's native-moodboard path); the brief never read image fields. Studio: `updateImage` keeps the analysis when only `privateNote` changes; each card has "Image note" and "Private note" fields, the second dashed, with "Only for you. Not sent anywhere." Client/CLI/MCP: `--private-note IMAGE=TEXT`, `privateNote` in `moodboard_update` image edits, in `brief()` (so `show --json`, `moodboard_get`), and in `previous`; human `show` prints `Private note (not sent anywhere): "..."`. `update_board` compares images without private notes, so a label-only change keeps the analysis.
  - *Growing notes:* `components/AutoGrowTextarea.tsx` measures `scrollHeight` (box-sizing aware) up to the CSS `max-height` (260px Notes, 180px image notes), then scrolls; re-measures when the text or the width changes. Script, not `field-sizing: content`, which Safari lacks.
  - *Rail:* the Studio derives `boardScope` from the open saved board's own `projectId` and keys the rail on it, so the rail opens on the board's scope however it was loaded. Empty states say which scope is empty, and where the open board is when it's the other one: "No project moodboards. This board is Global." (`moodboard-studio/railEmpty.ts`).
- **Decisions not in the brief.**
  - A link that loads the app goes past the Projects screen into the already-loaded open project (`projectStore.open(activeId)`, which only shows a loaded project; same as clicking its card). With no open project it waits there, and opens once the person opens one. The app otherwise always starts on Projects, so without this a link did nothing on load.
  - The hash follows `moodboardEditorId`, so an unknown id keeps its hash while the not-found message shows; saving a new board there moves the hash to the new id. A new draft (`new` sentinel) clears it.
  - Styles follow the same model as the other tabs (click selects, double-click or "Use in Create" opens Create), since a single click there also left the canvas.
  - Private note limit 2000 characters (the image note has none); the store refuses longer, the Studio stops typing there.
  - `brief()` (agents' view of the board) includes `privateNote`, and the MCP descriptions and SKILL.md tell agents to read it but never put it in a prompt: it's inspection, which the brief allows. Commons import copies only board notes, so it never sees it.
  - Setting a private note on a backend whose images have none is refused client-side ("this version of Nebula has no private notes"), since the backend's image model forbids unknown fields.
- **Docs.** `skills/nebula/SKILL.md`, `docs/MCP-SETUP.md`, the MCP server instructions and tool descriptions, `docs/contracts/07-studios-and-resources.md` (1.1 image fields, 1.6, new 1.7, changelog).
- **Tests.** Backend `tests/test_moodboard_private_note.py` (11): store keep/limit/old boards, not an analysis input (`source_hash` v1 and v2, `brief_basis`, the analysis JSON), keeps the analysis, not in the composed brief or negative prompt, not in node outputs, Studio-style PUT keeps the analysis, CLI set/show/JSON/restore, a steering change with it still clears, MCP update/get/undo, older backend. On the original backend 8 fail (3 no-leak tests pass there because the old store dropped the field); with the leak put back (handler without `without_private`, `privateNote` in `source_hash` and the per-image analysis) 4 fail. Frontend: `AssetsPanel.test.tsx` (8; on the original panel the click/double-click tests fail with `addMoodboardNode` / `addCharacterNode` called 1 and 2 times), `MoodboardStudioView.test.tsx` (4; on the original view the two rail tests fail with the wrong tab selected; with `updateImage` clearing the analysis again the private-note test fails), `useOpenOnDoubleClick.test.tsx` (3; without the native `stopPropagation` the pane's zoom fires), `useMoodboardDeepLink.test.tsx` (8), `AutoGrowTextarea.test.tsx` (1). `tests/components/AssetsPanel.test.tsx` now renders the panel in a `ReactFlowProvider`, as App.tsx does.
- **Live check** (isolated backend 8811, Vite 5811, Puppeteer, 43/43; ports 8000-8010 and the Vite proxy blocked by CDP and watched, 0 requests). Request interception made this Chrome fail every cross-origin call to 8811 (`net::ERR_FAILED`), so the second layer was a request watcher instead. Assets single click adds nothing and selects, keyboard focus reaches the item, double-click opens the board / the Character with the graph unchanged (project snapshot, `/api/graph` and the canvas store compared byte for byte), Add to canvas and a drag each add one node. Node double-click opens the Studio at zoom 3.43 and at 0.38 (`data-lod="low"`), the zoom unchanged after (a double-click on the empty pane still zooms 0.38 → 0.77); the Open button opens; graph unchanged. Rail: Global tab for a Global board, also re-entered with a project hint; the empty Project tab reads "No project moodboards. This board is Global."; a project board shows Project. Link: a full load of `/?fresh=1#moodboard/<id>` opens that board on the Global tab; picking another board in the rail updates the hash with no new history entry; Back to Canvas clears it; a hashchange opens a board; an unknown id shows "Moodboard not found. Add images to save a new one."; clearing the hash leaves the Studio. Private note: saved, analysis kept and still shown, not in `brief` or the analysis, not in the node's outputs after a run, still there after a reload. Notes: board Notes grew past 3 lines to show 6, the image note grew to fit, then stopped at 180px and scrolled. Screenshots in the scratch `live/shots/`.
- **Found, not fixed.** (1) Character Studio has the same `railScope` pattern and the same bug. (2) Moodboard Studio's Project scope is `/api/project` (the backend's working-folder project, e.g. `nebula_nodes-moodboard-studio`), not the canvas project, while `nebula moodboard new --project current` uses the canvas project's id (`activeProjectId`). A board the CLI makes for the current project never shows in the Studio's (or the Assets panel's) Project tab; it opens fine by link or node, but the rail then shows an empty Project tab with the board open. (3) React Flow zooms on any double-click on other nodes too (`zoomOnDoubleClick` default); only these two cards stop it.

## 2026-10-19 — Fit view shows the pictures; only the person's tab saves the view; the Nodes panel opens on empty canvases (design-canvas gap 19; V1, V2)

- **What was wrong.** Below 40% zoom the canvas hid every node preview (`[data-lod='low'] .model-node__preview`). Fit view on GM's 20-node project lands at 36%, so the overview meant for comparing branches showed titles only. Two more things showed up from a tab that isn't connected as the person: zooming there marked the project unsaved and saved that tab's view over the person's, and every project opened with the Nodes panel out over the canvas.
- **Cause.** The 0.4 cutoff came with the June large-graph work (`docs/research-2026-06/quick-wins-build-plan.md`) as a guess, and it hid images along with players and labels. The viewport went into every snapshot save from any tab. `resetPanelsForFreshCanvas` always set `leftDock: 'library'`.
- **Fix: thumbnails.** `GET /api/outputs/<rel>?thumb=1` (`services/output_thumbnail.py`) returns a copy at most 512 px on the long edge (Pillow LANCZOS, EXIF-rotated, JPEG q80, or PNG when there's alpha, never enlarged). Videos get a still at 0.1 s through `qc_common.extract_frames`. Thumbnails are cached in `<state>/thumbnails`, keyed by sha256 of version, edge, path, size and mtime, so a changed file gets a new one. The cache trims the least recently used down to 90% past 4000 files, and at most 4 are made at once per event loop. Formats it can't read and broken files return 415; paths outside the outputs root keep returning 404. On the canvas, `ZoomLodController` publishes `canvasZoomedOut` (set only when it changes). `OverviewImage` swaps an image's src for `overviewThumbnailUrl(src)` while zoomed out and falls back to the file if the thumbnail fails. `OverviewVideoStill` lays the still over the hidden player. Only Nebula's own `/api/outputs/` files get thumbnails (relative, loopback or same-origin URLs, raster and video suffixes); SVG, external, data: and blob: URLs keep their src. The CSS keeps `.model-node__preview--overview` visible at low detail and hides the rest as before, plus the video player, its download and loop buttons, and port labels.
- **Fix: V1, the saved view (my pick, pending Justin).** Only the person's tab saves the project's view. Backend: `_keep_person_viewport` puts the stored viewport back into any save or handoff that isn't `_is_person_request()`. Frontend: `holdsPersonCredential()` (`lib/personSession.ts`) decides whether the live viewport goes into the snapshot. Without it the snapshot carries the view as loaded, so zooming in such a tab never marks the project unsaved.
- **Fix: V2, the Nodes panel (my pick, pending Justin).** A project with nodes opens with the Nodes panel closed; an empty canvas opens with it out. `resetPanelsForFreshCanvas({ canvasEmpty })` takes that from `applyProject`.
- **Found in the live check.** (1) `useHomeSettingsDock` puts the dock from before Home back when you leave Home with no dock open, which reopened the Nodes panel on every project opened from Home. `uiStore.panelsResetRevision` now counts fresh-canvas resets, and the hook leaves the drawer alone when one happened while Home was up: the new canvas decides. (2) The reset set `leftDock: null` but left `panels.library.visible` at its default `true`, so the panel still showed while the store said closed (the rail and `data-dock-open` read `leftDock`). `withLeftDock()` now derives every dock panel's visibility from `leftDock`, and `setLeftDock`, `togglePanel` and the reset all use it, so the two can't disagree.
- **Decisions not in the brief.** (1) Fit view still fits everything; clamping its zoom above 0.4 would stop it fitting. (2) The 0.4 cutoff stays, and so does Settings' "Low detail when zoomed out" (off shows everything at full size, as before). (3) Crossing the cutoff re-renders the image components once through `canvasZoomedOut`. The June plan's LOD aimed for no per-node re-render, but swapping a src needs one, and only on the crossing. (4) A video-input node shows no preview until it has run; that's how main behaves too, and it's left as is. When it has run, its output shows the player, and the still when zoomed out.
- **Tests.** Backend: `test_output_thumbnails.py` (10: made once and cached, plain requests get the original, alpha stays PNG, no enlarging, a changed file gets a new thumbnail, 415 for text and a broken PNG, containment, video still, video failure, cache trim). `test_projects.py`: `test_only_the_persons_tab_saves_the_view`, and two existing tests now send the person's headers. `test_project_switching.py`: a non-person save during a handoff keeps the viewport. Frontend: `canvasOverview.test.ts`, `OverviewImage.test.tsx`, two saved-view tests in `projectStore.autosave.test.ts`, two Nodes-panel tests in `projectStore.switch.test.ts` (both check `panels.library.visible` too), and two in `useHomeSettingsDock.test.ts`. The Home test fails on the old hook (`expected 'library' to be null`); the panel assertions fail on the old reset. Backend suite 6938 passed; frontend 3093 passed (a first run under load average 41 timed out 60 tests, and the rerun passed them all).
- **Live check** on an isolated backend (8795) and Vite (5795), with ports 8000-8010 and the Vite proxy blocked and nothing reaching them. A project with twelve 1600 px PNGs and a run video-input, opened from Home in a tab without the person link, gave 12/12 checks. The Nodes panel stayed closed (store and DOM), at load and after zooming. Fit view landed at 0.34 (low detail) with all 12 images showing as 512 px `?thumb=1` copies and the video's 512 px still over its hidden player. Zoomed in to 0.49, the images were the files themselves and the still was gone. No "Unsaved changes", the saved view unchanged, 13 thumbnails cached, all 200s.

## 2026-10-19 — Agents see and set a board's brief through the CLI and MCP (#73 x #76)

- **What was wrong.** `moodboard_client.brief()`, which `nebula moodboard ... --json` and every `moodboard_*` MCP tool return, listed only settings, images and the analysis. It dropped `direction`, `avoid`, `pinnedColors`, `briefOverride` and the computed `brief` the API adds to every board. Agents read `analysis.styleBrief` and `analysis.negativePrompt` as the board's brief, but generators get `compose()`'s result: the override when there is one, Direction and pinned colours in the text, `DEFECT_NEGATIVES` + Avoid as negatives. Worst on migrated boards, whose edited briefs moved to `briefOverride` and extra negatives to `avoid`. `update_board()` had no way to set any of it, and human `show` printed the analysis's text as "Brief".
- **Cause.** #73 (CLI/MCP) and #76 (brief fields) landed in parallel; #76's notes left "CLI commands (another lane)", and #73 was written before the fields existed.
- **Fix.** `brief()` adds `direction`, `avoid`, `pinnedColors`, `briefOverride` (`text`, `by`, `updatedAt`, `stale`, with `stale` read from the backend's `brief.override`) and `brief`, passed on exactly as the backend sent it; `null` when an older backend sends none, never `analysis.styleBrief` instead. `update_board()` takes `direction` (`""` clears), `avoid` (replace) / `avoid_add` / `avoid_remove`, `pinned_colors` (replace) / `pin_colors` / `keep_out_colors` / `unpin_colors`, `brief_override` (`""` = generated) and `keep_brief`. `nebula moodboard set` gets `--direction`, `--avoid`, `--unavoid`, `--clear-avoid`, `--pin-color`, `--keep-out-color`, `--unpin-color`, `--brief`, `--clear-brief`, `--keep-brief`; `moodboard_update` gets the same as parameters. Human `show` prints Direction, Avoid, both colour lists, "Brief sent to generators (generated | written by an agent | written by the person)" with the composed text, a stale line (Keep/clear hint for an agent's text, "only they can" for the person's), the negative prompt and the Avoid sentence; the analysis block no longer prints its own Brief/Avoid.
- **Validation.** The client checks with the backend's own functions (`services/moodboard_brief.normalize_*`, same limits: 40 Avoid items of 200 characters, hex colours, 12 per list, no colour on both lists, Direction 4000, override 20000) before sending, and fails with the reason; nothing is truncated. Removing an Avoid item or colour that isn't there is an error naming what is there, like `find_image`.
- **403.** The backend's refusal (person gate + store sentence) becomes a `MoodboardError`, so the CLI prints `error: The person wrote this board's brief by hand, ...` and MCP returns that text. The gate's `person_required` text ("This tab isn't: open the link the backend printed...") is dropped: it's canvas advice, and the CLI without `NEBULA_AGENT_NAME` gets that variant.
- **Decisions not in the brief.** (1) Keep is in: `--keep-brief` / `keep_brief` call `POST .../brief-override/keep`, because otherwise an agent that changes the board after writing its own brief leaves a "changed since" badge it can't clear; the backend still refuses it on the person's text. (2) Analysis is cleared only when images, notes, mode or strength actually change value. Before, any `notes`/`strength`/`images` argument cleared it, so undoing a brief-only change with `previous` (which carries every setting) would have thrown the analysis away. (3) `previous` keys use update_board's argument names (`pinned_colors`, `brief_override`), so it passes back as is; `brief_override` is the agent's own text or `""`, there only when the change touched the override (see Review pass). Restoring an agent's text after it changed restamps its basis, so a restored stale override comes back not stale. (4) `analysis` stays whole in the output (`styleBrief` included); the tool descriptions, SKILL.md and MCP-SETUP say `brief.styleBrief` is what generators get and `analysis.styleBrief` is not. (5) Colour flags are `--pin-color` / `--keep-out-color` / `--unpin-color` because `--include` / `--exclude` already mean images; the wording follows Studio's "Colors that must appear" / "Colors to keep out".
- **Docs.** `skills/nebula/SKILL.md` (also lists the node's `moodboard` output), `docs/MCP-SETUP.md`, the MCP server's instructions and the `moodboard_get` / `moodboard_list` / `moodboard_update` / `moodboard_analyze` descriptions, and `docs/contracts/07-studios-and-resources.md` section 1.6.
- **Tests.** 19 new in `backend/tests/test_moodboard_cli.py` (brief fields and composed brief, older backend, override author and stale + Keep, Direction/Avoid add-remove-replace, colours, 7 validation cases with nothing saved, agent override set/clear, the person's brief refused in client/CLI/MCP, the `previous` round trip for brief fields and with the person's brief, CLI `set`/`show` JSON and human, `show` on an older backend, MCP get/list/update and undo). All 19 fail on main (`TypeError: update_board() got an unexpected keyword argument 'direction'`, `KeyError: 'brief'`, `moodboard_update() got an unexpected keyword argument 'direction'`).
- **Live check** on an isolated backend (port 8851, temp HOME and NEBULA_* paths): `nebula moodboard new` from two PNGs, `analyze`, `set --direction "Quiet coastal mornings" --avoid "neon signage" --avoid "lens flare" --pin-color "#E8593C" --keep-out-color "#0000FF"`; `show` printed all of them and a brief starting "Quiet coastal mornings." with "Make sure these colors appear: #e8593c."; a `nebula-moodboard` node run returned `direction`, `avoid`, `pinnedColors.include ["#e8593c"]`, the same `styleBrief`, and `negativePrompt "blurry, low-detail artifacts, neon signage, lens flare"`. Agent `--brief`, then a board change showed the stale line, `--keep-brief` cleared it. Pin + keep out the same colour and `--unavoid` of a missing item failed with their reasons. Through `mcp_server` against the same backend: a change to Direction, Avoid, pins and the agent's brief, then `moodboard_update(**previous)` put all four back with the analysis kept. With a person-written brief in the store, `--brief` and `--keep-brief` printed the store's sentence and exited 1; `show` said "written by the person" and "Only they can keep or replace it"; `set --json`'s `previous` had no `brief_override`.
- **Review pass.** (1) `keep_brief` with other changes sent the PUT, then Keep; a refused Keep (the person's brief, 403; no brief, 409) left the PUT saved and the caller with an error and no `previous`. Keep can't go first (the basis it stamps includes Direction, Avoid and pins), so `update_board` now checks it before sending anything, from the board it already read and the body: no override after the change, or the person's, is a `MoodboardError` ending "Nothing was changed"; new text in the same call skips Keep (it's stamped fresh). (2) `previous` carried `brief_override: ""` whenever the board had no override, so if the person wrote one between an agent's change and its undo, the undo (a single PUT) was refused whole. It now carries `brief_override` only when the change touched the override. (3) If the person replaced an agent's brief after the agent changed it, putting the agent's text back is still the person's call: the client now refuses before sending, says nothing was changed and to leave `brief_override` out, rather than skipping it silently (an explicit `--brief` on the person's text must be refused too, and the two calls look the same). Contract 1.6, MCP-SETUP, SKILL.md and the `moodboard_update` description say so. Tests: `test_keep_brief_is_checked_before_anything_is_saved`, `test_previous_leaves_the_brief_alone_when_the_change_didnt_touch_it`, `test_an_undo_that_would_replace_the_persons_new_brief_changes_nothing_and_says_how`; all three fail before the fix (`brief_override` in `previous`; the backend's 403 instead of "Nothing was changed"; Direction saved after a refused Keep).
- **Review pass (live check, round 1).** (1) A refused Keep of the person's brief reused the replace sentence ("the board keeps no history, and their text would be lost"), which is wrong for Keep: keeping loses nothing. Keep now has its own reason in the client and in the store: only the person can keep their brief, because keeping clears their notice that the board changed since they wrote it. The store's `_guard_override(..., "mark as kept")` also read "an agent can't mark as kept it"; it passes `"keep"` now and gets that sentence. (2) When the person writes their brief after the call read the board, the backend's 403 is what stops it, and its text is API copy ("Leave briefOverride out of the request"). The client now knows that refusal by its opening (`services/moodboard_store.PERSON_BRIEF_REFUSED`) and replaces it with the CLI/MCP sentence for that request (the PUT names `brief_override (--brief, --clear-brief)`, Keep names `keep_brief (--keep-brief)`); other 403s pass through as before. A Keep refused after the PUT of the same call saved the other changes, so that message says "The other changes were saved; the brief wasn't kept" instead of "Nothing was changed" (that call returns no `previous`; it needs the person to write in the few milliseconds between the read and the Keep). Contract 1.6 says both. Tests: `test_a_refused_keep_gives_the_keep_reason`, `test_a_backend_refusal_in_a_race_reads_as_cli_and_mcp_wording` (`test_moodboard_cli.py`, the race made by handing `update_board` the board as read before the person wrote) and a Keep-reason check in `test_an_agent_cannot_replace_remove_or_keep_the_persons_brief`; all three fail before the fix (the replace sentence for Keep; "Leave briefOverride out of the request"; "can't mark as kept it").
- **Final pass (coordinator).** The completeness check left three small gaps, closed here. (1) SKILL.md said to put `previous` back "with the same flags", which the CLI couldn't do in one step (no flag replaces both colour lists). Now `nebula moodboard set <board> --restore <file>` (`-` for stdin) sends a saved `previous`, or the whole `set --json` output, back as one change. It refuses other change flags alongside it, and keys `previous` never has (`moodboard_client.RESTORE_KEYS`). (2) A Keep refused after the other changes were saved (the person wrote or removed the brief while the call ran) now hands back `previous` for the saved part. That's `MoodboardError.previous`; the MCP error text carries it as JSON, and the CLI prints it on stderr with the `--restore` line. A 409 there (the brief was removed) reads in CLI words, not "send briefOverride with PUT". (3) `--clear-avoid` with `--unavoid` is refused up front, as `--brief` with `--clear-brief` already was. Tests: 4 new tests (8 cases) in `test_moodboard_cli.py`. All 8 fail on the lane's earlier head 552d0147, checked on an exported copy. A read-only review of this pass found two more defects, fixed here. (a) After a `set` with `--remove`, `previous` still listed the removed image, so `--restore` (or `moodboard_update` with `previous`) stopped before saving anything with "no image ... (1-0)". `previous` now leaves out images the change took off, which come back from `removed` (`nebula moodboard add`), as #73 designed, and a board with no images says so. (b) The CLI's restore line repeated the board as typed, which breaks after a rename or with a space in the name. `MoodboardError.board_id` now carries the id, printed through `shlex.quote`. Also, a Keep that got no answer (connect or timeout) now says the brief may or may not have been kept, not that it wasn't. 3 more tests; all fail on 552d0147. Backend suite: 6922 passed before this round; the moodboard CLI file has 61 tests and all pass.

## 2026-10-19 — A canvas finishing an agent's arrange joins the agent's undo step (#75 x #78)

- **What was wrong.** When an agent's edit asked for `arrange`, the canvas laid the new nodes out and wrote them back (`completeArrange`, `PUT /api/graph/layout` with `arrangeId`). The backend broadcast that write as a graph edit by the person's tab. Every other open tab made it a second undo step, credited to the person, so undoing the agent's edit there took two presses. The tab that arranged skipped it as its own echo, but the agent's step had been recorded before the arrange, so its `after` held the stacked positions: Undo then Redo put the nodes back stacked, and the redo's restore wrote those positions to the backend.
- **Cause.** `update_graph_layout` called `_broadcast_graph_sync(edit=True, ...)` for every write, arrange or not, and `_graph_edit_origin()` takes the actor and tab from the request, which here is the person's canvas.
- **Fix.** Backend: when the person's canvas (`is_person`: this launch's token, no agent marker) finishes an arrange, the graphSync carries `arranged: {id, nodeIds}` and `moved`, and no `edit`. Frontend: `foldFinishedArrange` (graphStore) reads that marker and `foldArrange` (lib/canvasUndo.ts) puts the arranged positions into the `after` of the foreign step that added those nodes (the newest such step, on either stack), and into every later step that still holds the old positions. No tab makes a step of it and no "changed the canvas" notice shows. A tab with no such step (opened after the edit, or the step fell off `UNDO_CAP`) just takes the positions.
- **Decisions not in the brief.**
  - *Later steps get the positions too.* The brief named only the agent's step. But a person's edit made after the agent's edit and before the arrange landed is a whole-canvas snapshot holding the stacked positions, so undoing it would put the agent's nodes back stacked (and write that to the backend). `foldArrange` rewrites a node's position in every later step where it still equals the position before the arrange; any other position (someone moved it on purpose) is left alone.
  - *A step already undone.* If the person undid the agent's edit before the arrange landed, the backend skips nodes that are gone (and closes the request once none are left), so usually nothing arrives. If the arrange wins the race, the step is on the redo stack and gets folded there, so Redo brings the nodes back arranged.
  - *History entries change in place.* The undo notice's Undo button and a refused restore find their step by identity, so `foldArrange` edits the entries rather than replacing them. Nothing renders their contents.
  - *Only the person's write folds; anyone else's stays an edit.* The arrangeId rides on every graphSync, so an agent or a script can send it. Their write keeps the old path: a normal `edit`, credited to whoever wrote it, its own undo step, no `arranged`. The fold path therefore gives a non-person nothing it didn't have before. Even for the person's write, it can only carry positions of the request's own new nodes, once (first write wins), and the fold only changes positions of nodes the request named. A canvas tab without the person link also counts as a script here, so its arrange stays a separate "outside" step, the same as every other edit from such a tab.
  - *Journal unchanged.* `node.moved` still credits the agent that asked (or the agent that wrote it, per the 2026-10-18 audit).
- **Other consumers checked.** Nothing on the backend reads graphSync `edit` or `moved` (CLI watchers and the MCP read the journal; agent presence and pins act on `graphReplaced`/`empty`). projectStore reads only the version, revision and `projectSwitch`; desktop only the event type. The canvas still takes the positions through `moved` as before. Docs: `docs/MCP-SETUP.md` (arrange and undo sections) and `services/canvas_arrange.py`. No contract under `docs/contracts/` describes graphSync.
- **Tests.** Backend `test_graph_apply.py`: `test_the_canvas_finishing_an_arrange_is_not_a_new_edit` (no `edit`, `arranged` set, journal credits the agent, a plain drag still an edit; fails on main: `assert 'edit' not in {... 'edit': {'actor': {'kind': 'person'}, 'tab': 'tab_arranging01'} ...}`) and `test_an_arrange_written_by_anyone_but_the_person_stays_an_edit` (agent and tokenless writes; passes on main, guards the trust rule). Frontend `graphStore.arrangeUndo.test.ts` (6): the other tab and the arranging tab (via `completeArrange`) each end with one step credited to Claude, no new notice, and Undo then Redo leaves the nodes arranged with the redo restore carrying the arranged positions; a person edit between the two keeps arranged positions when undone; a step already undone redoes to arranged; a tab without the step just takes positions; a drag from another window stays its own step. Four fail on main (`expected { x: 1000, y: +0 } to deeply equal { x: 1200, y: 40 }`).
- **Live check.** Isolated backend (8797, with the person link) and Vite (5797), two person tabs in headless Chrome, ports 8000-8010, 5173 and the Vite proxy blocked (zero attempts). An agent applies three nodes stacked at one spot with `arrange`; a tab lays them out. Round 1 undoes and redoes in the tab that didn't arrange, round 2 in the tab that did. On this branch 17/17: both tabs keep the agent's notice, one Undo removes the nodes on the canvas and the backend, and Redo puts them back arranged on both. The same script on main (1b2b2eed): 14/17. In the other tab the first Undo only moved the nodes back (two presses needed), and in the arranging tab Redo brought them back stacked at (600, 600), on the canvas and the backend.
- **Second live check (independent).** A separate run on its own ports (backend 8793 / Vite 5793 for this branch, 8794 / 5794 for main), same isolation, zero blocked attempts. This branch passed 36/36, main 17/36. On main the arrange's sync carries `edit {actor person, tab}` and no `arranged`. In the tab that didn't arrange it adds a second step credited to no agent, so the first Cmd-Z only puts the nodes back stacked.

## 2026-10-18 — Studios open a board or character in the scope it lives in

- **What a lane saw.** Double-clicking a board under the Assets panel's Project tab, in a tab without the person link, left Moodboard Studio on "Loading Moodboard...". An isolated repro (backend 8793, Vite 5793, 8000-8010 and the Vite proxy blocked, zero hits) didn't show a spinner that stays. The same trigger was worse: the studio said "Moodboard not found. Add images to save a new one." over an empty board, and adding images there would have made a second board. A tab with the person link behaved the same way.
- **Cause.** The studios looked the record up in the list for the scope they were opened with, so a record opened under the other scope looked missing. Two ways in: the Moodboard and Character nodes' open buttons (and the stored-asset picker) pass no scope, which defaults to Global, so every project board or character opened from its node showed as missing; and the Assets panel set a list even after the tab or scope changed, so a slow Global list could land under the Project tab.
- **Fix.** Both studios load the record by id (`fetchMoodboard` / `fetchCharacter`), and its `projectId` decides the scope: on a mismatch the studio re-enters itself in the right scope, which picks the right draft key. A record from another project opens too (the node in this project uses it). The Assets panel drops a list that arrives after its tab or scope changed. The studio rails already did this.
- **Not done.** Callers still pass a scope. It's now only a hint, so a wrong one costs one extra load.
- **Tests.** `AssetStudioDrafts.test.tsx` gets four new tests: a project board and a project character opened from their node, a global board opened as project, and a deleted board still showing not found. The first three fail on main. `AssetsPanel.test.tsx` is new: a late Global list is dropped, and it fails on main. `MoodboardStudioAnalysis.test.tsx` mocks the by-id fetch. Live, in both tab kinds: each board and the project character open as themselves.

## 2026-10-18 — The moodboard brief: Direction, Avoid, pinned colours, an override, and Avoid by model (design-canvas gap 14; B4-B7)

The person's direction used to live inside `analysis` (`styleBrief`, `negativePrompt`), so Analyze threw away their edits, and the default negatives were content bans ("logo replication", "identity transfer") that pulled diffusion models toward exactly those things.

- **Fields on the board.** `direction`, `avoid`, `pinnedColors {include, exclude}` and `briefOverride {text, basis, updatedAt}` sit beside `analysis` (`services/moodboard_store.py`). Changing them doesn't clear the analysis. Every API response adds a computed `brief` (`services/moodboard_brief.compose`), never saved. Contract: `docs/contracts/07-studios-and-resources.md` (new; Moodboard only).
- **The brief.** Direction comes first, then a positive mode intent ("Take the visual style only… The subject comes from the prompt."), palette minus kept-out colours (within dE00 5, Commons' "same colour"), accents, "Make sure these colors appear", cues, room for the vision reader's `motifs`/`materials`/`textures`, notes. Negatives are `blurry, low-detail artifacts` plus Avoid (B4). `ANALYSIS_VERSION` is 3 because the analysis's own brief and negatives changed wording.
- **Override and the badge (B6).** Clients send only `{text}`; the server stamps `basis` (a hash of the analysis inputs plus the brief fields, name left out like `source_hash`). Sending the same text again keeps the old basis, because Studio saves the whole draft on every change and would otherwise hide the badge. Keep is `POST /api/moodboards/{id}/brief-override/keep`; Regenerate is `briefOverride: null` (Studio then analyzes if the analysis was cleared). Editing the override text counts as Keep. A run with a stale override still uses it and adds a run note.
- **Avoid by model (B5), in one place.** `apply_to_generator` runs in the engine before every handler: the brief joins the prompt for every generator with a Moodboard port; the Avoid sentence joins only for ids starting `gpt-image-`, `nano-banana`, `krea-2-` (and their Krea catalog copies); a `negative_prompt` param gets the negatives. The Krea handler no longer appends the brief itself. Decision I made: image generators that had no Moodboard port gained one (GPT Image 1/1.5/2/2.5 and their fal copies, Nano Banana and its fal copies, FLUX.2 [pro], Fast SDXL), so the rule has generators to act on; before this only Krea 2 took a board. FLUX.2 and SDXL are the diffusion-style ones; SDXL shows the negative-field path.
- **Surprises found while wiring it.** (1) The engine would have passed the Moodboard port on to handlers; Krea's catalog routes send wired ports by name and refuse unknown fields, so the port is now folded in and not passed on, except to `krea-2-generate`, which reads the board's images. (2) The output cache keyed on the node's own params, so an Avoid edit that only changes the negative field would replay an old image; the key now uses the params the handler gets. (3) The `nebula-moodboard` node was output-cached by its params (the board id), so editing a board didn't reach a run in the same backend session for an hour; it is no longer cached (it only reads a JSON file). The `character` node had the same bug: a character edit (traits, seed, views) replayed the old bundle for up to an hour. Both now sit in `_READS_SAVED_RECORD` in `execution/engine.py`, the nodes whose params name a saved record rather than hold it. `test_an_edited_character_reaches_the_next_run` fails without it. It needs reference views the cache can see: with missing view files every lookup misses, which is why the bug didn't show in the existing tests.
- **Migration (B7).** At startup, boards without `briefVersion` are migrated once (and in memory on any read before that). Negatives beyond the old defaults move to Avoid. A `styleBrief` that doesn't match what analyzer v1 or v2 would have written (name as a wildcard, current notes or the notes the summary recorded) becomes the override; anything that doesn't match counts as edited, so a person's text is never lost to a guess. An override from an out-of-date analysis starts stale. Each changed file is copied first to `~/.nebula/moodboard-backups/brief-fields-<time>/<scope>/` with `migration-log.json`; copying a file back undoes that board. One board that fails to migrate is logged and skipped, and still opens as saved.
- **Studio.** A Direction section (what the board is for, Avoid chips, colours that must appear / keep out) and "Brief sent to generators" with Generated / Written by you, the badge, the negative prompt and the sentence GPT Image, Nano Banana and Krea 2 get. The old free-text Style brief and Negative prompt boxes are gone. `runAnalyze` now reads dirty state from the store, so Regenerate's save lands before the analysis.
- **Not in this change.** CLI commands (another lane). The vision reader. Quick-pick of palette swatches into the pinned lists would be a nice follow-up.
- **Checked live** on an isolated backend (8826) and Vite (5826), nothing sent to 8000-8010 (17/17). In Studio: set Direction, two Avoid items and a kept-out colour; Analyze kept all three and the brief led with the Direction and dropped the blue from its palette; wrote an override, changed an image weight, saw "Board changed since you edited this."; Keep cleared it; changed the weight again, Regenerate rebuilt the generated brief. Two old-format boards seeded before a restart migrated with backups and a log (the edited one got `chrome text` in Avoid and its brief as the override). A graph text → board → Krea 2 / GPT Image 2 / FLUX.2 / SDXL ran with Krea's API mocked (respx) and the others recording: Krea 2's request body and GPT Image 2's built body end with "Keep these out of the image: neon signage, lens flare, colors close to #485caa."; FLUX.2's prompt has the brief and no Avoid text; SDXL's has no Avoid text and its negative is `blurry, low-detail artifacts, neon signage, lens flare`.
- **Review pass (same day).** Found and fixed: (1) migration moved an old negative longer than 200 characters into Avoid whole, so every later Studio save of that board was refused; it now keeps moved text within the store's limits and logs what it cut (the backup and the analysis keep it whole). (2) One board that couldn't be backed up or written stopped the rest of the migration, and only `OSError` was caught at startup; now that board is skipped and logged, and startup never fails on the migration. (3) An unreadable board file left a new, empty backup folder on every start; the log folder is now made only when a board changed. (4) A board written by this analyzer but never migrated (a file copied in from an old backup) would have had its own brief turned into an override. (5) Keep on an id no board can have said "no hand-written brief" (409); it is now 404, and the 409 says to set one with `PUT`. (6) Studio let a person go past the backend's limits (40 Avoid items, 200 characters each, 12 colours per list), and the refused save showed only "Update moodboard failed: 422" and stopped autosave; it now stops at the limits (`briefLimits.ts`, checked against the backend by a test) and shows the backend's reason. (7) An emptied hand-written brief still said "Written by you" though generators got the generated one.
- **CI and security pass (same day).** CI failed only because Nano Banana gained its optional Moodboard port on purpose: `test_cli_apply`, `test_mcp_tools` and `modelDiscovery.test.ts` listed its old inputs; updated to include `moodboard`. Audit of the backend diff: nothing here infers the person from a missing header, an Origin or a body field. Fixed: (1) any agent (or curl) could replace, remove or Keep the person's hand-written brief, which the board can't give back (no history); overrides are now stamped `by: "person" | "agent"` from the person gate, and only the person may replace, remove or Keep text the person wrote (a migrated override, with no `by`, counts as theirs); a refused PUT saves nothing and answers 403 with the gate's code. Agents can still change every other field (the person sees the badge) and their own overrides. (2) A hand-edited board file (`"avoid": 5`, `"images": null` with an override) took `GET /api/moodboards` down with a 500; board fields are read leniently and a brief that can't be composed is `null`. (3) A board saved by a newer Nebula (`briefVersion` 2) would be "migrated" back down after a downgrade; it's left alone. Added a test that a failing migration can't stop startup (it already couldn't). Left for Justin: board edits still can't be undone (deletes become restorable with #74). Follow-up the same day: Studio now says who wrote the override. While the text is what an agent saved it reads "Written by an agent" / "An agent's brief"; once the person edits it, "Written by you" (the backend stamps it theirs on save). The label comes from the saved `by`, which only the backend sets; a client sending `by` gets a 422 (`test_a_client_cannot_say_who_wrote_the_brief`). `frontend/src/components/moodboard-studio/briefAuthor.ts`.
- **Tests.** `test_moodboard_brief.py` (32: fields survive Analyze, defects-only negatives per mode, override and Keep/Regenerate, per-model Avoid, port not passed on, cache key, engine run, migration with backups, idempotence, a failing board), `MoodboardBrief.test.tsx` (4), plus updated moodboard, Krea and reference-role tests.
- **Merged after #74 (Recently deleted).** The migration walked every folder under the moodboard store, which now includes `.trash`. It would have "migrated" each `<id>.trash.json` record as if it were a board, adding board fields to it. Boards in the trash still migrate, with backups like the rest, so a restore brings back a board with its fields; the records are skipped (`test_a_board_in_recently_deleted_migrates_and_its_trash_record_stays`, which fails without the fix). Reading a trashed board, saving it, or Keep on it now answers like #74's routes (404 with `code: "in_trash"`), and Studio says the board went to Recently deleted instead of "Save failed: 404" (`moodboardWriteError` in `lib/api.ts`). The restore route returned the raw saved file, so a restored board came back without `brief`; it now returns the board as `GET` does (`_asset_out`; `test_asset_trash.py` caught it).

## 2026-10-18 — Security audit of the apply-plans lane

- **CI fix.** `Canvas.continuity` and `Canvas.focus` render Canvas without a React Flow provider and stub its child layers; `ArrangeController` reads the React Flow store, so 25 tests threw. Stubbed it like the other layers.
- **Fixed: an agent could finish another agent's arrange under that agent's name.** The arrangeId rides on every graphSync, and the layout write-back journaled the move as the agent that asked, whoever wrote it. A write from a request with an agent marker is now journaled as that agent; a canvas's write (person or not) still credits the asker. Test: `test_another_agent_finishing_an_arrange_is_journaled_as_itself` (fails without the fix). Positions were never at risk: the write only accepts that request's new nodes.
- **Checked, not issues.** `/api/graph/apply` is agent-only (the person gets 403) and still runs every single-edit check per item (Krea auth, provider, asset ids, billing, internal params via `parse_spec`, World Labs delete holds, approved runs, cycles), now with the 413 size bound on the staged graph; it never runs anything (`run` isn't an apply key). Steps live only in the CLI: each is its own `/api/graph/apply` call with those checks, and the server holds no plan state. The layout write-back is open to every caller, as `PUT /api/graph/layout` already was; with `arrangeId` it can only position that request's new nodes, ids leave a request when their node goes (every removal exports and prunes) and all requests close on Clear or a project switch.
- **Permanence.** With no caps, one apply can remove every node. That is not new reach: `DELETE /api/graph` already clears the canvas in one call from any caller. With #75 merged and a canvas open, an apply is one undo step that brings nodes back with outputs and wires. With no canvas open, removals stay permanent, as on main; that needs the planned server-side history.

- **The copy promised an undo that isn't there.** The steps output said earlier steps were "a normal edit the person can undo", and MCP-SETUP said the same of direct edits and the arrange write. Nothing on main undoes an agent's edit: graphSync merges don't go on the canvas's undo stack, and the backend has no route to restore a node an agent removed (its journal keeps only the name and type). The copy now says what is true: earlier steps stay on the canvas, and the refusal tells the agent how to finish (fix the step, apply it and the rest alone, with the printed ids in place of the +refs). Lifting the removal cap therefore needs Justin's call; see the PR's open question.
- **Two step mistakes the server would only catch after step 1 landed** are now caught before anything is sent: a step that changes nothing, and a step with `arrange` that adds no nodes.
- **A tab could keep drawing every node forever.** If an arrange named nodes that never reached the tab, ArrangeController skipped it on every tick without counting toward the 15 s limit, so culling stayed off for good. It now gives up after the same 15 s (test: `ArrangeController.test.tsx`, fails without the fix).
- Live check rerun on the isolated stack (backend 8823 with the person link, Vite 5823, ports 8000-8010 blocked, zero attempts): 27/27.

## 2026-10-18 — Direct edits have no per-edit caps; plans take steps; edits can ask the canvas to arrange their new nodes (decisions C1, C2, C3; design-canvas gaps 9 and 10)

Justin's answers: C1 c) no per-edit cap, only the global size limits. C2 a) a CLI plan file can hold steps, later steps reuse earlier refs, the server stays stateless. C3 a) the canvas arranges only that edit's new nodes, only when the edit asks.

- **C1: the global bound exists, so the per-edit caps went.** Before lifting anything I checked for a canvas-wide limit: `RESTORE_MAX_GRAPH_NODES` (10,000) and `RESTORE_MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` (50,000) already bound import and restore, and every graph route runs `_validate_graph_ingress_complexity` (value count and depth). `POST /api/graph/apply` now checks the staged graph against the node and wire limits and refuses with 413 ("nothing changed") before committing. `parse_spec(capped=False)` drops the 12 nodes / 24 wires / 12 param changes for direct edits; the 24 removes/unwires/renames and 50 moves are gone too. Proposals keep every cap: the person reviews them item by item. The limits read as a canvas size limit, not anything to do with paying.
- **C2: steps live only in the CLI.** `{"note"?, "steps": [plan, ...]}`. `cli/plan.py` `check_steps` validates the whole file before step 1 is sent: a ref is created once across all steps, a step may use only refs it or an earlier step creates, no `run`, no nesting. `resolve_step` swaps earlier refs for the ids in each reply's `idMap` (edges, unwire, params, rename, move, remove). A refused step stops the run with exit 1, names the step and the reason, and lists what earlier steps applied (they stay on the canvas). `--json` gives `{status, steps, idMap}` or `{status: "stopped", failedStep, error, applied, idMap}`. `nebula propose` refuses steps (a proposal is one decision). Decision of mine: a top-level `note` (or `--note`) fills in steps that have none.
- **C3: the arrange request.** `arrange: true` or `{"direction": "right" | "down", "gap": 0-2000}` on `/api/graph/apply`, MCP `edit_canvas`, and `nebula apply` (`--arrange [right|down]`, also with `--file`; with steps it goes inside each step). An edit with `arrange` must add nodes. `direction` is the flow: "right" makes each step of the wiring a column, "down" a row, so unwired nodes in "down" sit side by side in one row. That matches how Auto-layout already thinks about ranks; I picked it over "down = one column" so wired graphs read the same either way.
- **How the canvas does it.** `services/canvas_arrange.py` keeps open requests in memory (like proposals) and every graphSync carries them. `ArrangeController` waits until the nodes are measured, their images loaded and sizes steady for 300 ms (at most 15 s), runs `arrangeNewNodes` (the size-aware `computeLayout` on the new nodes only, anchored at the top-left of where the agent placed them, shifted right or down if the block would cover another node), and writes with `PUT /api/graph/layout` + `arrangeId`. The backend applies the first write per id and closes it; another tab gets `already-arranged` and changes nothing. No tab applies its own result locally: every tab takes the winner's positions from the graphSync `moved` list, so two tabs can't disagree. The write only accepts that request's nodes (400 otherwise), and the journal credits the agent ("arranged n2, n3…").
- **With no canvas open, the nodes stay where they were placed and the first canvas that opens lays them out** (I picked this over "skipped"). The reply's `arrange.status` says `waiting` or `waiting-for-canvas`, with a plain sentence. A later explicit position (a drag, an agent `move`) wins and drops that node from the request; opening another project, Clear canvas or a restart drops requests.
- **Surprises found in the live check, all fixed here.**
  - The canvas culls off-screen nodes by default (`canvasPerfMode`, on), so they're never measured and the layout fell back to default sizes: image cards overlapped. While this tab has an arrange to measure, the canvas renders every node (`selectMeasuring` in `arrangeStore.ts`), then culls again.
  - Card images use `loading="lazy"`, so off-screen images never loaded and cards stayed short. `ArrangeController` switches an unloaded lazy image in a request's node to eager.
  - A tab that opens a project drops the graphSync its socket got on connect (it arrives before the tab has a project revision), so "the first canvas that opens" never saw the request. `projectStore.initialize` now hydrates `arrange` from `GET /api/graph/export`.
  - The reply's "is a canvas open" first counted only sockets verified with the person link. A tab opened without it still draws and arranges, so the reply now counts any socket without an agent marker (`manager.canvas_open()`).
  - The empty-canvas export no longer carries `arrange` (it broke an exact-shape test); the canvas clears its list on an empty sync.
- **Live check (isolated backend 8823 via `devserver.py` with the person link, Vite 5823, Puppeteer, ports 8000-8010 blocked, zero attempts): 27/27.** One edit of 20 nodes (10 Image Inputs of local test images 800x1400 to 1200x400, 6 Text Inputs, 4 Combine Text, 8 wires) with `arrange: true` and two tabs open: exactly one arranged event, credited to the agent; 21 nodes drawn in each tab, none overlap, every position matches the backend; the person's own node didn't move; card heights 145-516 px. A reload doesn't re-arrange. With no tab open, the reply said `waiting-for-canvas`, the nodes stayed at their placed spot, and the next tab that opened arranged them (`down`: one row). A two-step plan through the real CLI: step 2 wired and renamed step 1's nodes by ref, step 2's arrange ran on the open canvas, step 1's nodes (no arrange) stayed put.
- **Not done here.** The repo's `nebula` skill (`skills/nebula/SKILL.md`) is being added by the D1 lane (moodboard-cli-skill), not on main yet, so its `nebula apply` section doesn't mention steps or `--arrange`. See the PR's open question.

## 2026-10-18 — Moodboards from the CLI and MCP; `nebula skill install` (design-canvas gaps 1 and 3; decisions D1, D2, D6)

Gap 3: Moodboard Studio had no CLI or MCP, so an agent uploaded each image and wrote the board JSON by hand. Gap 1: the global `nebula` skill named one person's checkout path and told agents to `nebula clear` first.

- **One client, two front ends.** `backend/moodboard_client.py` does the work; `nebula moodboard list|show|new|add|set|analyze|delete` (`cli/commands/moodboard.py`) and the `moodboard_*` MCP tools both call it. It only uses the routes Moodboard Studio uses (`/api/uploads`, `/api/moodboards`), so the backend gained nothing.
- **Links are fetched on the agent side (D6 b), through Commons' guarded fetcher.** The first version wrote its own downloader, which a security review caught fetching anything: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/...`, the local network, the cloud metadata address. That mattered because the MCP server runs outside an in-app agent's sandbox (Codex's shell has no network precisely so it can't reach the backend), so a link was a way around it. Downloads now go through `commons.net.safe_fetch`, the fetcher Commons already uses for links: public addresses only, checked on every redirect (3 at most), the connection made to the address that was checked (no DNS rebinding), ports 80 and 443, no credentials in the link, odd IP spellings refused. On top: a PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP content type whose bytes also sniff as one, 20 MB (the backend's own upload cap) and 60 s in all. `commons/net.py` gained typed errors (`BlockedAddress`, `FetchStatus`, `FetchTooLarge`, subclasses of the old ones, so Commons is unchanged) so the message can say what went wrong. A test asserts the backend has no URL-fetching code path for boards. Everything is read and downloaded before the first upload, so one bad source leaves Nebula untouched. `moodboard_create` and `moodboard_add` now run off the MCP event loop (FastMCP calls sync tools on it, so a slow download stalled every other call); the turn's workspace scope reaches the worker thread, and a test checks it.
- **Small decisions I made.** A board is named by id or exact name (case-insensitive; two boards with one name asks for the id). An image is named by its number from `show` or its id. Folders take the images directly inside, in natural name order (`2.png` before `10.png`), hidden files skipped, no recursion. A Nebula output URL (`/api/outputs/...`) is used as is, after checking it is an image. Duplicate URLs are skipped and reported. Like Moodboard Studio, any change but a rename clears the analysis. `new` without `--project` makes a board for every project (Moodboard Studio's Global); `--project current` means the open one. `--remove` takes an image off the board and prints the URL that puts it back.
- **In-app chats.** With a turn token, local paths must be inside that turn's workspace (same rule as Commons), and a relative path means the workspace. Security review fix: images found in a folder skipped that check, so a link inside the folder could read a file elsewhere. Each folder image is now checked like a file named on its own, the check runs again when the file is read, and the read opens each folder and the file with `O_NOFOLLOW`, so a link swapped in after the check fails the read instead of leaving the workspace. Open question for Justin: in-app agents can reach public web addresses through link intake (Commons' `commons_add` already does this from the backend; moodboards now match it). Whether in-app agents should fetch links at all, or only after the person OKs each one, is a policy call for the freedom design.
- **Delete (fixed in review, then tightened).** Today's DELETE route is permanent; the trash lane (#74) makes it a move to Recently deleted. The client asks first whether this Nebula has Recently deleted (`GET /api/trash`). If it does, anyone may delete, agents included, and the CLI prints the restore command. If it doesn't, `nebula moodboard delete` and `moodboard_delete` refuse for everyone and point to Moodboard Studio. A first review fix let the CLI delete for good after the person typed the board's name at a terminal; a security review flagged that as authorization decided in the client (a tty, a typed name and an unset agent name prove nothing, and any client could skip the check), so that path is gone. Who may empty Recently deleted is decided by the backend (`require_person`, services/person_gate.py). Merge #74 first so `delete` works from the CLI at all.
- **Undo for edits (added in review).** `moodboard_update` and `set --json` return `previous`, the board's settings and each image's weight, notes and excluded before the change. Passing them back to `moodboard_update` undoes it; a test round-trips it. Removed images were already handed back as URLs.
- **Race fixed in review.** `add` read the board, then downloaded (up to a minute per link), then wrote the old image list plus the new images, so a weight set in Moodboard Studio meanwhile was lost. It now reads the board again after the downloads, right before writing.
- **`nebula skill install` (D1, D2).** Links `~/.claude/skills/nebula` to the checkout's `skills/nebula`, or copies it with `--copy` (the copy records its checkout in `.installed-from`). Codex has the same thing: its user skill folder is `~/.agents/skills` and it follows symlinked skill folders (checked on learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills today), so the command handles both, for each app found on the machine, or `--for claude|codex|all`. Whatever was there is moved, never deleted, to `skill-backups/nebula.backup-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` **next to** the skills folder, not inside it: a backup inside `skills/` would load as a second skill named `nebula`. An install that is already current does nothing. It needs no backend.
- **Surprise: the packaged app does have a repo.** Nebula.app runs from the checkout it was built from (`desktop/app-repo.mjs`), so a link works there too. `--copy` stays for a checkout that may move or be deleted.
- **The skill (`skills/nebula/SKILL.md`)** is new, built from the useful parts of the global one: no personal paths, how to find the checkout from the link, "never `nebula clear`; use `nebula project new`" (another lane adds that command; until then the skill says to ask the person to make a project), and the moodboard commands. It lives outside `.agents/skills/`, which Nebula's own chats read.
- **Checked live** on an isolated backend (8824) and Vite (5824), nothing sent to 8000-8010 or through Vite's proxy. From the CLI: `moodboard new` with a folder of four local PNGs plus one JPEG served by a local `http.server`, `set --weight 2=0.4 --image-note 5=...`, `analyze` (palette plus the orange accent). Moodboard Studio showed the board with five images in order, weight 0.40 on the second, the note on the fifth, and the analysed brief. `skill install` and `--copy --for codex` against a temp HOME made the links, the copy and the dated backups.
- **Seen, not fixed (not this lane).** Opening a global board by double-click while the Assets panel is on its Project tab left Moodboard Studio on "Loading Moodboard..." in the unauthenticated test tab; the Global tab opened it fine.
- **Tests.** `tests/test_moodboard_cli.py` (18 after review, adding the delete gate, the trash path, undo and the add race; first 14: folder + link + set + analyze + delete end to end through the real routes, duplicates, a bad source uploads nothing, value checks, outputs as is, the open project, download refusals and timeout, no backend URL fetching, workspace confinement, the MCP tools and their annotations) and `tests/test_skill_install.py` (7, temp HOME only). All fail on main (the modules don't exist there).
- **Merged after #74.** With Recently deleted in, the end-to-end CLI and MCP tests now delete the board, check it is gone, and bring it back (`nebula trash restore`, the restore route). The older-backend test fakes a 404 on `/api/trash` by patching `NebulaAPI.request` on the class. Its first version patched a throwaway instance (`NebulaClient.api` builds a new one on each access), so its "no DELETE was sent" check never saw a request; the refusals it checked held only because main had no `/api/trash` yet.

## 2026-10-18 — Recently deleted: CI and security fixes

- **CI.** Three frontend tests failed. Two in `tests/components/StoredAssetNodes.test.tsx` still expected a deleted board to read "Board not found"; the PR changed that on purpose (a deleted board is now in Recently deleted, and the card refetches on a delete broadcast). The test now covers both: trashed (name kept, "In Recently deleted", Restore brings it back, no Open) and deleted for good ("Board not found", "deleted for good or never existed"). The Inspector copy check now says "deleted for good". The third (`tests/components/AssetStudioDrafts.test.tsx`, Character uploads) mocked every `apiFetch` as the upload, so the Studio's new Recently deleted fetch got the same `Response` and read its body first ("Body is unusable"). The mock now sends only `/api/uploads` to the upload; the test's assertions are unchanged.
- **Audit of the backend diff for authorization bugs.** Purge and empty call `require_person`; restore and list are open to agents; nothing authorizes on `deletedBy` or `actor_for_headers`; ids go through the stores' regexes before any path is built; PUT and analyze can't write a trashed board back (lookups skip `.trash`), create always mints a fresh id, and restore refuses when the id is live (409). Two real gaps, fixed:
  - *Attribution spoofing.* An outside agent names itself (`X-Nebula-Agent`), and the trash UI and CLI printed an agent's name as is, so an agent called "You" read as "deleted by you". A first fix suffixed blocklisted names; the follow-up review showed a blocklist can't be complete (homoglyphs, zero-width, bidi, fullwidth). The structural fix: every display derives the label from `kind` (frontend `lib/trash.ts actorLabel`, used by the Studio list, Projects' list and the save-failure message; `cli/commands/trash.py _who`). An agent always shows as "<name> (agent)", and only `kind == "person"` shows as "you". `canvas_events.actor_record` also cleans the name where it enters attribution (NFKC, drops Cc/Cf/Co/Cs, collapses whitespace, 64 chars, "Agent" when empty). The `X-Nebula-Agent` path already keeps only ASCII name characters (`agent_presence.clean_agent_name`), so the lookalikes mostly couldn't arrive through it; the label no longer depends on that.
  - *Empty raced an agent's delete.* `POST /api/trash/empty` and `POST /api/projects/trash/empty` deleted for good whatever was in the trash at that moment, so an agent's delete that landed after the person's list loaded was destroyed without the person seeing it. Both now take what the list showed (`{"items": [{kind, id}]}` / `{"ids": [...]}`) and delete only those; the canvas sends it. Without the field they behave as before (person only either way).
- **Left for Justin.** Projects still expire 30 days after a delete, including projects an agent deleted, so an agent's delete becomes permanent with no person action. Recommendation: no timer for a project an agent or unnamed client deleted (only person-deleted projects expire), or drop the timer as boards and characters did.

## 2026-10-18 — Recently deleted: review fixes

An adversarial review of the Recently deleted lane found four gaps, all about a delete that happens while someone else is working on the same board.

- **Saving a board an agent just deleted.** The person has a board open in Moodboard Studio (or a Character in Character Studio) and an agent deletes it. The next autosave used to fail with "Update moodboard failed: 404". `PUT /api/moodboards/{id}` and `PUT /api/characters/{id}` now answer like `GET` does: 404 with `code: "in_trash"` and the trash record. The Studio says "This board was moved to Recently deleted by <agent>. Restore it from the list on the left, then Retry to save your changes." The edits stay in the draft, and the save never brings the board back on its own.
- **The Studio's list goes stale.** Recently deleted only loaded when the Studio opened or after the Studio's own delete, so an agent's delete didn't show up. It now reloads on every `storedAssetChanged` broadcast for its kind. When the set of ids in it changes, the library rail above it reloads too. Autosaves don't change the trash, so they don't make the rail reload.
- **Edits lost on delete.** Delete in the Studio moved the last *saved* version to the trash, dropping anything typed in the last 600 ms before autosave. Delete now saves pending edits first, and doesn't delete if that save fails. Undo and Restore bring back what the person last saw.
- **Restoring twice.** Two tabs, or an agent restoring after the person's Undo, got a 404 ("isn't in Recently deleted") for a board that was back. A restore of an asset that is already live now returns 200 with `alreadyRestored: true`. It is still 409 when a trash copy and a live copy share the id, and 404 when neither exists.
- **Tests.** Backend: `test_saving_a_board_or_character_someone_trashed_says_it_is_in_recently_deleted`, `test_restoring_twice_is_harmless`. Frontend: `AssetTrash.test.tsx` (the list reloads on a broadcast, and tells the rail only when the trash changed) and `lib/assetSaveFailure.test.ts` (the save message). Each fails without the fix. 409 backend tests across 16 related files pass, plus the 3 frontend files; `tsc -b` and eslint are clean.
- **Live check** (isolated backend 8822, Vite 5822, Puppeteer, 8000-8010 and the Vite proxy blocked, zero attempts, 12/12): an agent's API delete of the open board makes Recently deleted appear and the rail drop it with no reload; typing then shows the moved-by-agent message; Restore from the list, then Retry, saves the edit to the same id; typing and pressing Delete at once puts the edited version in the trash, and Undo brings it back; a second restore gets the 200 no-op.

## 2026-10-18 — Deleted moodboards and characters go to Recently deleted (design-canvas D5)

Justin's D5 answer lets agents delete moodboards "as the API allows today", with the note "As long as we have undo an agent can do anything." A delete used to unlink the board's or character's JSON file, so nothing could undo it. Now a delete moves it to Recently deleted, anyone (agents included) can restore it, and only the person can delete it for good.

- **Storage.** Each store gets a `.trash/` folder (`~/.nebula/moodboards/.trash/`, `~/.nebula/characters/.trash/`). Delete moves the file there with `os.replace`, byte for byte, and writes `<id>.trash.json` beside it: kind, name, thumbnail, projectId, the folder it came from, `deletedAt` and `deletedBy` (`{kind, name}`: "You", an agent by name, or "Unnamed client"). Restore moves it back to the same folder, so the id and contents are identical and nodes pointing at it run again. Delete writes the record first, restore moves the file first, and a record without its file is ignored, so a crash in between never lists a ghost. The store lookups skip dot folders, so a trashed asset is never "found". Shared code: `backend/services/asset_trash.py`.
- **Projects were already soft-deleted** (2026-10-10: `catalog["trash"]`, 30-day expiry). They now record `deletedBy`, show in the same `GET /api/trash` listing and `nebula trash` commands, and deleting one for good (`DELETE /api/projects/trash/{id}`, `POST /api/projects/trash/empty`) is person-only too.
- **Who can do what.** Delete (to trash) and restore: anyone, agents included. Delete for good: person only, through `require_person` (the gate the spending-limit settings routes use). It now takes a `hint`, so the 403 tells an agent it can restore instead. An unnamed client (no agent marker, no person token) gets `person_required`, as with every other person-only route. The CLI has no delete-for-good command on purpose: the CLI is never the person.
- **No automatic purge for boards and characters (a choice Justin can change).** They stay until the person deletes them for good or empties the trash. Projects keep their existing 30-day expiry, so the two behave differently; flagged as an open question rather than changed here.
- **API.** `GET /api/trash` (`kind`, `scope`, `projectId`), `POST /api/trash/{kind}/{id}/restore` (409 if a live copy and a trash copy share the id, 200 with `alreadyRestored` if it is already back, 404 if neither), `DELETE /api/trash/{kind}/{id}` and `POST /api/trash/empty` (person only; empty takes the same filters as the listing). `DELETE /api/moodboards/{id}` and `/api/characters/{id}` now return `{status: "trashed", trashed: <record>}`. `GET` on a trashed board or character is still 404, with `code: "in_trash"` and the record. A run of a node pointing at a trashed asset fails with "is in Recently deleted. Restore it ...", and `edit_canvas`/`nebula apply` refuse to point a node at one with the restore command in the message.
- **MCP and CLI.** New MCP tools `list_trash` and `restore_from_trash`, added to `NEBULA_MCP_TOOLS` so in-app Claude and Codex may use them (both are undoable). CLI: `nebula trash list [--kind] [--json]` and `nebula trash restore [kind] <id>` (the kind is looked up when left out). No `nebula moodboard ...` commands here: another lane adds those.
