## 2026-10-18 — An agent's canvas edit is one undo step on the person's canvas (D4, D5)

Justin's rule is that agents may do anything that can be undone. Undo didn't cover agents: an agent's edit reached open canvases as a graphSync, which the canvas merged without an undo step, so Cmd-Z skipped it. And no undo reached the backend: undo and redo only changed the canvas, so the next graphSync put the backend's version back (an undone deletion came back as a deletion).

- **Who made an edit.** `_broadcast_graph_sync(edit=True)` is set on every route that edits the graph: create, connect, node-and-connect, params, rename, layout, delete, clear, unwire, apply (`edit_canvas`, `nebula apply`), cluster, upload-with-node, proposal accept, Cinema send-to-motion, and the new restore route. The sync then carries `edit = {actor, tab?}`. `actor` comes from `actor_for_headers`, the journal's rule. `tab` is `X-Nebula-Tab`, which the canvas's `apiFetch` sets on every write (`lib/tabId.ts`, a fresh id per page load). Run results, status and paid-start bookkeeping carry no `edit`, and neither does a replaced graph.
- **The undo stack holds two kinds of step** (`lib/canvasUndo.ts`, `graphStore.ts`). The person's own edits stay whole-canvas snapshots (`UndoSnapshot`). A sync with `edit` from anywhere but this tab becomes a `ForeignEdit`: only the nodes and wires it touched, before and after (`diffCanvas`). Undo puts back `before` (`applySlice`), so later run outputs survive, and redo puts back `after`. Positions count only for nodes the sync says it `moved`.
- **Why one LIFO stack keeps snapshots right.** A snapshot is restored only after every later step, agent ones included, has been undone. So restoring a whole-canvas snapshot never silently reverts an agent's edit. That is also why another window's edits are steps here ("Undid an edit from another window"): without them, undoing an older snapshot in this tab would revert the other window's work.
- **Undo reaches the backend: `POST /api/graph/restore`.** After every undo or redo the canvas sends what changed for backend nodes: params (replaced, not merged), name, position, nodes to put back (with outputs, under their old id) or remove, and wires. It is staged on a copy with the single-edit checks (provider, Krea auth, asset refs, billing for agents, Cinema shot media, World Labs checkpoints, cycles, approved runs) and committed at once. A node already gone or a wire already there isn't an error, so two tabs undoing the same step agree. A node whose id now holds a different model gives a 409, and the canvas then puts the step back as it was and says why. `CLIGraph.add_node(node_id=…)` restores an old id and moves the counter past it. The journal records the restore as whoever the canvas is, with "(undo)" / "(redo)".
- **The person's own undo now syncs too.** This applies the same restore to the person's own steps, which fixes the old frontend-only undo. To make that safe, steps that a backend write's graphSync could beat are now taken *before* the request (`beginUndoStep`, `cancelUndoStep` on failure): deleting backend nodes, Clear canvas (toolbar and chat `/clear`), dropping an image on the canvas, a chat upload, and accepting a proposal. Before, the snapshot was taken after the echo had already applied the change, so undo did nothing. Snapshots now keep each node's outputs, so undoing your own deletion brings the node back with its results. A node still on the canvas keeps its live results.
- **Mid-change safety.** A graphSync used to overwrite every param the backend sent, including keys the person had typed but the 250 ms debounce hadn't sent yet. Now `unsavedParamEdits` keeps those keys as typed until the write settles, for any sync (agent edits and run results alike), while the rest of the node follows the backend. A node being dragged keeps its position (as before), so its position isn't part of the agent's step. After an agent's step lands, the person's next keystroke starts a new step, so undoing the agent's edit never takes later typing with it.
- **Notice.** `CanvasUndoNotice` sits in the proposal bar's panel, so the two stack. It shows "Claude changed the canvas" with Undo (agents only, not other windows), "Undid Claude's edit" with Redo, and "Couldn't undo that. <reason>". The button acts only while that step is next on its stack. It springs in (the project toast's spring), stays static under reduced motion, and goes away after 6 s. No history panel.
- **Not undo steps:** run outputs and node status, this tab's own echoes, and project open, switch or create. Frontend-only nodes (UUID ids) never go to the restore route; their undo is local, as before.
- **Review fixes (same day, adversarial pass).**
  - *An agent's `nebula graph load` couldn't be undone.* It goes through `POST /api/graph/import`, whose sync was `graphReplaced` and so never a step, and it also wiped the tab's frontend-only nodes. Now an import's sync carries `edit` (only reason "import"; project open, create and delete still don't), and a replacement from another tab or an agent is one step whose undo puts the whole canvas back, frontend-only nodes included. An import hands out ids from n1 again, so the same id can hold another model afterwards. The canvas now sends such an id in both `remove` and `nodes`, and the restore route treats that as a swap (it used to refuse it as "listed twice"). Swapped nodes come back whole with their own outputs (`applySlice`), and their wires are sent again. An id that changed model without being in `remove` still gets the 409.
  - *Stale steps after a replacement that isn't an edit.* A `graphReplaced` sync without `edit` used to leave the undo stack alone. Now that undo writes to the backend, an old step would have written the old graph into the new one. Both stacks now empty on such a sync, the same as `loadGraph` does for this tab's own loads.
  - *An agent could hide an edit from undo* by sending a tab id it read off an earlier graphSync (`edit.tab` is broadcast). The backend now leaves out `tab` whenever the actor is a named agent, so its edit is always a step.
  - Updated `test_graph_import_execution_guard.py` (the import now broadcasts with `edit=True`).
  - Live check rerun on the isolated stack (8821/5821, 0 requests to 8000-8010): the original steps all pass again. Then an agent import turned n1 into a Nano Banana, the notice read "Claude changed the canvas", and Cmd-Z brought back "Hero prompt" (text-input) as n1 with its value and wire, on the canvas and in `GET /api/graph`.
  - Known limit, not fixed: if this tab's own write and an agent's write commit back to back, and this tab's echo is broadcast before the agent's, the echo already carries the agent's change and the tab takes it as its own. The agent's own sync then changes nothing here, so that one agent edit is not a step. It needs per-request change sets on the sync to fix properly. It is rare (the window is one export of the graph).
- **Security audit (same day).** Restore checked line by line against import and the single-edit routes. Two fixes:
  - *A script could still hide its edit from undo.* The tab rule only excluded named agents, so a request with no agent marker and no person token (curl, a CLI run without a name, a forged Origin) could send a tab id read off a broadcast graphSync and pass as that tab's echo. `tab` is now kept only when `is_person` holds (no marker AND this launch's token). A canvas without the person token gets no echo match either; at worst its own echo shows as an "outside" step. Test: `test_only_the_person_can_mark_an_edit_as_a_tab_echo` (three header sets).
  - *Restore could push ids out of undo's reach.* `add_node(node_id=n999999999)` moved the counter there, so every later id had 10 digits, failed `SHORT_ID_RE`, and could never be restored: later deletions on that graph became permanent. An explicit id may now sit no higher than `max(counter, MAX_ID_JUMP = 1,000,000)` (ids above the counter stay legal: an import or Clear resets it). Test: `test_a_restore_cannot_push_node_ids_out_of_undos_reach`.
  - Checked and not issues: restore's outputs pass the same handle/type validator and storage normalization as import (cluster takes none); preview and `nebula path` read only inside OUTPUT_ROOT, and runs validate every resolved input with `validate_file_references`, so a forged output path reaches no more than an image-input `filePath` an agent can already set. Restore applies checks import doesn't (internal params for agents, `_provider`/`_kreaAuth` values and billing, asset ids, approved runs, World Labs delete holds and checkpoints). An agent's "undo" is just an edit (no history behind it): it is journaled under the agent's name with "(undo)", it is itself a foreign step on open canvases, and the journal actor is Person only with the token. Replacing params lets an agent drop internal `_` keys a PUT would keep, but deleting the node is already allowed and both are undoable on a canvas.
- **Known limits.** If a graphSync arrives in the few milliseconds between an undo and its restore commit, it briefly shows the backend's older state. An agent edit in that window would also include that difference in its step. Undoing it is harmless (the restore is idempotent). Pins detached when an agent deleted a node aren't re-attached when undo brings the node back. An agent making more than 50 edits pushes the person's oldest steps off the stack (`UNDO_CAP`, unchanged). With no person token (the "isn't connected as you" tab), the journal names the restore "Unnamed client", because the backend can't tell that tab from a script. With the person link it says Person (tested).
- **Prior work in this worktree.** The backend half, `canvasUndo.ts` and `tabId.ts` were left uncommitted by an earlier run of this lane. I reviewed them and kept them, with one fix: a restore item for a node that still exists used to replace params with `{}` and clear the custom name when the canvas left those keys out (it leaves them out when they didn't change). Now only the keys sent change (`test_an_item_changes_only_what_it_sends`).
- **Checked live** on an isolated backend (8821) and Vite (5821), with no requests to 8000-8010 (CDP-blocked and recorded: 0). Steps:
  - Seeded a named text prompt wired into Nano Banana.
  - An agent `POST /api/graph/apply {remove:[n1]}` with `X-Nebula-Agent: Claude` removed it on the canvas, and the notice read "Claude changed the canvas".
  - Cmd-Z brought back n1 with "Hero prompt", `{value: "a lighthouse"}` and its wire, on the canvas, in `GET /api/graph` and in the saved project (autosave). The notice read "Undid Claude's edit".
  - Cmd-Shift-Z removed it again on both sides.
  - An agent-added node was removed by the notice's Undo button on both sides.
  - Journal: `agent Claude | removed Hero prompt (n1)`, then `added Hero prompt (n1) (undo)` and `wired … (undo)`.
- **Tests.**
  - `backend/tests/test_graph_restore.py` (22 after review; the review added agent import, swap and tab-spoofing tests): actor and tab on syncs, every direct route marked, no `edit` on project switches, restore of a deletion with outputs, name and wires, restore of a creation, redo, replace-not-merge, live outputs kept, positions, idempotent for two tabs, 409 and 400s, journal as the person, agents can't change billing through it, partial items, CORS header.
  - `frontend/tests/graphStore.agentUndo.test.ts` (17 after review; the review added agent import undo and replacement-clears-stacks tests): agent create, delete, param, clear and move undone and redone with the restore bodies sent; own echoes, run results and project switches aren't steps; one stack with the person's steps; own deletion undone with outputs; begin/cancel steps; typing kept through an agent edit; drag; refused restore rolled back; another window.
  - `frontend/tests/components/CanvasUndoNotice.test.tsx` (3).
  - Updated: Toolbar, proposals and motion-handoff tests for the step taken before the request and `edit=True`.

## 2026-10-18 — Files a run passes along no longer log "escaped run directory"

GM - Design saw a Moodboard run log `[engine] output …/chat-uploads/<hash> escaped run directory …; excluding from manifest` once per board image (32 lines). An Image Input pointing at an upload logs it too.

- **Leaving those files out of the manifest is right.** The manifest lists files this run generated, each with the node, model, prompt and params that made it, and an `output_path` relative to the run folder (`find_output_record` and `/api/outputs/{path}/meta` rely on that). A board image or an upload was made earlier. Listing it would credit the Moodboard node with making it. Downstream nodes get port values straight from the run, never from the manifest, so they're unaffected.
- **The warning was the bug.** It was added (db3f6f90) to catch a handler writing a new file outside its run folder, which leaves that file with no record. It also fired for every file a run passes along. Now a file outside the run folder whose mtime is more than 2 s before the run started counts as passed along. Those are counted in one debug line, and the warning stays for files written during the run. The 2 s slack covers coarse filesystem clocks. A file uploaded under 2 s before the run still warns, which is harmless. `started_at` is optional, so direct callers keep the old behavior.
- **Not in this change.** A manifest section recording what a run consumed (inputs, board images) would be a new feature for reproducibility, not a fix.
- **Tests.** Two in `test_output_manifest.py`: an Image Input upload plus a board's images (60 s old) are left out with no warning while the generated file is listed, and a file a handler writes to another folder during the run still warns once. The first failed on main's code. All 41 test files that drive the engine pass (1,800 tests).

## 2026-10-18 — Arrange by real size; an agent's move reaches an open canvas (design-canvas gap 10, the parts that need no decision)

Gap 10: agents place nodes without knowing their rendered size, and image cards size to their image (236 to 497 px tall on the GM board). Arranging an agent's new nodes on the canvas once they render is decision C3, so this change does only what needs no decision.

- **Arrange spaces nodes by their measured size.** `computeLayout` (`lib/autoLayout.ts`) took fixed 360 × 220 steps, so Arrange and Arrange selected overlapped tall image cards too. Each column now stacks by node height plus `gapY` (40), and the next column starts after the widest node plus `gapX` (120). `layoutNode()` in graphStore passes React Flow's `measured` size. A node that hasn't rendered counts as 240 × 180, which gives the old steps, so nothing changes for unmeasured nodes. The options went from step sizes (`colGap`, `rowGap`) to gaps (`gapX`, `gapY`); only the tests passed them.
- **An agent's move of an existing node didn't show on an open canvas.** graphSync merges keep the canvas's own position for nodes it already has (the person may be mid-drag), so `move` in apply / edit_canvas and the layout route changed the backend while the open canvas kept drawing the old spot until it reloaded. Live on main's code: after an apply `move`, the node stayed at `translate(0px, 0px)`. The backend and the saved project kept the new position, even after the person dragged another node and the tab autosaved, so nothing was lost on reload. Fix: `_broadcast_graph_sync(moved=…)` adds `moved` (sorted ids of existing nodes this change positioned) from the layout route and apply, never on a replaced graph. The canvas takes the backend position for those nodes unless the node is being dragged or this tab has its own layout write for it in flight (`layoutWritesInFlight`, counted per node and cleared when the PUT settles). That keeps a quick second drop from snapping back to the first drop's echo.
- **Not in this change.** The `arrange` plan field, backend size estimates and the canvas re-arranging an agent's new nodes after they render all wait for C3. `nebula apply` will carry `arrange` once that's decided.
- **Checked live** on an isolated backend (8794) and Vite (5794), nothing sent to 8000-8010. Four image-input nodes 300 px apart (rendered 704, 134, 276 and 597 px tall) overlapped. After Arrange, none overlapped. An apply `move` showed on the open canvas (`translate(1400px, -200px)`), and the backend and saved project kept it after a drag and autosave. The dragged node stayed where it was dropped: the DOM showed 165.278px against the stored 165.2777…, the only difference being rounding. The same script against main's code failed both the Arrange and the move checks.
- **Tests.** `autoLayout.test.ts` (4 new: measured heights, widest node, unmeasured fallback, no overlaps), `graphStore.agentMoves.test.ts` (4: an agent move reaches the canvas, no `moved` keeps positions, a dragged node stays put, this tab's in-flight write beats an older echo), and 2 in `test_graph_apply.py` (`moved` from apply and from the layout route).

## 2026-10-18 — Moodboard analysis on Commons' measurement (design-canvas gaps 17, 6, 7; part of 5 and 14)

GM - Design raised four painterly references to weight 1.0, re-analyzed, and got the identical palette (gap 17). Two causes, both confirmed on main: `extract_palette` returns colours darkest first and the analysis kept `palette[:4]`, so each image gave its four darkest colours; then `round(weight * 4)` repeats went through an in-order dedupe that erased them, so the board palette was the darkest colours of the first images in upload order. Bright accents (the orange the GM board is about) were dropped before weighting started. Justin's direction: rebuild on Commons' measure, keep accents separate from dominant colours.

- **Colour comes from `commons/measure.py`.** Each image: K=8 k-means in CIELAB, a pixel share per colour, clusters closer than dE00 5 merged, and the accent pass (chroma ≥ 40, ≥ dE00 10 from the main colours, 0.1-5% of pixels). It is local and free, and doesn't need Commons switched on. A main colour Commons flags `is_accent` (small and saturated) counts as an accent too.
- **The board roll-up** (`_roll_up`). A colour's board share is the sum over images of (weight / total weight) × its share of that image. Colours under dE00 5 merge across images (Commons' rule; `_merge` keeps the distances in a matrix so a 200-image board doesn't take minutes, which Commons' pairwise loop would). `palette` is the top 8 dominant colours by share. `accents` (up to 4) rank by how much of the weighted board carries them, then share, since an accent is small by definition; an accent within dE00 5 of a kept palette colour is dropped. `colors` gives both with `share`, `role` and `images` (how many images it came from). Per image: `palette`, `accents` and `colors`.
- **Accents in the brief.** "Accent colors, used sparingly: …" follows the palette sentence, and `providerHints.generic.accents` carries them. The node's `palette` port stays the dominant colours; the bundle gains `accents`. No new port: no node takes a palette port today.
- **Weight 0 (decision B1, pending).** Implemented as the page's recommendation: a weight-0 image stays on the board and is measured, but adds nothing to the palette and isn't a representative image. It is one function, `steers()`. If Justin picks "still counts, ranked last", that function and the representative sort change. A board where every image is weight 0 says so in `warnings`.
- **Representative images (gap 6).** `rank_representative_images`: heaviest first, board order on ties, excluded and weight-0 left out, first 10. The analysis ranks only images it could read; the node's and Krea's fallbacks (no analysis) rank the whole board the same way.
- **Stale analyses.** The node used any saved analysis with a style brief, so a board re-weighted through the API kept running its old analysis. Now it compares `sourceHash` and analyzes again when the board changed, with a warning in the bundle; the saved analysis isn't touched. The version 2 hash leaves out the name, so a rename doesn't throw away a hand-edited brief. A version 1 analysis is checked against the version 1 hash and still used while the board is unchanged: whether hand edits on old analyses survive the next Analyze is decision B7, so the node doesn't decide it by re-analyzing them. Moodboard Studio shows "Made by the older analyzer… Analyze again to update it" on those.
- **PUT keeps an explicit `analysis: null`.** Studio nulls the analysis on any board change and saves the draft, but the route dropped every null, so the server kept the old analysis. `model_fields_set` now tells "null" from "left out".
- **Off the event loop (part of gap 5).** The analyze route and the node handler run the analysis in `asyncio.to_thread`. Measurements are cached per file (path, mtime, size; 256 entries), so a second analysis of a 6-image board took 0.02 s against 1.2 s.
- **Bodies refuse what they used to drop (gap 7).** `MoodboardImageModel`, `MoodboardCreate` and `MoodboardUpdate` forbid unknown fields (an image list under `imageUrls` was a 200 with an empty board); `MoodboardUpdate` gains `projectId`, which Studio sends back, and the store refuses a different one ("a board stays where it was created") where it used to ignore it. A blank image url is a 422 ("images[1].url is empty") instead of being skipped. Writes only; reading old files is unchanged. Gap 7 itself (32 images posted, 0 saved) still isn't reproduced; a 32-image POST round-trips in the tests.
- **Out of scope, small.** The brief read "…or identities Color palette:" (no full stop after the mode sentence); fixed. `docs/contracts/01-node-schema.md` didn't list #68's `moodboard` / `character` param types; fixed on #68. The Krea skill's bundle shape lists `accents`.
- **Not in this change.** The vision reader (gap 5's motifs, materials, keywords; decisions A1-A6, B2, B3), negatives built from the board (B4, B5), and a brief override that survives re-analysis (B6, B7). Keywords are still lifted word by word from the notes.
- **Checked live** on an isolated backend (8793) and Vite (5793), nothing sent to 8000-8010: six preset thumbnails, analyze, a Studio-shaped re-weight (analysis cleared, then the warm colours led the palette), the two 422s, an API re-weight the node noticed (warning, representatives followed the new weights, saved analysis untouched), and Studio showing Palette and Accents rows before and after Analyze. Puppeteer's request interception broke cross-origin GETs after a preflight (`net::ERR_FAILED`), so the run used CDP blocking alone and recorded any attempt on the blocked ports (none).
- **Tests.** `test_moodboard_analysis.py` (9: weights order the palette, largest colour beats darkest, accent kept apart, one swatch across images, weight 0, representative ranking, only readable images, current vs stale, version 1 hash), `test_moodboard_routes.py` (9: 32 images, unknown fields, blank url, Studio-shaped PUT, PUT without analysis, project move, analyze off the loop), 3 more in `test_moodboard_handler.py`, 1 in `test_krea_handler.py`, and `MoodboardStudioAnalysis.test.tsx` (2).

## 2026-10-18 — `nebula apply`: the CLI twin of edit_canvas (design-canvas gap 8)

GM - Design built the Good Machines canvas through the CLI one call per node and per wire: not atomic (a refused wire left half a graph), many calls, and no `+refs`, so each step had to read back the ids the last one made. `POST /api/graph/apply` already did the whole thing atomically for the MCP server's `edit_canvas`; the CLI never called it.

- **One plan, two commands.** The builder moved from `cli/commands/proposals.py` to `cli/plan.py`, and `nebula propose` and `nebula apply` both use it (`proposals.py` re-exports `build_body` and `BuildError`). A file of `nodes`, `edges` and `params` works with both. `propose` adds `run`; `apply` adds `rename`, `move`, `remove` and `unwire`.
- **Builder flags.** `apply` takes `propose`'s `--add`, `--param`, `--set`, `--wire` and `--at`, plus `--rename REF=name`, `--move REF=x,y`, `--remove nX` and `--unwire SRC:port DST:port`. `--rename` and `--move` take an existing id or a `+ref` from `--add`. `--file -` reads standard input (both commands).
- **Refused before sending.**
  - A plan with `run` given to `apply`: "apply never runs anything: send the same plan to `nebula propose` so the person runs it, or apply it without `run` and then `nebula run <node id>`." Refusing beats dropping `run` silently: an agent that asked for a run should know it didn't happen.
  - A plan with `rename`/`move`/`remove`/`unwire` given to `propose` says to use `nebula apply`. The backend already refused those keys with "unknown proposal field".
- **Output.** "Applied: added 3, wired 2, renamed 1." then one line per new node, `+ref → nN  Name`, so the next command can use the ids. `--json` prints the backend's result. Exit 0 on success, 1 on any refusal, with the backend's message.
- **Name.** `--as` or `$NEBULA_AGENT_NAME`, like proposals. The route already refuses an unnamed caller with "Name yourself with NEBULA_AGENT_NAME or --as".
- **Out of scope but needed: staging errors name new nodes by their ref.** A bad wire on a new node said "Invalid target handle 'nope' on node 'n12'": n12 was the id the node had on the staged copy, which the agent never saw and which doesn't exist after the refusal. `_stage_proposal` now maps staged ids back to the plan's refs in the wire validators' message ("on node '+b'"). It covers proposals, apply, `edit_canvas` and `nebula apply` alike.
- **Docs.** `docs/MCP-SETUP.md`: the apply route's section names `nebula apply` as its twin, and "Long runs and graph edits from the CLI" has the builder example. That example's output was copied from a live run, not written by hand.
- **Not done here.** The `nebula` skill in `~/.claude/skills/nebula` lists the CLI commands. Editing it is design-canvas gap 1, which is Justin's call, so it doesn't mention `apply` yet. `nebula --help` and `nebula apply --help` do.
- **Checked live** on an isolated backend (8792; temp HOME, state, settings and output; no keys):
  - the documented example ran on a seeded canvas;
  - a bad port changed nothing, and the error named `+b`;
  - `run` was refused before sending;
  - an unnamed call was told to name itself;
  - one file was proposed and then applied from stdin;
  - `--set n2._moodboardId=x` got the internal-param message from gap 13.
- **Tests.** `backend/tests/test_cli_apply.py` (10). They drive `run_apply` / `run_propose` through `NebulaClient` with its HTTP routed into the app. They cover: the atomic file apply and its output; a refused plan changing nothing, with the ref in the error; `run` refused client-side; the unnamed caller; builder flags equal to the file; editing existing nodes and the builder's own refusals; flags-or-file; stdin with `--json`; one file proposed and applied; and propose pointing at apply.

## 2026-10-18 — Moodboard and Character nodes take a public asset id (design-canvas gap 13)

GM - Design (an agent building Justin's Good Machines canvas) couldn't point a Moodboard node at a board. The node kept the board in hidden `_moodboardId` / `_moodboardName` / `_moodboardThumbnail` params: the proposal and apply paths refuse `_` keys, `nebula set` sent them but the card and the run then disagreed, and the card showed whatever copy of the name was written when the node was made. Fix: one public param per node, and the card reads the asset itself.

- **The param.** `nebula-moodboard` has `moodboard` (type `moodboard`), `character` has `character` (type `character`). The value is the saved asset's id, the same one `GET /api/moodboards` / `GET /api/characters` return. Both nodes got a `description` that says so (agents read it through `describe_node`). New param types are registered in `services/agent_params.ASSET_PARAM_TYPES`, `check-node-contracts.mjs` and the frontend `ParamDefinition` type.
- **Old nodes move over on their own.** `retired_nodes.RETIRED_PARAMS` gets an `_asset_reference` fix for both nodes: `_moodboardId` / `_characterId` moves to the public param (a public value already set wins) and the display copies (`_moodboardName`, `_moodboardThumbnail`, `_moodboardImageCount`, `_moodboardMode`, `_characterName`, `_characterThumbnail`) are dropped. It runs wherever the other retired-param fixes run: create, update, the engine's `_with_current_params`, project load and import. No `PARAMS_VERSION` bump: the fix is idempotent and never overrides a value someone set, so it doesn't need a version gate. The frontend's `storedAssetId` also falls back to the old key for a node the open tab holds that hasn't round-tripped yet.
- **Handlers read only the public param.** `handlers/moodboard.py` and `handlers/character_node.py` read `params["moodboard"]` / `params["character"]` and say what to do when it's empty or the asset is gone ("No moodboard chosen: set moodboard to a board id (GET /api/moodboards lists them)", "Moodboard 'x' not found; it may have been deleted. Pick another board for this node."). The moodboard handler's embedded-dict branch is gone; nothing ever produced it.
- **One rule for `_` keys, every agent path.** `services/agent_params.py` holds it: `_` keys are the canvas's bookkeeping and agents can't set them, except the billing keys (`_provider`, `_kreaAuth`), which keep going to `_refuse_agent_billing_change`. Proposals and apply already refused them; the message is now shared and names the public param where there is one ("n2._moodboardId is internal (the canvas keeps it); set moodboard instead"). The node routes (create, node-and-connect, PUT) refuse them only when the request carries an agent marker, because the canvas itself writes `_previewUrl` and friends through the same routes. The CLI refuses before sending.
- **Existence check.** `_check_asset_refs` in `main.py`. Everyone gets the type check (a string id). Agent-marked callers, apply and proposals also get the existence check: "n2.moodboard: there's no moodboard 'nope'; GET /api/moodboards lists them". A value equal to the node's current value is skipped, so a node whose board was deleted can still be re-saved, pasted or moved. The person's own edits aren't existence-checked (the Inspector only offers boards that exist, and the card already says "Board not found").
- **Live cards.** The backend broadcasts `{"type": "storedAssetChanged", kind, id, deleted}` when a moodboard is created, updated, analysed or deleted and when a character is created, updated or deleted. `frontend/src/store/storedAssetsStore.ts` caches what the cards show (name, thumbnail, image count, mode), fetches each asset once however many cards show it, refetches on that event and on a `graphReplaced` sync, and drops a late reply when a newer one is on its way. The cards show empty / loading / ready / not found / couldn't load. The Assets panel primes the cache with what it already has, so a new card doesn't flash empty.
- **The cache listens from first use.** `storedAssetsStore` subscribes to the socket the first time a card asks for an asset, not when the module is imported. graphStore imports it, and an import-time subscription made it the first `wsClient.subscribe` call, which `graphStore.test.ts` and `graphStore.cinemaPersistence.test.ts` read as graphStore's own handler (CI caught it; the local suite had timed out under load before reaching them). Nothing needs refreshing before a card has fetched something anyway.
- **Contract fixtures.** CI's backend run (the local single-process run timed out under load) found three more places that pin these nodes:
  - `test_node_contracts.py` takes its valid param types plus `ASSET_PARAM_TYPES`.
  - `test_reference_roles.py` approves the exact changes against its c708400 baseline, the way earlier deliberate changes were approved: both descriptions, Character's leading `character` param, and Moodboard's `moodboard` param going from a hidden optional string to the required reference.
- **Route table fixture.** `backend/tests/fixtures/route_tables.json` regenerated (`scripts/generate-route-tables.py`): the Character node's param list now has `character`.
- **Inspector picker.** `StoredAssetPicker.tsx` replaces the text field for these two param types: a select of global and project boards by name, "Not found (#id)" for a dangling id, and an Open button. Option labels are the name only; with the image count they truncated in the Inspector's width.
- **Settings in the selection toolbar.** The Moodboard and Character cards had no way to open the Inspector (no pill, no `data-node-inspector-anchor`), so the new picker was unreachable from the card. `NodeSettingsAction.tsx` portals the same "Settings" toolbar button ModelNode uses, and both cards now carry the anchor the Inspector popover positions against.

Import is atomic (no half-loaded canvas on a bad file), keeps the bookkeeping and runs the same migration. Its notes print as `note:`.

What changed: load now forwards the file's outputs and `_` params to `/api/graph/import`, where the old load dropped outputs and sent params through the node routes. Checked: the import route runs `validate_file_references` over the whole body before staging (so a protected path in an output or param is a 400), it runs `_refuse_agent_billing_change`, the CLI checks the file the same way before sending, and the engine checks params and inputs again before dispatch. The `_` keys it now accepts were writable through `nebula create` on main, and none of them grants access: `_paperSource` needs a pinned snapshot id and SHA-256 the store verifies, `_maskData` must be a data URI, `_previewUrl` is display only, and billing keys keep their rule. One thing import doesn't do is the agent existence check on `moodboard` / `character`; a loaded file with a dead id shows "Board not found" and the run says so. `test_a_loaded_graph_still_meets_the_file_and_billing_guards` pins the file and billing refusals on import.

- **`nebula info`** prints "(a moodboard id; GET /api/moodboards lists them)" under these params, and `describe_node` adds `idsFrom`.
- **Seen, not fixed.** `nebula info` doesn't print a node's `description` at all. ModelNode and DynamicNode each have their own copy of the toolbar Settings logic that `NodeSettingsAction` now also has; folding them together is a separate cleanup. The Inspector popover's bottom action row looked clipped in the screenshots; it predates this change.
- **Checked live** on an isolated backend (8791) and Vite (5791), nothing sent to 8000-8010. `nebula create nebula-moodboard --param moodboard=<id>` and `nebula run` finished in 0.49 s with the brief, palette and images; `nebula set n1 _moodboardId=…` and a raw agent PUT both get the "is internal" message; a missing id gets the "there's no moodboard" message. In the browser the card followed a rename and a new image, Settings opened the Inspector, picking a board saved `moodboard`, and a deleted board showed "Board not found".
- **Tests.** `backend/tests/test_asset_reference_params.py` (25 tests: migration, legacy node runs, agent PUT and run, apply and proposals, missing ids, the deleted-board re-save, who is existence-checked, the internal refusals and their wording, `_previewUrl` still allowed for the canvas, billing still 403, CLI refusal, `idsFrom`, broadcasts, the `nebula info` hint). 18 of them fail on main; the 6 that pass guard behavior that must stay the same. `frontend/tests/components/StoredAssetNodes.test.tsx` (12 tests: live card, rename, delete, empty, legacy id, one fetch for two cards, singular count, toolbar Settings, character card, Assets panel add, picker writes `moodboard`, the not-found option).

## 2026-10-17 — Merging main (#63) down the provider-routes stack

#63 (newer chat models, per-model Max Tokens, the params-version upgrade and the stale-tab gate) merged into main, and main was merged into #57, then each branch into the next. Most conflicts were notes files and node counts. The real ones:

- **Create's param pills (#58, `ParamPills.tsx`).** Both sides rewrote `set()`: #58 added the provider pill and its switch note, #63 made `set()` snap a per-model default (Max Tokens) when the model changes, with its own notes. Kept both: `set()` snaps as on main, and the provider pill and its note sit above the pills. The snap notes' map variable is `snapNote`, so it doesn't shadow the switch note. `Inspector.tsx` only needed both imports.
- **Applying a preset (#59, `applyPreset.ts`).** #59 returns early for a preset on a model in the catalog, ignores a preset on a model it couldn't map, and drops billing keys from a style-only preset. #63 snapped per-model defaults after the merge. Combined in `withSnappedDefaults`: a preset that switches models snaps the new model's defaults against its fresh defaults, and a style-only preset (billing keys dropped) snaps against the current params. A value the preset sets always wins.
- **Reading saved graphs and presets (#59, `cli_graph.py`, `preset_store.py`, `main.py` import).** #59 moves retired and folded Krea FLUX nodes onto the nodes they became, and #63 upgrades params by the stored version. Both now run, migration first: `CLIGraph.load` migrates, then builds everything and assigns together (#63's all-or-nothing load) and upgrades; preset reads are `_upgraded(_as_current(raw))`; `/api/graph/import` parses `paramsVersion` first (a bad one is still a 400 before any work), migrates, then upgrades. A stored project goes the other way round (upgraded when the catalog is read, migrated on open). Version 1 and the fold touch different nodes, so the order changes nothing today; `saved_graph_upgrades.py`'s header now says a later rule for a retired or folded node must match both ids.
- **Open replies carry both** `warnings` (#59: what folding dropped) and `paramsVersion` (#63: the stale-tab check), and `ProjectActivation` types both.
- **An edit on a route-table node (#61, `ParamPills.tsx`, `Inspector.tsx`).** #61 sends every edit through `snapHidden` (a setting the shown provider now hides goes back to its default, with a provider note), and #63 snaps per-model defaults on a param change. Both run, per-model defaults first: `set()` / `onParamChange` snap defaults, then the edit goes through the hidden-setting snap. A per-model default note whose value that second snap moved again is dropped, so a note never names a value the node doesn't hold. Clearing a param still makes no default notes. `writeEdit` in the Inspector now returns the params it wrote.
- **Startup bundle over budget (#61 only).** With main merged in, CI's build check failed on this branch: the entry script was 512,248 bytes against the 512,000 limit (`scripts/check-build-budget.mjs`). #60 passed just under it. The limit stays where it is. Instead, Settings' three tabs now load when the panel first opens (`React.lazy` in `Settings.tsx`), and opening the panel starts all three loads alongside the settings read. That moves ProvidersTab, PreferencesTab and StorageTab with their rows (Krea sign-in, key rows, spending limits, connected apps), about 47 KB, out of the startup bundle: the entry is 464,755 bytes now. A tab whose code can't load (a rebuild removed the chunk an open tab asks for) shows "This part of Settings couldn't load. Reload the tab to try again." in the panel (`TabLoadBoundary`) instead of taking the canvas down. Test: `tests/Settings.lazyTabs.test.tsx`. It drives the boundary with a tab that throws, because vitest didn't apply `vi.mock` to `Settings.tsx`'s dynamic import, so a mocked load failure couldn't be staged there.

Node counts: 304 on #57/#58, 308 from #59 (`AGENTS.md`, `test_video_qc_nodes.py`). `route_tables.json` regenerated on #57 for the dialogue node and Claude's `effort`; it carried down without conflicts. `MODEL_REFERENCE.md` regenerated, not hand-merged. `scripts/export-node-defs.ts` was not used: it rewrites four nodes' JSON-only fixes, as `AGENTS.md` warns.

## 2026-10-16 — Text to Dialogue: speakers are voice names

Justin approved (2026-10-16): write the voice's name in the script (`Rachel: Hi there`), look it up in the person's ElevenLabs voices at run time, and drop the Speaker 1-4 fields.

- **Script format.** One line per turn, `<speaker>: <text>`. The speaker is everything before the first colon, trimmed, so names with spaces and punctuation work, and later colons stay in the text (`R2-D2: Time: 3:15`). The old `1:` / `Speaker 1:` labels are gone; `1` would now be looked up as a name. The node isn't merged anywhere, so no saved graph has `voice_1`..`voice_4`, and they were removed from both registries with no migration.
- **Lookup: page through everything, not search per name.** The reference calls `has_more` + `next_page_token` the way to page "reliably", and says `search` "Searches in name, description, labels, category" without saying how it matches. Exact-name matching on a full list is the documented-reliable path. One call per 100 voices, once per run for all speakers. `include_total_count=false` because the reference says it "incurs a performance cost". A token already seen stops the loop; past 100 pages (10,000 voices) the run stops and says to write IDs.
- **`search` is still used, for suggestions only.** When a name matches nothing, one `search=<name>` call (page_size 5) gives the close matches the error lists. If that returns nothing, near spellings from the full list (`difflib`, cutoff 0.6). A failed suggestion call doesn't change the error.
- **Matching.** Names compare with `strip().casefold()`. Name first, then the label as an exact (case-sensitive) `voice_id` of one of their voices, or any ID-shaped label (see the review fixes below). A voice ID still resolves when its name is shared by several voices. Every unresolved speaker is reported in one error, starting "Nothing was generated."
- **Order.** Script present, key present, then every local check (`build_dialogue_request`: speaker labels, empty turns, 10-speaker limit, 2,000 characters, model, language, seed, output format), then the voices lookup, then the paid call. Tests assert `client.post` is never awaited when resolution fails, and that local failures make no HTTP call at all.
- **Distinct-voice limit = 10**, from the text-to-dialogue reference: "The maximum number of unique voice IDs is 10." Counted on distinct speaker labels (case-insensitive) before the lookup, so it costs nothing. Edge case: a name and its own ID written as two labels count as two. I accepted that to keep the check local.
- **Permission error.** 403 from `/v2/voices` is `authorization_error` ("The authenticated user doesn't have the required permissions for this action", errors page). The permission is `voices_read`. It is in the `PermissionType` enum of ElevenLabs' OpenAPI spec (api.elevenlabs.io/openapi.json, fetched today), but no docs page maps `/v2/voices` to it, so "voices_read is what listing needs" is my reading of the name, not a quote. On 403, labels shaped like a voice ID (exactly 20 letters and digits, Nebula's own reading of the docs' example IDs) run as written, so the "or write voice IDs instead" advice actually works. A name stops the run with that advice. A 401 is reported as a rejected key, unless it names a missing permission (review fixes below).
- **Same key, base URL and a timeout.** `xi-api-key` on `https://api.elevenlabs.io/v2/voices`, inside the same `httpx.AsyncClient` as the dialogue call, with `timeout=15` per listing request (the dialogue call keeps 180 s).
- **Wording.** New `description` on the node (agents read it through `describe_node` / `GET /api/agent/nodes/{id}`; `capabilityNote` isn't in that response) and a rewritten `capabilityNote`. Both say to write `Rachel: Hello` with names from the ElevenLabs voice library, that an ID works in place of a name, and the 10-voice / 2,000-character limits.
- **Contract checks.** `check-node-contracts.mjs` no longer requires `voice_1` and now refuses `voice_1`..`voice_4`. `test_node_contracts.py` asserts no `voice*` params and that the description mentions voice names. `test_reference_roles.py` didn't pin this node, so no change there.
- **Sources (read 2026-10-16):** https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/voices/search (GET /v2/voices: `page_size` "Can not exceed 100", `next_page_token` / `has_more`, `search`, `voice_ids` "Maximum 100 voice IDs", `voice_id` / `name` / `category`); https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-dialogue/convert (10 unique voice IDs, 2,000 characters); https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/resources/errors (403 `authorization_error`, `insufficient_permissions`); https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/authentication and https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/administration/workspaces/api-keys (keys can be scope-restricted); https://api.elevenlabs.io/openapi.json (`PermissionType` includes `voices_read`).

### 2026-10-16 — review fixes

- **Any 20-letters-and-digits label is an ID.** `_VOICE_ID_SHAPE` no longer needs a digit (that refused about 3% of real IDs). When a label matches no voice name and has that shape, it is sent as a voice ID whether or not it's in the person's list, and the same in the 403 path. The dialogue call rejects an ID that doesn't exist. Names still win: a label equal to a voice name resolves as the name. The "isn't the name" and 403 errors now say that a 20-character label is used as an ID, so the advice doesn't loop back. The shape is Nebula's reading of the docs' examples; ElevenLabs doesn't define the format. Labels of 19 or 21 characters, or with a space, are still refused.
- **401 with a missing permission.** A 401 from `GET /v2/voices` whose `detail.status` is `missing_permissions`, or whose message mentions "permission", raises `VoicesPermissionError` like a 403. Other 401s stay "rejected the API key". Defensive: not verified live.
- **Token cycles.** The pager keeps a set of tokens it has followed and stops on any repeat (A, B, A), not just a repeat of the last one. Tests cover the cycle and running out `VOICES_MAX_PAGES`.
- **Docs.** The elevenlabs skill (both copies) and `docs/api-guides/elevenlabs.md` no longer say Nebula can't look voices up at all: `elevenlabs-dialogue` reads names via `GET /v2/voices`.
- **New tests.** Digit-free ID passing through (normal and 403), a name that is ID-shaped resolving as the name, off-shape labels refused, missing-permission 401s, a failing suggestion search (500 and a network error) still giving the main error, the token cycle and the page limit.

## 2026-10-16 — Newer chat models on Claude, OpenAI Chat and Gemini

Added Claude Fable 5.1 / Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Astra / GPT-6.1 Sol / GPT-6 Luna, and Gemini 4 Argon / 3.8 Flash / 3.6 Flash / 3.5 Flash-Lite to the existing `claude-chat`, `gpt-4o-chat` and `gemini-chat` menus. The `gemini-chat` default moved from `gemini-3.5-flash` to `gemini-3.6-flash`. Facts come from the makers' pages fetched 2026-10-16 (list below).

- **Every handler change is gated on the new model ids** (`ADAPTIVE_EFFORT_MODELS`, `GPT6_MODELS`, `GEMINI_CHAT_NO_SAMPLING` / `GEMINI_CHAT_THINKING_LEVELS` / `GEMINI_CHAT_MAX_OUTPUT`). Explicit sets, not prefix checks, so a future `claude-opus-6` or `gpt-6.2` doesn't silently pick up the wrong call shape. `tests/test_chat_model_catalog.py` pins full request bodies for old models too, and those "unchanged" tests also pass against origin/main's handlers (checked by swapping the three handler files back temporarily), so existing models send byte-for-byte what they did.
- **Hidden params still reach the handler.** `graphStore.buildDefaultParams` seeds every param default into `node.params`, visible or not, so a fresh node always carries `temperature: 1` (and `thinkingBudget`, `reasoning_effort`, ...). `visibleWhen` alone can't keep a rejected param off the wire; the handlers skip them for the new models. This answers the research note's open question.
- **Claude 5.x:** no `temperature`, `top_p` or `thinking` (Anthropic returns 400 for a budget and for non-default sampling). Extended Thinking stays hidden for these models (its `visibleWhen` never listed them), and a stale `extended_thinking: true` from another model is dropped. Replacement: a new **Effort** param (Default / low / medium / high / xhigh / max), shown only for the four, sent as top-level `output_config: {"effort": ...}` only when set. Default `""` leaves each model at its own default effort. `max_tokens` is clamped to 128,000 (sync output limit) for these four only. An unknown effort is refused before the request.
- **Claude streaming:** thinking arrives as `content_block_delta` with `delta.thinking` / `delta.signature` and no `delta.text`; `_get_nested` returns None and the runner skips it (traced in `stream_runner.stream_execute`, and a test streams thinking + signature deltas and gets only the answer text).
- **GPT-6:** treated as reasoning models: `reasoning_effort` sent, no sampler params. `max` added to the effort menu for GPT-6 only (`gpt-5.5` doesn't support it per its model page; not verified for 5.4, so not offered there). `none` hidden for Astra and 6.1 Sol via option-level `visibleWhen`.
- **A saved choice the new model rejects is refused, not remapped.** Example: `reasoning_effort: none` from GPT-5.4, then switch to GPT-6 Astra; or `thinkingLevel: minimal`, then switch to Argon. The Inspector already shows such a value as "(unavailable for selected model)" and Runway's handler refuses a saved ratio the same way, so the handler raises "isn't available for <model>. Pick one of: ..." before any request. I first wrote a silent map to `low` and dropped it: it would run a different level than the card shows.
- **Gemini:** `temperature` not sent and `temperature` / `top_p` / `top_k` hidden for the four new models (Google ignores them from 3.6 Flash on and says future models will 400). `minimal` hidden for Argon and 3.8 Flash. Argon's `maxOutputTokens` capped at 65,536 (UI max is already 65,535; this guards agent-set values). The handler's fallback model (no `model` param) also moved to `gemini-3.6-flash`. Note: the handler has never forwarded `top_p`, `top_k` or `stop_sequences` for any Gemini model; left as is (existing behaviour), flagged for Justin.
- **Not changed, on purpose:** the 4096 Claude / 8192 Gemini `max_tokens` defaults (one default per param, shared by old models; the brief said leave other defaults alone). Google recommends at least 32,768 for Argon and Anthropic suggests 64K at xhigh/max, so short defaults can cut answers off; put to Justin. Opus 4.7 / 4.8 Extended Thinking behaviour left as is (A-OV footnote suggests they no longer accept `budget_tokens`; untested). Optional GPT-6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Sol / Terra / Luna ids left out: the approved item was "GPT-6 models", and the docs point to GPT-6.1 Sol as the newer Sol.
- **Labels:** makers' display names (Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, ...). "(flagship)" moved from Fable 5 / GPT-5.5 to Fable 5.1 / GPT-6 Astra. Retiring models stay with a date: gpt-4.1-nano 2026-10-23; gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4.1, gpt-4.1-mini 2027-01-14; gpt-5.4-nano 2027-04-01; gemini-3.1-flash-lite 2027-05-07; gemini-3.5-flash "(deprecated, runs Gemini 3.6 Flash)". Existing "Mini"/"Nano" capitalisation kept as it was.
- **Pricing: none added.** `model_pricing.json` has no rows for the chat nodes and its `per` units are image / video / second / request (`services/model_pricing.py` `PER_UNITS`); per-token prices need a schema change, out of scope.

- **Fingerprint test.** `tests/test_reference_roles.py` hashes every baseline node and only accepts listed deltas. It had no table for prepended options, option label changes, changed param fields or a param inserted mid-list, so I added four (`APPROVED_LEADING_OPTIONS`, `APPROVED_OPTION_LABEL_CHANGES`, `APPROVED_PARAM_FIELD_CHANGES`, `APPROVED_INSERTED_PARAMS`) and pinned every chat delta to its exact value, same as earlier entries. ## 2026-10-16 — ElevenLabs Text to Dialogue node (Eleven v4)

`elevenlabs-dialogue` ("ElevenLabs Text to Dialogue"), `POST /v1/text-to-dialogue`. Facts from ElevenLabs' own pages read 2026-10-16: the text-to-dialogue reference, the models page and the Eleven v4 page.

- **Why a new node and not a TTS menu entry.** "Eleven v4 is available via the Text to Dialogue API" (models page). Only v3 gets "can also be used with the Text to Speech API". So v4 is on the dialogue node and `elevenlabs-tts` doesn't list it.
- **Script shape (a choice; Justin can change it).** *Superseded the same day: speakers are now voice names, see "Text to Dialogue: speakers are voice names" above.* A `script` Text input with one line per turn, each starting `1:` to `4:` (`Speaker 1:` also works, any case), plus four voice params `voice_1`..`voice_4`.
  - Why: the card model has no list-of-rows param type. Voice IDs are free-text strings on every ElevenLabs node (there is no voice picker anywhere in the frontend), so one string per speaker is the existing pattern. The script comes from a wire, like TTS's `text`, so any Text node or LLM output can write it.
  - Four, not ten (the endpoint allows 10 unique voices), to keep the card short. `DIALOGUE_SPEAKERS` in the handler; raising it means adding `voice_5`.. to both registries.
  - Numbers instead of names: a name like "Ava:" would need a name param per speaker as well (eight params), and a line of prose that happens to contain a colon could be read as a name. Numbers are unambiguous.
  - `voice_1` defaults to Rachel (the TTS node's default), so `1: Hello.` runs with no setup. `voice_2`..`voice_4` have no default; a line for an empty speaker is an error naming the param.
  - A line with no label is an error, not a continuation of the previous turn. That keeps "which voice says this" explicit.
- **Validated before any call** (`parse_dialogue_script`, `build_dialogue_request`): unknown label, missing voice, empty turn, empty script, a voice ID that isn't letters and digits (the same rule as TTS), `model_id` outside v4/v3, `language_code` not 2-3 lowercase letters, `seed` outside 0..4294967295, and `output_format` (same pattern check as the other nodes).
- **2,000 characters: refuse, not warn.** The endpoint says to keep the total at or below 2,000 "for reliable generation" and that longer requests "can terminate early ... or return a validation error". The models page gives `eleven_v4` 10,000. Handlers have no way to show a warning on the card (nothing in `handlers/` returns one), and a run past 2,000 may be billed and cut short, so the handler refuses with the count and suggests splitting. The card's `capabilityNote` states the limit up front.
- **Body.** `{inputs, model_id, settings: {stability, similarity}}`, plus `language_code` and `seed` when set; `output_format` in the query. `model_id` is always sent because the endpoint's default is `eleven_v3`. No `speed`, `style` or `use_speaker_boost` (no such fields; "Style and Speed sliders are not available in Eleven v4"). `similarity` is the endpoint's name, not `similarity_boost`.
- **Not exposed:** `previous_text`/`next_text` ("Not supported by every model"), pronunciation dictionaries, request ids for stitching, `apply_text_normalization`, `use_pvc_as_ivc`, `audio_effects`, `enable_logging`, and Eleven v4 Turbo (WebSocket only, which doesn't fit a sync node).
- **No price row.** The pricing file can't multiply by text length (same reason `elevenlabs-tts` has none), so the node is unpriced and agent runs of it must be proposed. The per-character figure is in the api guide's existing price paragraph, not in `model_pricing.json`.
- **Timeout 180 s** (TTS uses 60 s): a dialogue is one request for the whole script.
- **TTS Turbo labels.** `eleven_turbo_v2_5` and `eleven_turbo_v2` are in ElevenLabs' "Deprecated models" table (replacements Flash v2.5 / Flash v2). Their labels now say "deprecated: use Flash ...". The values stay so saved graphs open. The reference-roles fingerprint test gained `APPROVED_OPTION_LABEL_CHANGES` for exactly these two labels, rather than a new baseline hash.
- **Contract checks.** `scripts/check-node-contracts.mjs` and `tests/test_node_contracts.py` pin the dialogue node's `model_id` default and options and that it has no speed/style/speaker-boost/similarity_boost.
- **Not live-tested.** No paid or keyed call was made. Request bodies are checked with mocked HTTP only, so whether ElevenLabs accepts every field exactly as sent is unverified until a first real run.

## 2026-10-16 — PR 5 review fixes (provider-hidden-params)

Twelve review findings, each reproduced first. All twelve were real; each fix has a test that fails without it. Only this branch changed (nothing belonged to flux-3-nodes or flux-2-bfl).

- **Rule H's one-level check was inverted (major).** `hidden_stops` / `hiddenStops` let route R' honor a value only if every stop R' had one level down was "hidden because of this value". When two routes each hid a non-default value the other takes, both checks cancelled, so neither route stopped and the run dropped one value silently. Seen on FLUX.2 (Klein 9B on fal at Safety 5 with the checker off), Krea 3 (thinking High on fal plus fal's own Model Jam) and FLUX 3 Image (Grounding off plus Prompt expansion on). Now R' is disqualified only by a stop on a setting that hides the param on R (the param's failing controllers on R), which is what the core section below already described. Results: the Draft-on-fal-at-Full-HD case still runs at 720p (OpenRouter's Draft stop is on fal's controller of Resolution); Draft on OpenRouter still stops; the mutual cases now stop on both routes, each with its own one-click reset. An Inspector edit Pro to Klein 9B with the checker off now resets Safety too. Six new route_cases and one switch_case (both languages).
  - **For Justin:** this restores the approved rule 4 for these mutual cases. It isn't a new decision, but before, these runs went ahead and now they stop with a reset, so you may notice it.
- **Schema coverage reaches every mode.** `_fillings` is the required ports plus every subset of the optional ones (168 cases), and the test asserts every route reaches every endpoint it names, so FLUX 3 Video's fal route covers all ten endpoints. It also asserts no hidden setting reaches the body under the provider's name. Offered settings with an empty-string default now get a sample value so a leak shows: the mutation "send route_param_keys" now also fails on Krea 3's Jam negative prompt.
- **Hidden-price validators read extras and multiplyBy.** `price_row_problems(definition, route, rows, extras, multiply_by)` and `validateHiddenPrices`. `check-node-contracts.mjs` takes `NEBULA_CONTRACTS_PRICING_PATH` and `NEBULA_CONTRACTS_ROUTE_CASES_PATH` (test-only overrides) so `test_node_contracts.py` / `test_node_route.py` can run the script on a broken copy.
- **Endpoint keys and circles.** New `_hideable_problems` / `validateHideable`: an `endpointWhen` key that is a param must be one the route always shows (otherwise a value that is never sent would pick the endpoint and price row), and visibility conditions can't form a circle. Chose validation over "resolve the endpoint from sent values only", because no shipped definition does it and the runtime stays as it is.
- **Rounding.** Python `_closest_value` rounds halves up (`math.floor(x + 0.5)`) like JS `Math.round`; Python `round()` rounded 2.5 to 2.
- **Create pills on legacy nodes.** `deriveVisibleParams` keeps Create's old rule (a controller with no value hides the option) for nodes without a route table, so Veo 3.1 on fal or with no key offers 720p/1080p again, not 4K. `matchesVisibleWhen` is back to its old strict body. Route-table nodes still share `visibleParams` with the Inspector.
- **Docs:** replicate skills (draft at fhd runs at 720p), PROVIDER-ROUTES.md (fix shape `[{param, value}]`, the flux-2-pro legacy delta), the MCP describe_node description, `PROVIDER_CHOICE_NOTE` and MCP-SETUP.md (structured `fixes` come only on propose_change cost entries), `.claude/skills/bfl` (copied the line the `.agents` copy had), and a hidden-settings section in krea-3.md and the krea skill. New tests in test_route_agent_surfaces.py hold these to the code and keep the 11 mirrored skill copies identical.
- **Gate** (gate_pr5_review_fix.sh, a copy of gate_pr5_merged.sh; fresh temp HOME and NEBULA_* dirs, keys unset): 246 backend files, 0 failed; the four script checks rc=0; vitest 2869/2869; tsc and lint clean. No paid calls.
- **Not changed:** structured `fixes` still reach agents only on cost entries; run errors stay message-only, as before (the docs now say so instead).

## 2026-10-16 — PR 5 UI: the Inspector, switcher and pills read hidden settings (hide-params-ui)

Stacked on the PR 5 core (provider-hidden-params, 51e3eb4c).

- **Inspector edits snap.** `onParamChange` and `clearParam` go through one `writeEdit`: on a route-table node it works out the shown route with the edited values (wired blockers and loaded keys, the same inputs as the list) and runs `snapHidden`. The notes go to `providerNoteStore`, the card's note line. An edit that resets nothing leaves an existing note alone instead of clearing it. The visible list already came from `visibleParams` (core).
- **Create pills snap the same way.** `ParamPills` `set`/`unset` run `snapHidden` against `shownRouteId(def, next, apiKeys)` and show the note in the pills' own note line (Create has no node id). `deriveVisibleParams` already used `visibleParams`.
- **Fix rows.** `ProviderMenu` takes an `onFix`; `ProviderSwitcher` applies a fix as `onPick(applyFix(params, fix), [])`. That is a plain edit, so the empty notes list clears any old switch note on the card. The fix rows and the switch rows share one wrapping line (`provider-switcher__actions`, a `role="none"` wrapper around two `role="group"`s: "Settings that let it run here", "Providers that can run it"). Fix rows reuse the switch-row pill style (`provider-switcher__alternative`) plus a `provider-switcher__fix` hook. The row notes and the Auto reason for hidden stops came from the core's `rowBlock`/`autoReason`.
- **Tests.** `switchToClient.test.tsx` now runs every `switch_cases.json` case through the rendered Inspector, including `edit:` (the Model select) and `fix:` (the reset row). Both fail with the wiring reverted. `ProviderSwitcher.test.tsx` gained a hidden-settings block on the real FLUX.2, FLUX 3 Image Klein, FLUX 3 Video and Krea 3 nodes, plus the chip popover's reset row and the pill snap (the pill test fails with the pill wiring reverted).
- **Live check** (isolated: backend 8149, Vite 5269, temp HOME, scratch NEBULA_* dirs, placeholder keys, no runs). Screenshots in the session scratchpad `flux3/pr5-shots/`. The key-change stop used Krea 3 with Reasoning level Medium (a fal-only setting) and both a fal key and a Krea token: Auto lands on Krea and shows "Set Reasoning level back to Low" and "Switch to fal.ai". FLUX.2 can't show both rows under Auto, because the route that honors Safety (BFL) comes first.
- **Surprise, not caused by this PR.** In the Playwright Chromium, the canvas tab crashed ("Target crashed") a few seconds after about four quick Inspector edits on any node. The same thing happened with the frontend source checked out at 46a853c3 (before PR 5), so it came before this work. Not investigated.

## 2026-10-16 — PR 5 agent surfaces: agents see what the card shows (hide-params-agents)

Stacked on provider-hidden-params. Justin, 2026-10-16: describe_node, the generated MODEL_REFERENCE.md (a settings table per provider) and the MCP describe_node description read the same per-route function, with a test that they agree ("Yeah we should do that").

- **describe_node needed no new filter.** `_describe_routes` already listed `route_param_definitions`, which the core lane taught to drop `paramVisibleWhen: false` and merge conditions into `visibleWhen`, so `onlyWhen` and the absent seed came for free. Added: `hides` per route (new `node_route.route_hides`, the card's words: "no Seed", "Safety only with Model FLUX.2 [pro], FLUX.2 [max] or FLUX.2 [flex]") and a rewritten `providerNote`.
- **Bug fixed on the way: describe_node dropped a 0 min or default.** `_brief_param` used `not in (None, False)`, and `0 == False`, so Safety 0-4 read as "max 4". Now `is not None and is not False` (a `false` boolean default is still omitted, as before). The agreement test caught it.
- **`fixes` where agents get a stop as data.** `canvas_proposals.cost_for` (a proposal's per-node cost entry) now carries `fixes` when non-empty. Not changed (deviation from "wherever route_unavailable is returned"): run validation errors and `multi_route`'s `MissingCredentialError` stay message strings (`ValidationErrorDetail` is shared with the canvas WebSocket event); the message already ends with the fix sentence. The estimate's `unavailable` map stays message-only too (the frontend reads it).
- **MODEL_REFERENCE.md reads `route_tables.json`, not a third copy of the rule.** The generator is plain Node and can't import directRoute.ts (extensionless imports) or Python. `route_tables.json` `routeParams` is written by `generate-route-tables.py` from `route_param_definitions` and held equal to `routeParamDefinitions` by routeTables.test.ts, so it is that function's output. Tradeoff: the generator reads a file under `backend/tests/fixtures/`, and the regeneration order matters (route tables first); the generator throws when a route-table node has no `routeParams`, and PROVIDER-ROUTES.md step 5 says the order.
- **Reference table shape for route-table nodes.** The shared table is gone; each route gets "Parameter | Key | Type | Default | Options/Range | Shown when", options as every value the route takes (not cut to 8) with the label when it differs, and "not offered here: Seed (`seed`)" on the heading. Route headings use the card's provider names (`node_route.PROVIDER_LABELS` via route_tables.json: "fal.ai", "Black Forest Labs"); the metadata row and legacy nodes keep the old labels. A route with no settings says "No settings."
- **Size.** docs/MODEL_REFERENCE.md went from 246,009 to 252,653 bytes (48% of the 512 KiB per-file cap). New `test_agent_knowledge_size.py` fails at 85% of the per-file cap, and also of the file-count and total caps (same failure mode), using `agent_knowledge._tracked_files` / `_allowed_relative` so it measures exactly what a snapshot copies.

Mutation-checked: removing a "Shown when" cell from the doc, or `onlyWhen` from describe_node, fails it.
- **Not done:** `onlyWhen` naming a controller that only another route takes (the card treats it as absent) would still be listed as is. No current node has one (checked all eight route-table nodes); the agreement test would need the same filter if one appears.

## 2026-10-16 — PR 5 core: hide what the provider doesn't offer (provider-hidden-params)

Design: the approved hide-params DESIGN.md (Justin: "Yes to all 4", D1-D4). This is the core: the route grammar (`paramVisibleWhen`), rule H, `route_sent_keys`, the Python/TS twins, the definitions, validation, fixtures and tests. The Inspector/switcher/pills wiring of `snapHidden` and fix rows, `describe_node` (`onlyWhen`), the MODEL_REFERENCE generator, the MCP docstring and the CLI came in the two lanes above (hide-params-ui, hide-params-agents), merged into this branch; the functions they need are built and tested here. Legacy `directRoute` nodes are byte for byte unchanged (the first 147 route cases, `route_sent_keys` = `route_param_keys` on every legacy node, now a test).

### Behaviour changes for saved graphs

1. FLUX.2 on fal, Flash: `safety_tolerance` is no longer sent (`Flux2FlashInput` has no such field). The only approved delta against the 6,048 legacy requests (`APPROVED_LEGACY_DELTA`); the legacy fixture and its sha are unchanged.
2. FLUX.2 on fal, Klein with a saved Safety other than 2: still stops, now with "it doesn't offer Safety 3 with Model FLUX.2 [klein] 4B. Set Safety back to 2, or switch provider." A click on the fal row resets it to 2 with a note; an Inspector model edit or a Create pill edit does too (`snapHidden`, wired in the UI lane below). On Flash the saved value is ignored (BFL has no Flash).
3. FLUX.2 on BFL with the safety checker saved off: still stops (rule H; the explicit `rejects` is gone).
4. FLUX 3 Image Klein on OpenRouter: no Seed row, no seed sent; a saved seed stops with "Clear Seed"; a click on the OpenRouter row clears it.
5. FLUX 3 Video drafts on bfl, fal and replicate send no `resolution` (D1). A draft saved at Full HD or above now runs as the 720p draft instead of stopping, priced at the draft row. Replicate draft + 4K runs.
6. FLUX 3 Video with a saved draft on OpenRouter or Krea: still stops ("doesn't offer Draft (fast preview)", fix "Turn Draft (fast preview) off"); the explicit `rejects {draft}` is gone.
7. Krea 3 on fal with Jam: a negative prompt typed under Berry is no longer sent, and the run doesn't stop.
8. Krea 3 high thinking on fal is now unpriced and stops there (the shipped price case was renamed; fal → null), because fal's route doesn't offer Krea's own `thinking_mode` and Krea would honor it.
9. `route_unavailable` (and the TS `RouteUnavailable`) always carries `fixes` (`[]` unless the block is hidden). A message whose honoring route has no key ends "(add its key in Settings > Providers)."
10. The switcher's snap on a click now also resets hidden stops (e.g. "Grounding isn't on fal.ai: turned off" on the fixture table, "Seed isn't on OpenRouter: cleared"); the row note for a hidden stop reads "Doesn't take Safety 5 (Permissive)".

### Decisions and deviations from the design

- `DirectBlock` gained a `when` field, and `on` names the honoring route for a hidden block, so the message can say "with Model FLUX.2 [klein] 4B" and "Black Forest Labs can take it".
- Rule H checks the honoring route one level deep: R' must itself have no hidden stop other than one on a setting R's condition reads. (Review fix, 2026-10-16: the first version tested the reverse, "R''s stop is hidden because of this value", which let two routes that each hide the other's value cancel out. See the review section at the top.) The design said no recursion; removing `rejects {draft}` from OpenRouter/Krea made "would BFL honor it?" need one level to resolve (otherwise a saved draft on OpenRouter loops or is wrongly ignored).
- A route's own value rules read a hidden listed setting at its default (`_shown_rules_block`), so a value nobody sends can't trip a rule.
- Fix sentences: "Set X back to Y" for an enum/number default, "Turn X on|off" for a boolean default (not in the design), "Clear X" when there is no default.
- `snapForRoute` loop 1 skips hidden settings (so it doesn't snap a value the route won't send), and loop 2 is `hiddenStops`. Python twins of the snap (`snap_for_route`, `snap_hidden`, `_closest_value`, `_default_note`) were added so `switch_cases.json` is checked in Python too (`test_switch_cases_snap_like_the_switcher`).
- Messages use option labels ("Safety 5 (Permissive)", "Model FLUX.2 [klein] 9B"), not raw values.
- Small component change: the Inspector's visible list now comes from the shared `visibleParams` predicate (one predicate with Create's pills, `route_sent_keys` and rule H). Create's legacy pills now pass undefined controllers the same way the Inspector does. (Reverted in review, 2026-10-16: nodes without a route table keep Create's old rule; see the review section at the top.)
- `test_flux3_nodes.py`: the BFL and Replicate cheapest draft bodies changed (no `resolution`). The task said "unchanged", but D1 (design 10.5) approves exactly this.
- The schema-backed coverage test lives in a new `backend/tests/test_route_schema_coverage.py`, not `test_route_clients.py`, because it needs `test_flux3_nodes.py`'s host fakes, which import from `test_route_clients.py` (a circular import otherwise). Mutation-checked: sending `route_param_keys` instead of `route_sent_keys` fails it on FLUX.2 (`steps`) and FLUX 3 Video (`resolution`). Krea 3's Jam negative prompt is in fal's schema ("Used by berry only"), so a dedicated test covers it in `test_flux3_nodes.py`.
- `test_reference_roles.py`: `APPROVED_ROUTE_TABLE_CONVERSIONS["flux-2-pro"]` replaced per D4 (dated comment), and four drift cases added (drop, widen or add a `paramVisibleWhen`, or bring back the BFL `rejects`).
- `test_route_agent_surfaces.py` `onlyWhen` coverage came with the agent-surfaces lane (above).

### Prices

- BFL publishes no video-continuation draft price. Re-checked 2026-10-16: https://docs.bfl.ai/quick_start/pricing's v2v Draft cell is `<Pricing endpoint="/v1/flux-3" field="v2v720" effort="draft">` (renders "Not listed"), and https://bfl.ai/pricing's CMS "FLUX 3 Video Draft" rates are only `{"effort":"draft","t2v720":6}`. It stays unpriced; the `model_pricing.json` note and `checked` date say so.
- New check: a price row may not read a setting its route hides with the values the row matches (`price_row_problems`, `validateHiddenPrices`); both were mutation-tested and agree.

### Review follow-up (PR 4, 2026-10-15)

Four findings, each confirmed on HEAD first (a reproduction, then a test that failed on the old definition: 16 of the new `test_flux2_nodes.py` cases fail with the pre-fix definition and clients).

- **A `model` no route lists ran Pro, unpriced.** `{model: "MAX"}` or `"Flash"` fell through `endpointWhen` to `/v1/flux-2-pro` and `fal-ai/flux-2-pro` on both routes, unblocked and unpriced (`estimate_run` put it in `unpriced`), and `"Flash"` got past BFL's `rejects model [flash]`. Fixed in the definition (both twins): each route's `accepts.model.values` is exactly the models it serves (BFL five, fal six), replacing BFL's `rejects.model`. Any other value now stops through the normal route block ("it doesn't take model MAX") before any request, with no route offered. Lowercasing was not chosen: it would be a translator in both twins for a value the UI can't produce, and it would hide a typo instead of naming it. Pinned by three `route_cases.json` cases (both languages) and `test_a_model_no_route_lists_stops_unbilled_instead_of_running_pro`. Side effect: a model stop now names the route's models ("Pick pro, max, flex, klein-9b or klein-4b, or switch provider."), since the stop message lists a param's `accepts` values. That also listed the models under fal's Klein safety stop, whose `rejectsWhen` match led with `model`, so the eight Klein entries now lead with `safety_tolerance` (the block's `param` is the first match key); that stop says "Change that setting" again. Two existing `route_cases.json` cases were updated for the new wording, and "steps on Pro stop every route" now expects no stop (renamed).
- **Agents can now spend on saved FLUX.2 nodes without asking.** Confirmed (`agent_spend.decide` refuses unpriced nodes whenever a USD limit is set, and `flux-2-pro` had no price entry on `flux-3-nodes`). No code change: added to "Behaviour changes on saved graphs" above and to the PR body; Justin approved it on 2026-10-16.
- **Flex-only steps and guidance showed on every model and could dead-end the run.** Set on Flex, then the model changed: the fields stayed visible, and both routes' `rejectsWhen` stopped the run with nothing to switch to. Now both params carry `visibleWhen: {model: ["flex"]}` (the Inspector and `describe_node`'s `onlyWhen` read it), the 18 steps/guidance `rejectsWhen` entries are gone, and the route clients drop a hidden value: BFL sends `steps`/`guidance` on `flux-2-flex` only (`BFL_FLUX2_FLEX_ONLY`), fal drops them on every endpoint but `fal-ai/flux-2-flex` (`FAL_ENDPOINT_DROPS`). That is Nano Banana's rule for its hidden resolution: a hidden, stale value changes nothing on either route. Pinned by `test_steps_and_guidance_left_from_flex_are_hidden_and_not_sent` and a `route_cases.json` case. The legacy fal parity (6,048 combinations) is unchanged: the old node had no steps or guidance.
  - **Not fixed: Safety on fal Klein.** fal's Klein still lists Safety 1-5 and stops every value but "2". `visibleWhen` is per node, not per route, so it would also hide Safety on BFL's Klein, which takes 1-5. Route narrowing (`_narrowed`) can't cut options by another param's value: `rejectsWhen` stays a run-time block by design. The stop isn't a dead end, because it offers BFL. A per-route, per-model narrowing rule would be a grammar change in both twins, so it's left for a later PR.
  - **Edge left:** steps 1 saved under BFL Flex, then the model changed and fal picked: fal's `accepts num_inference_steps {min: 2}` still reads the hidden 1 and stops fal (offering BFL). Rules don't know about visibility. Making hidden params count as unset in the rule reader would change `krea-3` too, so it's left out of a review fix.
- **The fal skill still called FLUX.2 a fal wrapper.** Both copies: `flux-2-pro` left the `sync_runner.py` wrapper tables, gained a row in "fal as a route" (endpoints by `model`, Flash only on fal, Klein drops `safety_tolerance`, Flex-only steps), and `.claude`'s param entry matches `node_definitions.json`. The BFL skill, `docs/model-providers/bfl/flux-2.md` and `PROVIDER-ROUTES.md` describe the new `accepts` and hidden-value rules.

`test_reference_roles.py`: `APPROVED_ROUTE_TABLE_CONVERSIONS["flux-2-pro"]` changed exactly (dated comment): BFL `rules` are `{"accepts": {"model": {"values": [pro, max, flex, klein-9b, klein-4b]}}, "rejects": {"enable_safety_checker": [false]}}`; fal `rules.accepts` gains `model: {values: [pro, max, flash, flex, klein-9b, klein-4b]}` and its `rejectsWhen` keeps only the eight Klein safety entries, each matching `{safety_tolerance, model}` in that order; the two `addedShared` Flex params gain `visibleWhen: {"model": ["flex"]}`. The drift test now also checks adding `flash` to BFL's models and removing a `visibleWhen`. The baseline isn't regenerated. `route_tables.json` was regenerated (generated from the definitions).

Six review findings; five distinct (the two Krea 3 price findings are one). Each was confirmed on HEAD first (a failing test or a reproduction), then fixed with a regression test.
