### Item 1, saved 4,096 Max Tokens upgraded at load

**Where saved graphs reach the canvas, agents and runs (mapped before changing anything):**
- Project open/switch (`POST /api/projects/{id}/open`), home/recent list (`GET /api/projects`), reading the active project at startup (`GET /api/projects/{id}`; startup does *not* call open), autosave (`PUT`), stale-tab recovery (`POST /api/projects/recover`), trash restore: all read the catalog through `ProjectStore._read` (projects/catalog.json).
- The live graph that the CLI, agents, MCP and `/api/graph/run` read: `cli_graph`, restored at boot by `CLIGraph.load` (state.json), and replaced on open/import from already-staged data.
- Graph-file import: `.nebula` / `.nebula.zip` → (zip: `POST /api/outputs/restore` validates and returns the file unchanged) → `POST /api/graph/import`.
- Canvas runs (`/api/execute`, `/api/execute-node`) post the canvas's own params, which came from one of the paths above; history replays post a run's saved recipe (`snapshot.runHistory[].snapshot`).
- Templates/samples: none in the repo hold claude-chat params (checked `backend/data`, `frontend/src`); `backend/data/presets/seed.json` has no Claude presets.
- Existing mechanism: `services/retired_nodes.py` (`migrate_node` / `migrate_params`) runs on every path, statelessly, for values a provider shut down. It has no "ran once" notion, so it can't tell an old 4,096 from a deliberate one. No schema/param version existed anywhere (the catalog's `version: 1` and the .nebula `version` 1-3 are format versions).

**Decision: a separate one-time upgrade with a version marker per saved graph** (`backend/services/saved_graph_upgrades.py`, `PARAMS_VERSION = 1`):
- Rule (version 1): claude-chat, model in Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 / Opus 4.7 / Opus 4.8, `extended_thinking` truthy (the handler's own test), `max_tokens` exactly 4096 (int, float or the string "4096") → `64000` (int). The value is frozen in the module; a test checks it equals today's definition default for those four models.
- Catalog projects and trash entries: `ProjectStore._read` upgrades every entry below the version and sets `_paramsVersion` (hidden: `public_project` returns only metadata + snapshot). This is the one point every project reader goes through, so open, list, the startup read of the active project, recovery and agents all see 64,000. The upgraded catalog reaches disk with the next commit (open always commits; so does the first startup list when the live overlay changes anything). Until then every read upgrades the same file the same way, and a deliberate 4,096 can only reach disk through a commit, which also stores the marker. So it is one-time without a separate write. *(Since round 2 item 3 the boot also writes it at once, with a new workspace revision, when any entry is behind.)*
- `make_project` starts new projects at the current version (including "Recovered canvas", whose content comes from the already-upgraded live graph).
- Live graph: `CLIGraph._save_state` always writes `"paramsVersion"`; `CLIGraph.load` upgrades a file below it, and main's boot step persists right away when anything changed (prints `[main] upgraded saved params on N node(s)`).
- Run recipes inside a project's history are upgraded with the project, because a replay sends the recipe as saved. **Tradeoff:** an old history record now shows 64,000 although that run sent 4,096 (with a budget that no longer exists on these models). I preferred the replay running what the node runs now over a run-time net that can't tell a deliberate 4,096 apart. *(Superseded 2026-10-17, review follow-up: run records are left as they were sent.)*
- Import: the canvas forwards the file's `paramsVersion` (0 when missing) and `/api/graph/import` upgrades below the current version. **Decision:** a body without the key (an agent or script writing a graph now) is taken as current, so an agent's 4,096 is honoured. A malformed version is a 400. `serializeGraph` writes `paramsVersion`; `GRAPH_PARAMS_VERSION` in `frontend/src/lib/graphFile.ts` must equal the backend's (test). *(Moved 2026-10-17 to `frontend/src/lib/savedParamsUpgrades.ts`, re-exported from graphFile.ts.)*
- Recovery copies (`/api/projects/recover`) take the source project's version: the tab's canvas came from it. If the source is gone entirely (the placeholder), the copy is version 0 and upgraded like any old project. *(Superseded 2026-10-17, review follow-up: the tab sends its own version.)*
- **Handler:** `LEGACY_MAX_TOKENS` and its run-time rewrite are removed. Every run path now reads upgraded params, so no narrower safety net was kept. The empty-answer `stop_reason: max_tokens` error stays (its test now expects "4,096", the value sent).
- **No save storm, no dirty loop, no undo entry:** the rewrite happens in the backend before the canvas receives the project, so `applyProject` records the upgraded snapshot as `lastSaved` and nothing is dirty; the canvas never edits params itself, so no undo step or autosave is triggered. The upgrade isn't journalled separately: it rides on the open commit (or the next catalog commit), and the live graph's boot write is logged.
- ~~**Edge left (documented, not fixed):** a browser tab loaded from the old backend and kept open across the upgrade restart. On reconnect the backend's `graphSync` merges the upgraded live nodes into it, but a frontend-only node (not in the live graph) keeps 4,096 in that tab and its next autosave stores it as current. The desktop app restarts both together, so this needs a dev tab left open across a `git pull` restart.~~ *(Fixed 2026-10-17, round 2 item 3: such a tab can no longer save or run, and a current bundle reloads.)*
- ~~**Not covered:** user style presets (`~/.nebula/presets`) are param sets, not graphs; a saved preset holding claude-chat Max Tokens 4,096 isn't upgraded. Presets that pick a model already go through `snapParamDefaults`.~~ *(Covered 2026-10-17, round 2 item 2: presets are upgraded when read.)* Also branch-only: a graph saved on this branch between 2026-10-16 and today with a deliberate 4,096 has no marker and gets upgraded once (Justin's live app runs main, which never had the new default).

Tests (`backend/tests/test_saved_graph_upgrades.py`, 13 fail without the wiring): a saved project opens holding 64,000 in the snapshot, the live graph and the run recipe, with the marker on disk; thinking off, 8,192, Haiku 4.5, Fable 5 and Opus 5.5 untouched; a 4,096 set after the open survives switching away and back and a fresh store; the active project and state.json upgrade at startup without a revision change (when read; the boot step added in round 2 item 3 now rotates it); the boot write; new projects start current; trash; recovery copies; import at version 0 / current / without the key / malformed; frontend-backend version parity; a run of the upgraded node sends 64,000 and a later 4,096 sends 4,096. `test_chat_defaults_effort.py` swaps "saved 4,096 sends 64,000" for "upgraded at load sends 64,000" and "deliberate 4,096 sent as set". Frontend: `graphFile.paramsVersion.test.ts`, and `GraphFileActions.test.tsx` now expects `paramsVersion` in the import body.

### Review follow-up on item 1 (2026-10-17)

Two reviewers checked the commits after 2707ab76 and sent five findings. Four reproduced as failing tests before the fix (16 backend and 2 frontend tests failed). The fifth was a trace, and fix 1 removes its cause. No new provider fact was needed: the only Anthropic behaviour relied on is the thinking-troubleshooting quote above ("thinking tokens count toward `max_tokens`…").

- **Run records are no longer rewritten (medium).** `upgrade_snapshot` used to rewrite `runHistory[].snapshot` recipes, so a record of a run that sent 4,096 read 64,000 after the upgrade, and a Paper run's `recipeRevision` hash stopped matching its recipe. Justin approved changing the card value, not past run records. Now only `snapshot.nodes` (and the Create draft, below) are upgraded. **Tradeoff:** replaying a record from before the upgrade sends 4,096, as the original run did. With thinking on, that can stop with the "ran out of Max Tokens" error, which tells the user to raise Max Tokens. Raised with Justin as an open question. *(Answered in "Justin's answers 2026-10-17, round 2" below: a replay sends the recipe upgraded, and the record still keeps what it sent.)*
- **Recovered copies use the tab's version (low).** `/api/projects/recover` took the source project's `_paramsVersion`. That was wrong both ways. A deleted and purged source gave version 0, which overwrote a 4,096 the user set after the upgrade. A source that had already been upgraded gave version 1 to a tab that loaded before the upgrade. Now the canvas sends `paramsVersion` in the body. `projectStore.ts` records it in `applyProject` (`canvasParamsVersion`), and it goes into `pendingRecovery`. The backend validates it the same way as import (shared `request_version`; a malformed value is a 400). **Decision:** a body without the key counts as version 0. Only the canvas calls this endpoint, so a body without the key comes from a bundle older than the marker, and that tab's canvas predates every upgrade. The recovery fingerprint does not include the version, because a retry resends the same body.
- **Malformed saved values can't crash a load (low).** `upgrade_params` now only checks a model that is a string (a list or dict made the set lookup raise a TypeError). `upgrade_snapshot` skips `nodes` that aren't a list. `CLIGraph.load` builds nodes, edges and the counter into locals and assigns them together, so a load that fails part way leaves the previous graph whole. Before, the nodes were assigned and the edges were not, so the next save could drop every edge. Tests cover an unhashable model in a catalog node and a recipe, in state.json, and in an import body at version 0, plus a load that fails part way.
- **Create drafts are upgraded (medium).** `upgrade_snapshot` now also upgrades `snapshot.createDraft` when `modelId` is `claude-chat` (the Create model id is the node definition id). Drafts in localStorage (`nebula:create:drafts:v1`) get the same rule in the browser. The payload gained `paramsVersion` next to its format `version: 1`. **Decision:** I added a field rather than bumping `version` to 2, so an older bundle still reads the drafts and the storage format and the params version stay separate. A payload without the field is version 0. `loadDrafts` upgrades in memory, and every save writes the current version, so a 4,096 typed later is kept. The rule is mirrored in the new `frontend/src/lib/savedParamsUpgrades.ts`, which now owns `GRAPH_PARAMS_VERSION`. A backend test checks that its version, its four models, 4096 and 64000 match the Python module.
- **Legacy localStorage run history adopted into "Recovered canvas" (low, trace only).** This is not a defect after the first fix: run records are never upgraded anywhere, so the adopted legacy records keep what they sent, the same as every other record. The canvas, the live graph and the Create draft in that project are still upgraded: the live graph by `CLIGraph.load`, the draft by `loadDrafts`.

## Justin's answers 2026-10-17, round 2: replays, presets, stale tabs

Justin (2026-10-17), on the three open questions from PR #63: "1. what do you recommend? 2. Yes 3. we should fix that shouldn't we? Basically all of the answers come down to what are the best and correct answers - not what are the easiest or quickest". Then "go" to the plan: 1. old runs are upgraded when you replay them, and the stored record stays as it was sent; 2. presets are upgraded once, the first time they're read; 3. a tab opened before an update reloads instead of saving or running old values. Each item is its own commit.

### Item 1: run records

- **Stamp on the record, outside the snapshot.** `RunRecord.paramsVersion` (runHistory.ts). `openRunRecord` stamps `GRAPH_PARAMS_VERSION` on every new record, fresh runs and replays alike: a fresh run sends the canvas, which is at this bundle's version (the backend upgrades before `applyProject`), and a replay sends the upgraded recipe. `OpenRunRecord` omits the field, so no caller can pass another value. It sits outside `RunGraphSnapshot`, so `paperRecipeContent` and `recipeRevision` are unchanged (tested).
- **Missing = 0.** Every writer of an unstamped record predates the stamp: main's bundle, legacy pre-project localStorage, and records already in projects. The backend only validates and stores records (`main.py` project snapshot validation deep-copies `runHistory` whole), and agents, the CLI and MCP have no way to create or replay one. A backend test confirms a stamped and an unstamped record round-trip through a project save unchanged.
- **Malformed stamp.** `isRunRecord` doesn't check the field, so a bad stamp never drops a record. `loadRunHistory` drops a stamp that isn't a non-negative integer (read as 0) and rewrites storage once. `runParamsVersion(record)` is the one reader.
- **One helper.** `upgradeRunSnapshot(snapshot, version)` in savedParamsUpgrades.ts maps `upgradeSavedParams` over the nodes, never mutates, and returns the same object when nothing changes. `currentRunSnapshot(record)` in runHistory.ts applies it at the record's version.
- **Replays:** `executeHistoricalRun` freezes `currentRunSnapshot(source)` instead of `source.snapshot`. That one line covers rerun, retry, latest-Paper-source (which passes `{...source, snapshot}`, so the version carries), cluster, Create and cinema-shot replays. The source record is untouched; the new record holds what was sent, stamped current, with `sourceRunId` set.
- **Create "Reuse settings":** `resultContextForNode` builds `reusableDraft.params` from the upgraded params. **Decision:** the details panel (`context.params`) keeps showing what the run sent, since it describes that run; only the new draft starts from the upgraded value.
- **Paper freshness:** `paperRunOutOfDateReasons` compares `currentRunSnapshot(record)` with the canvas. A version-0 4,096 equals the canvas's upgraded 64,000, so pre-upgrade Paper records are no longer flagged "Recipe settings or connections changed" (they were, after the load-time upgrade). A real edit is still flagged, and so is a stamped 4,096 against a 64,000 canvas. Records already holding that wrong reason are corrected by the existing freshness subscriber on the next pass (a one-time history change and autosave; `reconcilingPaperFreshness` prevents a loop).
- **No version on `/api/execute` bodies** (per the integrated design): a stale bundle replaying old records is handled by item 3, which stops that tab from running at all.
- **Edge (accepted):** a record that a stale tab (main's bundle) creates is unstamped, so a later replay from a new tab upgrades it, even if that tab's 4,096 was set on purpose. Item 3 stops stale tabs from running, which closes this for tabs open across an update. *(Done: item 3 below.)*
- Tests: `frontend/tests/runRecordParamsUpgrade.test.ts` (22). 11 failed with the wiring reverted (stamp, both Paper freshness cases, Reuse settings, and every replay path: rerun, retry, node rerun, latest Paper source, cluster, Create, cinema shot); the rest guard the stamped-4,096 and helper behaviour. Backend: `test_saved_project_keeps_each_record_s_params_version` (confirms existing behaviour; it passes without a backend change).

### Item 2: presets

- **A per-preset marker, `paramsVersion`, in each preset file.** The existing `version` is an edit counter (`update()` adds 1), so it can't carry the params version: the boot thumbnail backfill alone would set it to 2. **Why per file, not per store:** each file is written on its own (new tabs, a main tab open across an update, boot seeding), so a store-level "upgraded" flag would let a later unmarked 4,096 through. A file without the marker is version 0; a malformed one (a string, a bool) also reads as 0.
- **Upgrade on read, no write on read** (`_upgraded` in `services/preset_store.py`, used by `get` and `list`), mirroring `ProjectStore._read`. Every reader gets the upgraded params: `/api/presets`, Create's library, the Assets panel, `pendingPreset`, the thumbnail backfill. **Why not a boot sweep:** it would bump every touched file's edit counter and `updatedAt`, and it would miss files that arrive later (a restored `~/.nebula`, a copy from a main install). Reading is deterministic and a deliberate 4,096 only reaches disk through a write, which stamps the marker, so the upgrade still happens once in meaning.
- **Every write stamps the version.** `create(..., params_version)` (now required, so each caller decides) upgrades the incoming params by the caller's version and writes the current one; seeding passes `PARAMS_VERSION`. `update(..., params_version=PARAMS_VERSION)` upgrades new params by the caller's version, or, without new params, the stored params by the file's own version, against the merged `modelId`. So a thumbnail-only update on an unmarked file stores the upgraded params once, with the edit counter up by exactly 1. A `paramsVersion` passed through the field kwargs is ignored, so the marker can't be set without the upgrade.
- **Partial presets are left as stored:** no `model`, no Extended Thinking, `modelId` not `claude-chat` (or null). `upgrade_params` only matches the full saved shape, so nothing guesses a model.
- **HTTP.** `PresetCreate` and `PresetUpdate` gained `paramsVersion: Any`, checked with the shared `request_version` rule (non-negative int, not a bool; `"1"`, `true`, `1.5`, `-1` and an explicit `null` are a 422, matching the preset routes' existing 422 for bad input). `model_fields_set` tells a missing key from a sent one. **POST without it = 0:** main's `CreateView` POSTs without it, and no agent, CLI or MCP tool posts presets (seeding calls the store directly). **Tradeoff:** a raw-HTTP script posting a deliberate 4,096 on one of the four models with thinking on and no key gets 64,000; it can send `paramsVersion: 1`. Same reasoning as `/api/projects/recover`. **PUT without it = current:** no bundle, old or new, sends PUT, so a caller is deliberate API use writing params now (as `/api/graph/import` treats a body without the key).
- **Frontend:** `PresetCreateInput.paramsVersion` is required, and Create's "Save current" sends `GRAPH_PARAMS_VERSION`. That is only right because the draft is current: `loadDrafts` and the backend upgrade saved drafts, presets are upgraded on read, and item 1 upgrades "Reuse settings" by the run's version. `applyPresetToComposer` doesn't repeat the rule: everything it gets from the backend is already upgraded.
- **Decision not in the plan: a version newer than this backend is kept.** A file or body at a higher version (a newer backend or bundle) is stored and served with that version, not lowered to `PARAMS_VERSION`, so a later backend doesn't run an upgrade on params that are already past it. A bogus large number from a raw API caller only freezes that caller's own preset.
- **Gaps left to item 3:** a main tab open across the update keeps its fetched preset list (with 4,096) in memory, and its POST is upgraded here only because it lacks the key. Applying a stale in-memory preset into that tab's draft and autosaving it is the stale-tab problem item 3 closes. *(Closed by item 3: that tab's preset writes, autosave and runs are refused.)*
- **Branch-only edge (accepted):** a preset saved from this branch's bundle before this commit with a deliberate 4,096 has no marker and is upgraded once. Main never had the 64,000 default, so only dev testing is affected, as with graphs.
- Tests: `backend/tests/test_preset_params_upgrade.py` (30). 18 failed with the store and route changes reverted (read upgrade for every model, malformed marker, create and update by the caller's version, thumbnail-only update, field-kwarg marker, POST without the key, malformed versions, PUT, GET/list, seeding); the other 12 guard what must stay as stored. Existing preset store, seed and thumbnail tests now pass `params_version`. Frontend: `CreateView.save.test.tsx` "sends the params version the draft is at" failed before the CreateView change; `createPresets.test.ts` checks the body carries it.

### Item 3: tabs loaded before an upgrade

A tab whose canvas loaded before an upgrade is treated as stale: the backend never accepts its writes or runs its params, and a current bundle reloads. Upgrading its request bodies on the server was rejected: the card would still show 4,096, and a body from that tab can't tell a stale 4,096 from one typed on purpose there.

- **Header on every request.** `apiFetch` (`frontend/src/lib/backend.ts`) sends `X-Nebula-Params-Version: GRAPH_PARAMS_VERSION` on every method, project open or not (the revision header still goes only on writes with a project open). `_DESKTOP_CORS_HEADERS` lists it for the opaque-origin branch.
- **Gate** (`_params_outdated` in `project_workspace_fence`, main.py), before the revision check so the refusal says why. Writes to `/api/graph*`, `/api/execute*`, `/api/cinema*`, `/api/quick`, `/api/projects*` except `/api/projects/recover`, and `/api/presets*` get 409 `{code: "params_outdated", detail, paramsVersion}` when the version header is present and not exactly `PARAMS_VERSION` (lower, higher or garbage), or missing while `X-Nebula-Workspace-Revision` is present. No header at all passes as sent (agents, CLI, MCP, curl: their 4,096 is deliberate). Reads are never gated.
- **Proof that a missing version with the revision header means an old bundle:** only `apiFetch` sets the revision header (grepped backend, CLI, MCP, skills, desktop: no other setter), and every bundle from this commit on sends the version header from the same function.
- ~~**The MUST VERIFY: can main's bundle store or run params with no project open (no revision header)?** No, checked in origin/main's source. `getProjectContext()` is null only before `initialize` finds an active project, after `initialize` finds none, and after deleting the open project, and in all three `screen` is `'home'`. `screen` becomes `'workspace'` only in `activate` (after `applyProject` sets the context) and in `open` for the already loaded project. While `screen === 'home'`, `App.tsx` renders `ProjectHome` and the Home settings dock only (no canvas, studio, Create view, chat panel, command palette or shortcuts; brand showcase renders only its own view). From Home it can create, open, rename, delete, restore or purge projects (none carry tab params; open, once it succeeds, sets the context, so every later write carries the revision header and is refused). Its `flush` returns early without a context, its `graphStore` ignores graphSync events carrying a revision while it has no context, and every request goes through `apiFetch` (no raw `fetch` to these routes; `/ws` takes only the hello frame). A preset POST from main carries no `paramsVersion` and is upgraded from 0 by item 2 regardless of headers. A future bundle with no project open sends the version header, which the gate checks on its own.~~ *(Wrong: main can reach the canvas with no project context. Corrected in "Review follow-up, round 2" below; the gate now also treats a browser request without the version as version 0.)*
- **Boot rotation** (`ProjectStore.advance_params_version`, `_finish_params_upgrade_at_boot` in main.py). When the catalog on disk has a project or trash entry below `PARAMS_VERSION`, or state.json was below it (`CLIGraph.params_advanced_on_load`, version, not changed values: the tab can hold unsaved values), the boot sets a new `workspaceRevision` and commits the catalog under the store lock. It uses `project_store.commit`, not `_commit_project_workspace`: only the catalog changes, so the live graph and provider-recovery seeding aren't touched. It is skipped when state.json failed to load, and does nothing without a catalog file (the revision is new in every process then). The state.json boot write now runs whenever the file was behind, not only when a value changed, so a file with nothing to upgrade gets its marker and the next boot doesn't rotate again. The lazy-write gap from item 1 is closed: the upgraded catalog is on disk before any tab can save.
- **Main's bundle after the restart.** Its graphSync carries the new revision, so its graphStore doesn't merge (and the tab doesn't go dirty from a merge) and its projectStore goes into its existing conflict flow: recover if dirty (no `paramsVersion` in its body: version 0, upgraded), else Home. Before the socket reconnects (3 s), its autosave or run is refused with `params_outdated`. After Retry re-applies the upgraded project, every write it tries is refused with a detail main prints as is: "Nebula was updated while this tab was open, so this tab can't save or run until it reloads. Reload the tab; your saved work is kept. If this keeps happening after a reload, this window's frontend build doesn't match the backend: rebuild the frontend, or restart the backend."
- **Current bundles.** `paramsVersion` is in `_workspace_context()` (graphSync, every execution event, `/api/graph/export`) and in `GET /api/projects`. projectStore reacts to a graphSync or listing at another version, or a `params_outdated` refusal (`noteParamsOutdated` in `lib/paramsOutdated.ts`, read from a clone like the person-gate check), all through one `handleParamsVersionChange`: stop saves (the existing conflict state), recover once if dirty with the tab's own version, then `location.reload()` instead of `applyProject`. graphSync is checked for the version before the revision, so the tab says "Nebula was updated…" rather than "changed in another window". graphStore also skips merging a graphSync at another version.
- **No loops, no repeated copies, no noise.** One handling at a time (a shared promise); the recovery helper (`recoverPendingWork`, now also used by `initialize`) marks the recovered canvas as saved, so a later report or Retry can't make a second copy (a failing test caught this: Retry made a second copy with a new recoveryId). A clean tab reloads with no copy. The reload sets a sessionStorage mark for that backend version; a reload that brings the same old bundle (an unbuilt desktop `dist`, a stale dev server) stops with "Rebuild the frontend (or restart the dev server)" instead of reloading again, and the mark is cleared when the versions match. Without sessionStorage it doesn't auto-reload at all *(and since review round 2 it says to reload the tab, not to rebuild)*. A backend older than the bundle never reloads: "Restart the backend, then reload." The unsaved-changes prompt is skipped only for a reload whose edits are in a recovered copy; if the copy fails, nothing reloads and the prompt stays.
- **Tradeoffs (from the map, accepted under "best and correct"):** every tab open across an update makes one trip (a reload for current bundles; Home and Retry for main's) even when clean. Edits typed in main's bundle after Retry re-applied the project are refused and lost on reload; the refusal shows on the first autosave (600 ms) and the beforeunload prompt warns. A dirty main tab that already re-applied the upgraded project still recovers as version 0, so a 4,096 typed there on purpose is raised (rare).
- **Not done:** the desktop launcher doesn't check that its built frontend's `GRAPH_PARAMS_VERSION` matches the backend's. A stale `dist` now fails loudly (every write refused with the rebuild message) rather than silently; a launch-time parity check would catch it earlier.
- Tests: `backend/tests/test_params_version_gate.py` (12; 7 failed with the backend change stashed). It replays origin/main's request shapes (projects.ts autosave, rename, create, open, delete, empty trash; api.ts execute, execute-node, cinema shot; graphStore param push, node create, cluster; quick; createPresets.ts POST and DELETE) with the revision header at today's and a pre-restart revision: each is 409 `params_outdated`, no run route is entered (`_capture_execution_workspace` and `_normalize_execute_nodes` recorded), no HTTP transport is used, and the live graph and every file under the state dir are byte-identical. Main's recovery body is accepted and upgraded. Header-less requests store and run 4,096 as sent. Lower, higher and malformed versions are refused with or without a project; GETs pass. Boot is tested in a fresh process importing main against isolated state: rotation plus both files written, only once; rotation when only state.json advanced with no value changed; nothing when current, after a failed state.json load, or without a catalog. `test_saved_graph_upgrades.py`'s boot test lost its source regex (the subprocess test covers the real boot). Frontend: `tests/lib/backend.paramsVersion.test.ts` (7; 6 failed before) and `tests/paramsVersionReload.test.ts` (11; 9 failed against the old stores, the two that passed guard existing merge behaviour). `backend.test.ts` and `graphStore.test.ts` now expect the headers object on `fetch`.

### Review follow-up, round 2 (2026-10-17)

Seven findings (two were the same docstring). Each was reproduced as a failing test first, except the docs.

- **Main's bundle on the canvas with no project context (medium): fixed.** The round-2 "MUST VERIFY" proof was wrong. In main's projectStore, a conflict sends the tab Home with `activeProject` kept; Try again while the backend has no active project calls `setProjectContext(null)` but leaves `activeProject`; and Open of that same project takes `open()`'s shortcut (`initialized && id === activeProject.id`) to the canvas without `applyProject`. Its runs, param pushes and saves then carry neither header and passed the gate. **Fix:** a gated write with no version header is version 0 when it carries the revision header *or comes from a browser* (`_from_a_browser` in main.py: an `Origin` or `Sec-Fetch-Site` header). **Why these two headers:** every browser sends `Origin` on a request that isn't GET or HEAD. The packaged desktop renderer (a file: page) sends no Origin, as the desktop pass found, but it does send `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`. curl and Python (the CLI, MCP, agent tools) send neither, and Node's fetch sends only `Sec-Fetch-Mode`. I checked the renderer and Node cases live on 2026-10-17: a bare Electron 44.3 `BrowserWindow` loading a file: page, and Node 22.16 fetch, both pointed at a local header-echo server (no Nebula process). **Proof that the new bundle is never caught:** every write it makes to a gated route goes through `apiFetch`, which always sets the version. The raw `fetch` calls in `frontend/src` are all GETs of assets or `/api/health`. The desktop smoke checks in `desktop/main.mjs` only hit settings, spend and Krea routes. **Tradeoff:** a script that writes an `Origin` to a gated route without the version is now refused with the reload message. The test fixtures `PERSON`, `FORGED_ORIGIN` and `person.headers` (conftest.py) now carry the version header, because the canvas sends it and a forger copies it. That fixed 40 tests, and each still checks what it checked before. Tests: `test_main_bundle_without_a_project_context_is_refused` (Vite tab, Origin only, desktop renderer; all 3 failed first) and `test_requests_without_canvas_headers_pass_unchanged` (now run for curl/Python and for Node fetch).
- **A refused Run made a recovered copy of a clean tab (low): fixed.** The refusal (`noteParamsOutdated`) and the run's own catch can arrive in either order. Either way the snapshot held the new run record and the nodes' queued or error state, so it counted as dirty. **Fix:** graphStore records every start a backend refused (`settleFailedStart`, now the first line of all six run-start catches) and exports `runsThatNeverStarted(includePending)`. For a params-version stop, `preserveWorkspaceConflict` leaves those records out of both the dirty check and the recovered copy, and it ignores node `state` and `error` in the dirty check (run state, not authoring). Starts still waiting for an answer are left out too when the backend reported a version or refused with `params_outdated`, because such a backend refuses every start from this bundle. They are kept for a version-0 backend, which has no gate, so they may really run. Tests: three in `paramsVersionReload.test.ts` "a Run refused with params_outdated is not unsaved work" (both orders for a clean tab, plus an edited tab whose copy keeps the edit and has no run record). All 3 failed first.
- **`upgrade_snapshot` docstring (low, reported twice): fixed.** It now says the canvas upgrades a copy by the record's stamp when the record is replayed or reused, so a version-0 record's replay sends 64,000.
- **New bundle against a backend from before the gate (medium): fixed.** Such a backend sends no `paramsVersion`, and the new bundle used to skip the check and load its projects, stamping run records, recovered copies and drafts as current. **Fix:** `backendParamsVersion` (lib/paramsOutdated.ts) reads a missing or malformed version as 0, and every place the bundle learns the backend's version uses it: the listing in `initialize`, graphSync in projectStore and graphStore (no merge), and, new, the create and open replies, which now carry `paramsVersion` (main.py). `activate` doesn't apply a project from a reply at another version. Without that, opening a project in the seconds before the socket reconnected to a restarted older backend would load it. So `applyProject`, and with it `canvasParamsVersion`, is reached only from a backend at this bundle's version. The tab stops with "This window's frontend is newer than the Nebula backend… Restart the backend, then reload." **Test churn:** fixtures in 9 frontend test files that built graphSync events, listings or activation replies without a version now include `GRAPH_PARAMS_VERSION`, as the real backend always does. Tests: the three "a backend that sends no paramsVersion predates the gate" cases in `paramsVersionReload.test.ts` (all failed first) and `test_listing_and_graph_sync_carry_the_params_version`, which now also checks the create and open replies. I wrote that check after the change, so it is not a fail-first test.
- **sessionStorage blocked (low): fixed.** `reloadOnceFor` now returns `'reload' | 'reloaded' | 'unmarked'`. With storage blocked, the tab says "Nebula was updated while this tab was open. Reload the tab to use the update." It still doesn't reload by itself, because without the mark a stale build would loop. The rebuild wording stays for a tab that already reloaded once. Test: "with sessionStorage blocked, asks for a reload instead of a rebuild" (failed first).
- **claude-chat doc omitted presets (low): fixed.** `docs/model-providers/anthropic/claude-chat.md` now lists saved style presets among the things the upgrade covers. It also says a tab with no project open is refused too, and that a current tab connected to an older backend stops. `docs/projects-implementation-notes.md` describes the browser rule and the version-0 backend.
- **Same bug in the new bundle: fixed too (not in the findings).** This bundle's `initialize` had the same else branch, which cleared the context but kept `activeProject`, and the same `open()` shortcut. With the version header that no longer let old params through, but such a tab sat on a canvas with no project context, and its edits went unsaved. The else branch now also clears `activeProject`, so Open goes through the backend and `applyProject`. Test: `projectStore.test.ts` "opens the former project through the backend after Try again found no active project" (failed first).

## 2026-10-17 — SelectionToolbar's chat-focus timer outlived the toolbar

CI failed three of ten PR runs on 2026-10-17 (#57, #59, #64) with "ReferenceError: document is not defined" from `SelectionToolbar.tsx`, after every test had passed. "Ask agent about selection" opens the chat panel and focuses its text box 180 ms later, on a timer nothing cleared. When `SelectionToolbar.test.tsx` finished within those 180 ms, the timer fired after jsdom was torn down. Load-dependent, so it showed up only sometimes.

- **Fix in the component, not the test.** The timer lives in a ref and the toolbar clears it on unmount, so a toolbar that disappears first (the selection cleared) no longer moves focus afterwards. A second click restarts the wait instead of stacking timers.
- **Tests:** "focuses the chat box once the panel has opened" and "cancels the pending chat focus when the toolbar unmounts" (fake timers). The second failed before the fix.
- **Not changed:** the 180 ms wait itself. Focus requested by the panel when it mounts would avoid a fixed delay, but that is a separate change to `ChatPanel`.

## Desktop launch params check (2026-10-17)

Justin approved "Desktop launch check" (after #63). The desktop app runs the checkout's backend but a frontend someone built earlier, so a `git pull` that raises `PARAMS_VERSION` used to open an old bundle that failed only at its first save or Run. Now the app checks at launch. Branch `desktop-params-check`.

**What was built**
- `frontend/vite-plugins/buildStamp.ts`: a Vite plugin (build only) that emits `nebula-build.json` = `{"paramsVersion": GRAPH_PARAMS_VERSION}` next to `index.html` in both `dist/` and `dist-desktop/`. It imports the constant from `savedParamsUpgrades.ts`, the same import the bundle uses.
- `/api/health` adds `"paramsVersion": PARAMS_VERSION`; the other fields are unchanged. Still unauthenticated.
- `desktop/frontend-build.mjs` (pure, Electron-free): `readBuildParamsVersion` (missing stamp: `build_stamp_missing`; unreadable or no non-negative integer: `build_stamp_unreadable`) and `checkParamsVersions` (`frontend_older`, `frontend_newer`, `backend_version_unreadable`). Errors are `FrontendBuildError` with a `heading` the failure surface shows.
- `desktop/main.mjs`: stamp read right after the "renderer is not built" check, before app data, migration or spawn; the comparison after `startSidecar` resolves and before `createMainWindow`. A mismatch runs `cleanupSidecar()` and throws into the existing catch (`startupError` + `showFailure`), so a Dock click or second launch shows it again. Both are skipped in dev mode.

**Decisions not in the spec**
- **`savedParamsUpgrades.ts` imports nothing now.** Importing it from `vite.config.ts` pulled `runHistory.ts` (a type import) into the Node tsconfig program, where `window` and `import.meta.env` don't exist: 60 tsc errors. Instead of moving the constant (the backend test reads it from this file by regex), `upgradeRunSnapshot` is typed structurally (`<T extends { nodes: { definitionId, params }[] }>`). Callers still pass and get `RunGraphSnapshot`. The header asks to keep the module import-free.
- **The plugin lives in `frontend/vite-plugins/`**, added to `tsconfig.node.json`, not in `src/` (which is browser-typed with no Node types).
- **The sidecar handle carries `health`** (the body that confirmed readiness), so main.mjs compares without a second request. The `sidecarStarting` flag stays true until the comparison passes, so a Cmd-Q while a mismatched sidecar is stopping waits for the stop, like a quit during cold start.
- **The comparison runs after the `NEBULA_SIDECAR_PID/PORT` log lines.** The integration test reads the PID to prove the sidecar is gone afterwards.
- **A non-integer `paramsVersion` in health** (no real backend sends one) gets its own `backend_version_unreadable` message under the usual "Backend startup failed" heading, instead of blaming the frontend.
- **Failure-surface heading.** The page always said "Backend startup failed"; it now uses `error.heading` when there is one ("The desktop frontend needs a rebuild").
- **Smoke JSON includes `type`** for `FrontendBuildError` as for `SidecarError`.
- **`npm run package` rebuilds a renderer with no stamp** (its mtime check alone would call a fresh pre-stamp build up to date and package an app that refuses to start), and `vite-plugins/` counts as a build input.
- **Electron integration tests now skip unless `dist-desktop` has the stamp**, not just `index.html`: a pre-stamp build would stop every launch at the stamp check and the old tests would fail with a confusing error.

**Tests**
- Desktop unit: `tests/frontend-build.test.mjs` (17: missing, unreadable, seven damaged shapes, equal, older, newer, health without the field, a bad backend value, heading). `sidecar.test.mjs` asserts the handle's `health`.
- Desktop integration (`integration.test.mjs`): two launches against the `serve-health` fixture, one at `stamp + 1` (frontend older), one with no field (frontend newer). Each checks the smoke error type and message, a non-zero exit, that the logged sidecar PID is gone and its port has no listener, and that no renderer loaded. The existing smoke run (real backend, stamp 1 = health 1) still passes.
- Also checked by hand: a launch with the stamp removed reports `build_stamp_missing` and creates no `Nebula Nodes` app-data folder.
- Backend: `/api/health` body equality in `test_params_version_gate.py`. Frontend: `tests/buildStamp.test.ts`.

**Surprises**
- `cd desktop && npm test` had three failures on main before this branch. Two pinned 19 provider keys, but both lists have held 20 since TypeSafe joined (#53): `credential-service.test.mjs` and `sidecar.test.mjs` ("the provider-key list"). The pins now say 20. The provider stack (#57) raises them to 21 with BFL, so expect that one-line conflict there. The third, the parent-lifeline test, runs the checkout's own `backend/.venv`, which a fresh worktree lacks; it passes with one. Whole suite with a venv in place: 378/378, none skipped.
- The in-tab gate from #63 is unchanged; it still covers browser tabs (the web build's stamp is written but nothing reads it).

**Live check with real Electron (2026-10-17), and one fix**
- Launched the app three ways in smoke mode (isolated user data, app id and HOME, mock keychain, flux2-bfl venv), capturing each window through `webContents` (`capturePage`, `executeJavaScript`) from a scratch harness that wraps `main.mjs`. A matching build opened a new project on the canvas ("Saved"); an edited stamp (0) and a removed stamp each stopped with the rebuild message, and the version-mismatch sidecar was gone afterwards.
- **Bug found: the fix line was cut off.** `showFailure` reuses the 480x320 loading window when it exists (it always does at launch), and the message box was capped at `50vh` (160px), so the frontend-older message ended at "Run `cd frontend && npm run build:desktop`" half out of view; the box sat inside the window's drag region, so it couldn't be scrolled or selected either. The old sidecar errors had the same limit, but these are the first messages whose last line is the whole point.
- **Fix:** the failure page moved to `desktop/failure-surface.mjs` (with `htmlDataUrl`/`escapeHtml`, which the other inline pages also use). `showFailure` grows the reused loading window to `FAILURE_WINDOW_SIZE` (600x400, the size a fresh failure window already had) and centres it; the box is `max-height: calc(100vh - 140px)`, selectable and `no-drag`. Re-captured: all three launch-check messages (older, newer, no stamp) show in full. Test: `desktop/tests/failure-surface.test.mjs`.

## TLS errors mid-response count as connection failures (2026-10-15)

- **Bug.** During a demo recording a Jev Box run failed with the raw node error `[SSL: SSLV3_ALERT_BAD_RECORD_MAC] ssl/tls alert bad record mac (_ssl.c:2559)`, although `typesafe_client.system_one` retries transport errors.
- **Cause (checked in the venv: httpx 0.28.1, httpcore 1.0.9, anyio 4.13.0).** anyio's `TLSStream._call_sslobject_method` (`anyio/streams/tls.py:197-208`) turns only an SSL EOF into `BrokenResourceError` and re-raises any other `ssl.SSLError` as is. httpcore's anyio backend maps `ssl.SSLError` only in `start_tls` (`httpcore/_backends/anyio.py:61-66`); its `read`/`write` maps (lines 26-31, 43-47) don't list it, and httpx's `map_httpcore_exceptions` re-raises anything it can't map. So a TLS error after the handshake reaches us as a raw `ssl.SSLError`, outside `httpx.HTTPError`. The sync backend maps every `OSError` on a read (SSLError included) to `ReadError` (`httpcore/_backends/sync.py:124-128`), so only async clients are affected.
- **Fix at the root.** New `backend/services/http_errors.py`: `TRANSPORT_ERRORS` / `HTTP_ERRORS` (the httpx class plus `ssl.SSLError`), `is_transport_error()`, and `describe()` (readable text for a TLS error instead of OpenSSL's). Used in `typesafe_client.system_one` (retry), `poll_retry.is_transient` (every async video poller), both FAL recovery requests in `stream_runner`, `vision_llm` and `prompt_enhance` (which now falls through to the next provider on a TLS error instead of crashing).
- **Safety net for the rest.** Handlers that don't catch httpx errors let a raw SSLError reach the engine, whose `classify_error` filed it as "unknown" and showed the OpenSSL text. Added four narrow network markers ("bad record mac", "decryption failed", "ssl/tls alert", "record layer failure"), so those now get the friendly "Couldn't reach the provider" message and `retryable=True`. Deliberately not "[ssl:", which would also catch certificate-verify failures (those come through `start_tls` as `ConnectError` anyway).
- **Not changed, on purpose.** `nebula_api.py`, `services/backend_address.py`, `cli/commands/mcp_connect.py` use sync httpx to plain-http loopback (no TLS, and the sync backend already maps SSLError). `krea_mcp_server.py` is async but talks plain http to Nebula's loopback URL, so there is no TLS to break.
- **Tradeoff.** Retrying a mid-response read failure can re-send a billed request (TypeSafe charges per request). The code already did this for `httpx.ReadError`, so this keeps the behaviour consistent rather than adding a new risk; a poll retry is a GET and isn't billed.
- **Tests.** 12 new test cases across `test_typesafe_client.py`, `test_poll_retry.py` (helper, BytePlus ride-out, BytePlus gives up and DELETEs), `test_stream_runner_fal_recovery.py`, `test_prompt_enhance.py`, `test_error_classifier.py` and new `test_http_errors.py` (incl. vision). All 12 fail with the source changes stashed and pass with them.
- **Reproduced locally, not only read.** A scratch TLS server on 127.0.0.1 (self-signed cert, TLS 1.2) sent a garbage application-data record after the handshake. A real `httpx.AsyncClient` raised `ssl.SSLError: [SSL] record layer failure (_ssl.c:2559)` and `isinstance(exc, httpx.HTTPError)` was False. OpenSSL words the same failure differently by version, which is why "record layer failure" is a classifier marker too.

## TypeSafe minimum image side: 256 -> 280 (2026-10-16)

- **Source.** docs.typesafe.ai/images, fetched 2026-10-16: "Width and height 280 to 1568 pixels each. An image with either side under 280 pixels is rejected." and "Total pixels (width × height) 78,400 to 2,458,624, the area of a 280 × 280 to a 1568 × 1568 square." The page also says "Scale up, or pad, an image smaller than the minimum."
- **The old value was wrong, not stale.** `MIN_SIDE = 256` didn't match the page; the Jev integration entry above ("Image limits (256 to 1568 px a side ...) match") was mistaken. `MIN_PIXELS = 78_400` was already right (it is 280 x 280), which is why square images were padded to 280 x 280 and only thin images went out under the limit.
- **What broke.** Any image whose short side came out between 256 and 279 after shrinking was sent short and TypeSafe would refuse it. Two cases now have tests that fail on 256 and pass on 280:
  - a 2000 x 320 banner shrinks to 1568 x 251 and was padded to 1568 x 256 (now 1568 x 280);
  - a 3:1 candidate on Pick Best's 768 px retry is 768 x 256 and was sent as is (now padded to 768 x 280).
- **Every use checked.** `_target_size` pads (never refuses) up to `MIN_SIDE`, so the one constant fixes Decide, Box, Pick Best (both passes) and `qc_jev` (frames thumbnailed to 768, then fitted by `prepare_images`). The `max_side` check in `prepare_images` now reads 280 to 1568; the only caller with a smaller `max_side` is Pick Best's 768 retry, which is inside it.
- **Kept on purpose.** The `MIN_PIXELS` grow step in `_target_size` can't trigger any more (280 x 280 is exactly 78,400), but stays in case TypeSafe moves the two limits apart.
- **Tests updated to the documented value:** the `_target_size` table, the `max_side` error message, and the hand-built `ImageTransform` box-mapping case (now a realistic 280 px sent height).
- **Docs:** `docs/api-guides/typesafe.md` and both copies of the typesafe skill say 280-1568 px.

## Dev frontend port isolation (2026-10-16)

A screenshot run's second Vite page found Justin's live backend on 8000 and saved test nodes into his project. Two causes: `frontend/vite.config.ts` hard-coded its `/api` and `/ws` proxy to 8000, and `frontend/src/lib/backend.ts` scanned 8000-8010 (plus a URL stored by earlier runs) unless `VITE_NEBULA_BACKEND_PORTS` was set. Fix on `dev-backend-port-isolation`.

- **One setting, `VITE_NEBULA_BACKEND_PORT`.** The brief suggested `NEBULA_BACKEND_PORT`. A `VITE_` name reaches the page through Vite's own env loading and `vite.config.ts` reads it with `loadEnv`, so one value drives both with no `define` plumbing, and it can't expose other `NEBULA_*` variables (tokens) to the client the way widening `envPrefix` would.
- **Shared pure module** `frontend/src/lib/devBackendPort.ts`: used by `vite.config.ts` (Node) and the page. It reads no `import.meta.env` or `window`, so both can import it.
- **Pinned means pinned.** Discovery probes only same-origin (the Vite proxy, which follows the pin) and `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`/page host at that port. A stored `nebula:backendBaseUrl` on another port is skipped. The not-found error names the pin and says it isn't scanning.
- **Person links follow the pin** (`personSession.ts`). A link or stored credential for another port is refused (the link is still stripped from the address bar); a link without `backend=` defaults to `127.0.0.1:<pin>` instead of 8000. Without this, opening the main backend's person link in the test tab would have pinned it back to 8000.
- **Fail closed.** An invalid pin (`abc`, `0`, `8155,8156`) throws instead of falling back to the scan. A pin plus `VITE_NEBULA_API_BASE` on another port stops Vite at startup (`assertBackendEnvConsistent`) and also throws in the page before any probe.
- **Unchanged:** nothing set means proxy to 8000 and the 8000-8010 scan with the stored URL first (tested). `VITE_NEBULA_BACKEND_PORTS` still works; the pin wins over it. The desktop app's injected bridge is checked before any of this (tested with a pin set).
- **`vite.config.ts` became `defineConfig(({ mode }) => …)`** to call `loadEnv`, and exports `devBackendProxy` for the test. The whitespace diff is large only from reindenting the object; `git diff -w` shows the real change. Scratch configs that import it already handle the function form.
- **Docs:** `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Running a second, isolated dev instance" (the recipe), a pointer in `AGENTS.md` Other conventions and the README quickstart, and a gotcha in the `nebula-nodes-visuals` capture-pipeline reference (both the `.agents` and `.claude` copies).
- **Live check (ports 8155 / 5275 only):** backend with temp `HOME`, `NEBULA_SETTINGS_PATH`, `NEBULA_STATE_DIR`, `NEBULA_OUTPUT_ROOT`; Vite with `VITE_NEBULA_BACKEND_PORT=8155`. Playwright aborted any request or socket to localhost/127.0.0.1 ports 8000-8010: zero attempts. Requests went to 127.0.0.1:5275 (proxied; the 8155 backend log shows `/api/projects`, `/api/settings` and the `/ws` socket) plus one direct `/api/health` probe each to 127.0.0.1:8155 and localhost:8155, and Google Fonts. No nodes added.
- **Seen in passing, not fixed:** on page load without a person link, `runCostConfirm.ts` tries `PUT /api/settings` and logs a 403 warning ("Could not save the run cost threshold"). That's the person gate working; the page could skip that write when not connected.

## Autosave flush loop fix (2026-10-16)

- **The bug.** Change a param and change it back within the 600 ms autosave window, and the canvas tab saves itself in an endless loop until the renderer dies. Also on main; it explains the headless Chromium tab crashes after rapid Inspector edits.
  - The first edit's `markDirty()` sets `dirty: true` and starts the timer. The revert's `markDirty()` sees the snapshot equal to `lastSaved` and returns early, so `dirty` stays true.
  - The timer's `flush()` finds nothing to send and returns without touching `dirty`. Its tail (`if dirty && saveStatus !== 'error'`) then calls `flush()` again, which finds the same thing, forever. Each round is only microtasks, so timers, input and paint never get a turn.
- **A second way into the same loop, found while testing.** A save in flight when another window takes over the project: `preserveWorkspaceConflict` sets `initialized: false, dirty: true`, the landed save leaves the newer edit dirty, and every re-flush returns at the "not initialized" check.
- **Fix (`frontend/src/store/projectStore.ts`, `flush`).** Two small changes, both needed:
  - The "nothing to send" branch now marks the store clean (`dirty: false, saveStatus: 'saved'`): if the canvas equals the last save, that is true.
  - The save task returns whether a save landed, and the tail re-flushes only then. An edit made during a save still gets saved (that path returns true), but an exit that saved nothing can't spin. `saveQueue` is now `Promise<unknown>` because it holds that boolean task.
  - No timeouts or retry caps. `markDirty()` is unchanged: clearing `dirty` there when the canvas matches `lastSaved` would be wrong while a newer save is still in flight (the test "saves the older value when an edit is reverted while a newer one is in flight" covers that).
- **Tests.** `frontend/src/store/projectStore.autosave.test.ts` (vitest, fake timers, `saveProject` mocked). A wrapper on `flush` counts calls and throws after 20, so a regression fails the test instead of hanging it.
  - Fail without the fix: change + revert ends clean with at most the one timer flush and no save; the takeover case stops after two flush calls.
  - Guards that already passed and must keep passing: an edit during an in-flight save is saved afterwards; reverting to the older value during a newer in-flight save still saves it; a failed save shows `saveStatus: 'error'` with the message, and Retry saves it.
